Collections — List, Dictionary, HashSet & Friends

Which container, what each operation costs, and the read-only, immutable and frozen variants.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12
  • dotnet >=8
  • .NET (the base class library)

Sources: Collections and data structures — .NET · Collection expressions — C# reference

Pick the container

Enumeration order of `Dictionary` and `HashSet` is not guaranteed — sort when order matters.

NeedUseWhy
ordered listList<T>, T[]contiguous; [..] collection expressions build either
key → valueDictionary<TKey, TValue>O(1) average; TryGetValue for a miss
membership, dedupeHashSet<T>O(1) Contains; set operations mutate in place
sorted keysSortedDictionary, SortedSetO(log n)
FIFO / LIFOQueue<T>, Stack<T>O(1) at the end that matters
priority queuePriorityQueue<TElement, TPriority>a min-heap since .NET 6
read-mostly lookupFrozenDictionary, FrozenSetbuilt once, optimized for reads (.NET 8)
snapshots you can shareImmutableList, ImmutableDictionaryevery change returns a new collection

What operations cost

Amortised costs (*) include the occasional resize.

TypeLookupInsertRemove
List<T>O(1) by index, O(n) ContainsO(1)* Add, O(n) InsertO(1) last, O(n) other
Dictionary / HashSetO(1) averageO(1)* averageO(1) average
SortedDictionary / SortedSetO(log n)O(log n)O(log n)
Queue<T> / Stack<T>O(1) peekO(1)*O(1)
PriorityQueueO(1) peekO(log n)O(log n)
ImmutableList<T>O(log n)O(log n)O(log n)

Dictionary and HashSet

`GetValueOrDefault` reads a missing key as the default; `UnionWith` changes the set in place.

var counts = new Dictionary<string, int>();
foreach (var word in "the cat and the hat".Split(' '))
{
    counts[word] = counts.GetValueOrDefault(word) + 1;
}
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", counts.OrderBy(kv => kv.Key, StringComparer.Ordinal).Select(kv => $"{kv.Key}={kv.Value}")));
Console.WriteLine($"{counts["the"]} {counts.ContainsKey("dog")} {counts.TryGetValue("cat", out var cat)} {cat}");

var set = new HashSet<int> { 1, 2, 3 };
set.UnionWith([2, 3, 4]);
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", set.Order()));
Result
and=1, cat=1, hat=1, the=2
2 False True 1
1,2,3,4

Keys need value equality

A `record` generates `Equals` and `GetHashCode`; a class compares by reference.

var points = new HashSet<Point> { new(1, 1), new(1, 1) };
var cells = new HashSet<Cell> { new(1, 1), new(1, 1) };
Console.WriteLine($"{points.Count} {cells.Count}");

record Point(int X, int Y);
class Cell(int x, int y)
{
    public int X => x;
    public int Y => y;
}
Result
1 2

Queue, Stack, PriorityQueue

`PriorityQueue` dequeues the lowest priority first and is not stable for equal priorities.

var queue = new Queue<string>(["a", "b"]);
queue.Enqueue("c");
var stack = new Stack<int>([1, 2, 3]);
var tasks = new PriorityQueue<string, int>();
tasks.Enqueue("low", 5);
tasks.Enqueue("urgent", 1);
tasks.Enqueue("mid", 3);
Console.WriteLine($"{queue.Dequeue()} {stack.Pop()} {tasks.Dequeue()} {tasks.Dequeue()}");
Result
a 3 urgent mid

Read-only, immutable, frozen

A read-only interface is a view; immutable collections return new ones; frozen ones trade build time for fast reads.

using System.Collections.Frozen;
using System.Collections.Immutable;

var colors = new Dictionary<string, int> { ["red"] = 1, ["green"] = 2 }.ToFrozenDictionary();
ImmutableList<int> v1 = [1, 2];
var v2 = v1.Add(3);                            // a new list; v1 is unchanged
var backing = new List<int> { 1 };
IReadOnlyList<int> view = backing;
backing.Add(2);                                // the view sees it
Console.WriteLine($"{colors["green"]} {v1.Count} {v2.Count} {view.Count}");
Result
2 2 3 2

Pitfalls

Where C# differs from Swift's value-type collections.

  • Modifying a List or Dictionary inside its own foreach throws InvalidOperationException.
  • list.RemoveAt(0) in a loop is O(n²) — use Queue<T>.
  • Relying on Dictionary or HashSet enumeration order: it is an implementation detail.
  • Expose IReadOnlyList<T> / IReadOnlyDictionary from APIs and keep the mutable type private.
  • Collections are reference types even when they hold structs: var b = a aliases the list.

Filter, project, fold

`Sum` says the intent; `Aggregate` is the general fold.

Order[] orders = [new(1, "ana", 30), new(2, "bo", 12), new(3, "ana", 8)];
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", orders.Where(o => o.Total >= 10).Select(o => o.Id)));
Console.WriteLine($"{orders.Sum(o => o.Total)} {orders.Aggregate(0, (acc, o) => acc + o.Total)}");

record Order(int Id, string Customer, int Total);

Group, index, count

`GroupBy` keeps the order in which keys first appear; `CountBy` is new in .NET 9.

Person[] people = [new("Ana", "web"), new("Bo", "data"), new("Cy", "web")];
foreach (var team in people.GroupBy(p => p.Team))
    Console.WriteLine($"{team.Key}: {string.Join(",", team.Select(p => p.Name))}");

Console.WriteLine(people.ToDictionary(p => p.Name)["Bo"].Team);
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", people.CountBy(p => p.Team).Select(kv => $"{kv.Key}={kv.Value}")));
Console.WriteLine(people.ToLookup(p => p.Team)["web"].Count());

record Person(string Name, string Team);

data: Bo

Deferred execution

A query is a recipe, not a result — it runs each time it is enumerated, against the source as it is then.

var source = new List<int> { 1, 2, 3 };
var evens = source.Where(n => n % 2 == 0);     // nothing has run yet
source.Add(4);
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", evens));    // runs now, and sees 4

var snapshot = evens.ToList();                  // materialize once
source.Add(6);
Console.WriteLine($"{string.Join(",", evens)} vs {string.Join(",", snapshot)}");
Result
2,4
2,4,6 vs 2,4

Sort by several keys

`OrderBy` is stable; pass an explicit comparer for text so the culture cannot change the order.

Player[] players = [new("cy", 7), new("ana", 9), new("bo", 7)];
var ranked = players.OrderByDescending(p => p.Score).ThenBy(p => p.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal);
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", ranked.Select(p => $"{p.Name}:{p.Score}")));
Console.WriteLine($"{players.MaxBy(p => p.Score)!.Name} {players.MinBy(p => p.Score)!.Name}");

record Player(string Name, int Score);

Chunk, distinct, zip, skip/take

All built in since .NET 6.

int[] xs = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", xs.Chunk(2).Select(c => $"[{string.Join(",", c)}]")));
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", new[] { "b", "a", "b", "c", "a" }.Distinct()));
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", new[] { "a", "b", "c" }.Zip(new[] { 1, 2 }, (s, n) => $"{s}{n}")));
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", xs.Skip(1).Take(3)));

Rules

Where LINQ costs more than it looks.

  • Enumerating the same query twice runs it twice — including any database or network call behind an IQueryable.
  • Count() > 0 walks the sequence; Any() stops at the first element.
  • Materialize (ToList, ToArray) at the boundary where you want a snapshot.
  • Lambdas in hot loops allocate; for tight numeric code a for loop over a Span<T> is faster.

Strings — Standard Operations

UTF-16 chars underneath, text elements on screen. Search, split, slice with spans, compare ordinally or by culture, normalize, build, format and match text correctly.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=13
  • dotnet >=9
  • .NET 9 base class library (System, System.Text, System.Globalization, System.Text.RegularExpressions); culture data from ICU

Sources: Character encoding in .NET · Best practices for comparing strings in .NET · String class — .NET API · .NET regular expressions

I want to…

The standard member for each everyday job and its trap — some `string` methods compare ordinally by default and others by culture.

I want to…UseWatch out
know if text contains a wordContains, StartsWith, EndsWith with a StringComparisonContains(string) is ordinal, but StartsWith(string)/EndsWith(string) use the current culture
find where it isIndexOf(value, StringComparison.Ordinal), LastIndexOfIndexOf(string) with no comparison is culture-sensitive; -1 when absent

char, Rune, text element — and slicing safely

Count and cut by text elements whenever a person sees the result: length limits, truncation, cursor movement.

using System.Globalization;
using System.Text;

Console.OutputEncoding = Encoding.UTF8;           // Windows consoles default to a legacy code page
var samples = new (string Name, string Text)[]
{
    ("plain", "Ada"),
    ("family", "\U0001F469\u200D\U0001F469\u200D\U0001F467"),   // 👩‍👩‍👧: three emoji joined by U+200D
    ("composed", "Zo\u00EB"),                                    // Zoë, ë as one code point
    ("decomposed", "Zoe\u0308"),                                 // Zoë, e + COMBINING DIAERESIS
    ("flag", "\U0001F1E8\U0001F1F4"),                            // 🇨🇴: two regional-indicator letters
};
foreach (var (name, text) in samples)
{
    // Length and s[i] count UTF-16 chars; EnumerateRunes yields code points;
    // StringInfo counts text elements, which is what a reader sees
    var runes = text.EnumerateRunes().Count();
    var elements = new StringInfo(text).LengthInTextElements;
    Console.WriteLine($"{name,-10} chars {text.Length}  runes {runes}  text elements {elements}");
}

var status = "Shipped \U0001F680 today";                     // "Shipped 🚀 today"
var naive = status[..9];                                      // ends on half of 🚀
Console.WriteLine($"{char.IsHighSurrogate(naive[^1])} {Rune.TryGetRuneAt(naive, 8, out _)}");
Console.WriteLine(Truncate(status, 10));
Console.WriteLine(Rune.GetRuneAt(status, 8).Value.ToString("X", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));

// cut on text-element boundaries, so an emoji or an accent is never split
static string Truncate(string text, int max)
{
    ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfLessThan(max, 2);       // room for one element and the ellipsis
    var info = new StringInfo(text);
    return info.LengthInTextElements <= max ? text : info.SubstringByTextElements(0, max - 1) + "…";
}
Result
plain      chars 3  runes 3  text elements 3
family     chars 8  runes 5  text elements 1
composed   chars 3  runes 3  text elements 3
decomposed chars 4  runes 4  text elements 3
flag       chars 4  runes 2  text elements 1
True False
Shipped 🚀…
1F680

Search, split, join, trim, replace, pad

Parsing a pasted contact list: trim first, split on a known separator, and default every field that may be missing.

string[] pasted =
[
    "  Lovelace, Ada ; ADA@Example.com ; admin|editor ",
    "# exported 2026-03-08",
    "Hopper, Grace;grace@navy.example;",
    "Alan Turing;alan@example.org",
    "",
];

for (var index = 0; index < pasted.Length; index++)
{
    var line = pasted[index].Trim();
    if (line.Length == 0 || line.StartsWith('#')) continue;

    // TrimEntries trims every field; a missing field reads as "" instead of throwing
    var fields = line.Split(';', StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries);
    var name = fields[0];
    var email = fields.ElementAtOrDefault(1) ?? "";
    var roles = fields.ElementAtOrDefault(2) ?? "";

    var nameParts = name.Split(',', 2, StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries);       // "family, given", or one name
    var display = nameParts.Length == 2 ? $"{nameParts[1]} {nameParts[0]}" : name;
    var at = email.IndexOf('@');
    var domain = at < 0 ? "(no email)" : email[(at + 1)..].ToLowerInvariant();
    var roleList = roles.Split('|', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);

    Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" | ",
        FormattableString.Invariant($"C-{index + 1:D4}"),
        display.PadRight(14),
        domain.PadRight(14),
        roleList.Length == 0 ? "-" : string.Join(", ", roleList)));
}

var title = "Ada Lovelace";
Console.WriteLine($"{"2026-03-08".Replace("-", "/")} {title.Contains("love")}");
Console.WriteLine($"{title.Contains("love", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)}");
Console.WriteLine($"{"".Split(';').Length} {"admin|".Split('|').Length} {"--x--".Trim('-')}");
Console.WriteLine(title.IndexOf("Love", StringComparison.Ordinal));
Console.WriteLine($"[{"Total".PadRight(8)}][{"9.50".PadLeft(8)}]");
Console.WriteLine(string.Concat(Enumerable.Repeat("ab", 3)));
Result

C-0003 | Grace Hopper   | navy.example   | -
C-0004 | Alan Turing    | example.org    | -

Ranges, Span<char> and slicing without allocating

Parse with `ReadOnlySpan<char>` on hot paths, because a slice is a view rather than a copy, and search a fixed character set with a `SearchValues<char>` built once.

using System.Buffers;
using System.Globalization;

var orderId = "ORD-2026-001042";
Console.WriteLine($"{orderId[^6..]} {orderId[4..8]} {orderId[..3]}");   // a range on a string copies
// orderId[10..40] throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException: clamp the end yourself
Console.WriteLine(orderId[10..Math.Min(40, orderId.Length)]);

// a span is a window onto the same chars: slicing it copies nothing
ReadOnlySpan<char> id = orderId;
var year = int.Parse(id.Slice(4, 4), CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
var number = int.Parse(id[^6..], CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
Console.WriteLine($"{year} {number} {id.StartsWith("ORD-")}");      // span StartsWith is ordinal

// totalling a pasted price list without a string per field (.NET 9: Split on a span yields Ranges)
ReadOnlySpan<char> prices = "12.50;  4.25 ;;3.00";
decimal total = 0;
var skipped = 0;
foreach (Range range in prices.Split(';'))
{
    var field = prices[range].Trim();
    if (field.IsEmpty) { skipped++; continue; }
    total += decimal.Parse(field, NumberStyles.Number, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
}
Console.WriteLine($"total {total.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)}, {skipped} empty field");

// SearchValues (.NET 8): a character set prepared once, then searched fast many times
ReadOnlySpan<char> address = "Calle 10 #45-12, Bogotá";
Console.WriteLine(address.IndexOfAny(Separators.Address));          // the first '#', ',' or '-'
Console.WriteLine(address.ContainsAnyExceptInRange('\0', '\x7F'));  // any non-ASCII character?

static class Separators
{
    public static readonly SearchValues<char> Address = SearchValues.Create("#,-");
}

Ordinal or culture? Comparing and sorting

Compare ordinally (or with `OrdinalIgnoreCase`) anything a program reads — keys, identifiers, paths, protocol tokens — and use a culture comparer only for what a person reads.

using System.Globalization;

string[] customers = ["zoe", "Émile", "adam", "Zoë", "Ärzte GmbH", "Oskar", "Øster"];
var english = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");
var swedish = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("sv-SE");                 // å, ä, ö are letters after z

Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", customers.Order(StringComparer.Ordinal)));      // UTF-16 values
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", customers.Order(StringComparer.Create(english, ignoreCase: false))));
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", customers.Order(StringComparer.Create(swedish, ignoreCase: false))));

// identifiers, keys, file paths, HTTP headers: ordinal, ignoring case where the protocol says so
var headers = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
{
    ["Content-Type"] = "application/json",
};
Console.WriteLine(headers.ContainsKey("content-type"));

// the Turkish i: culture-sensitive case rules change the answer for ASCII text
var turkish = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("tr-TR");
Console.WriteLine($"{"title".ToUpper(turkish)} {"TITLE".ToLower(turkish)} {"title".ToUpperInvariant()}");
Console.WriteLine(string.Compare("FILE", "file", turkish, CompareOptions.IgnoreCase) == 0);
Console.WriteLine(string.Compare("FILE", "file", english, CompareOptions.IgnoreCase) == 0);
Console.WriteLine(string.Equals("FILE", "file", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

// a culture-aware match that ignores accents and case — for search boxes, not for keys
var compare = english.CompareInfo;
var loose = CompareOptions.IgnoreCase | CompareOptions.IgnoreNonSpace;
Console.WriteLine(compare.Compare("Zoë", "ZOE", loose) == 0);
Console.WriteLine(compare.IndexOf("Crème Brûlée", "brulee", loose));

// numeric ordering: "Room 10" after "Room 9" (.NET 10 adds CompareOptions.NumericOrdering)
string[] rooms = ["Room 10", "Room 9", "Room 1"];
var byNumber = rooms.OrderBy(r => int.Parse(r.AsSpan(5), CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", byNumber));

Case mapping and normalization

Normalize user input at the boundary, and remember that .NET maps case one char to one char, so `ß`/`ss` needs a linguistic comparison.

using System.Globalization;
using System.Text;

// .NET case mapping is one char to one char: lengths never change, and ß has no one-char capital
var german = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("de-DE");
Console.WriteLine($"{"straße".ToUpper(german)} {"straße".ToUpperInvariant().Length}");

// ordinal ignore-case misses ß = ss; IgnoreNonSpace matches it — and also ignores accents
var loose = CompareOptions.IgnoreCase | CompareOptions.IgnoreNonSpace;
Console.WriteLine(string.Equals("STRASSE", "straße", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
Console.WriteLine(german.CompareInfo.Compare("STRASSE", "straße", loose) == 0);
Console.WriteLine(german.CompareInfo.Compare("resume", "RÉSUMÉ", loose) == 0);

// the same visible name in two encodings: NFC (one code point) vs NFD (letter + combining mark),
// as old HFS+ file names and some pasted text deliver it
var fromFileName = "Zoe\u0308";
var storedInDb = "Zo\u00EB";
Console.WriteLine($"{fromFileName == storedInDb} {fromFileName.Normalize() == storedInDb}");
var linguistic = string.Equals(fromFileName, storedInDb, StringComparison.InvariantCulture);
Console.WriteLine($"{fromFileName.IsNormalized()} {linguistic}");

// NFKC also folds compatibility forms (ligatures, full-width digits): for keys, never for display
Console.WriteLine("ﬁle Ｎｏ１".Normalize(NormalizationForm.FormKC));

// an accent-insensitive key for Latin text: other scripts pass through with their marks
foreach (var name in new[] { "Crème Brûlée", "Zoë", "мой", "Ελλάδα", "パン", "हिंदी" })
    Console.WriteLine($"{name} → {LatinSearchKey(name)}");

// drop a combining mark only right after a Latin letter, so й, ї, Greek tonos, kana and Indic marks stay;
// đ, ø, ł and ß have no decomposition and stay too. Across scripts, use CompareInfo with IgnoreNonSpace
static string LatinSearchKey(string text)
{
    var builder = new StringBuilder(text.Length);
    var afterLatin = false;
    foreach (var c in text.Normalize(NormalizationForm.FormD))
    {
        var isMark = CharUnicodeInfo.GetUnicodeCategory(c) == UnicodeCategory.NonSpacingMark;
        if (isMark && afterLatin) continue;
        if (!isMark) afterLatin = char.IsAsciiLetter(c);
        builder.Append(c);
    }
    return builder.ToString().Normalize(NormalizationForm.FormC).ToLowerInvariant();
}

Building strings in a loop

Each `+=` copies everything built so far, so use one `StringBuilder`, whose interpolated `Append` overloads format straight into the buffer in the culture you pass.

Concatenation in a loop
using System.Globalization;

var usd = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");
(string Item, int Qty, decimal UnitPrice)[] order =
[
    ("Espresso", 2, 3.50m),
    ("Croissant", 1, 3.25m),
    ("Orange juice", 3, 4.00m),
];

// each += copies everything built so far: O(n²) characters for n lines
var receipt = "";
decimal total = 0;
for (var i = 0; i < order.Length; i++)
{
    var amount = order[i].Qty * order[i].UnitPrice;
    total += amount;
    receipt += order[i].Qty + " x " + order[i].Item.PadRight(13)
        + amount.ToString("C", usd).PadLeft(8) + "\n";
}
receipt += "Total".PadRight(17) + total.ToString("C", usd).PadLeft(8);
Console.WriteLine(receipt);
StringBuilder + interpolated Append
using System.Globalization;
using System.Text;

var usd = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");
(string Item, int Qty, decimal UnitPrice)[] order =
[
    ("Espresso", 2, 3.50m),
    ("Croissant", 1, 3.25m),
    ("Orange juice", 3, 4.00m),
];

// one growing buffer; the interpolated-string handler formats straight into it — no temporary strings
var receipt = new StringBuilder();
foreach (var (item, qty, unitPrice) in order)
    receipt.AppendLine(usd, $"{qty} x {item,-13}{qty * unitPrice,8:C}");

var total = order.Sum(line => line.Qty * line.UnitPrice);
receipt.Append(usd, $"{"Total",-17}{total,8:C}");
Console.WriteLine(receipt);
Result

1 x Croissant       $3.25
3 x Orange juice   $12.00
Total              $22.25

Format specifiers, culture, raw and UTF-8 literals

Pin the culture with `string.Create(culture, $"…")` or `FormattableString.Invariant`, parse runtime format strings once with `CompositeFormat`, and write JSON and paths as raw literals.

using System.Globalization;
using System.Text;

var german = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("de-DE");
var placed = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 3, 8, 14, 30, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(1));
decimal total = 1234.5m;
var orderNumber = 1042;

// format specifiers after the colon, alignment after the comma; string.Create pins the culture
Console.WriteLine(string.Create(german, $"Bestellung {orderNumber:D6}: {total:C} am {placed:d}"));
Console.WriteLine(string.Create(german, $"MwSt. {0.075:P1}"));
Console.WriteLine(FormattableString.Invariant($"{total:N2}|{orderNumber,8}|{orderNumber,-8}|{255:X4}"));
Console.WriteLine($"{placed:O}");          // round-trip ISO 8601: the same in every culture

// a format string from a resource: parse it once, reuse it (.NET 8)
var shipped = CompositeFormat.Parse("Order {0} shipped to {1} on {2:D}.");
Console.WriteLine(string.Format(CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US"), shipped, orderNumber, "Ada", placed));

// raw string literals: no escaping; with $$ a {{x}} interpolates and a single { is literal
var json = $$"""
    { "order": {{orderNumber}}, "customer": "Ada \"the first\"", "path": "C:\orders" }
    """;
Console.WriteLine(json);

// UTF-8 literal: the bytes are baked into the assembly — no transcoding at run time
ReadOnlySpan<byte> contentType = "application/json; charset=utf-8"u8;
Console.WriteLine(FormattableString.Invariant($"{contentType.Length} bytes, first byte {contentType[0]:X2}"));
Console.WriteLine($"{Encoding.UTF8.GetByteCount("Zoë")} UTF-8 bytes for Zoë");

Order 1042 shipped to Ada on Sunday, March 8, 2026.

Regex: named groups, [GeneratedRegex], CRLF, and catastrophic backtracking

Generate every pattern known at compile time, and give patterns that see untrusted input a match timeout, `RegexOptions.NonBacktracking` or an atomic rewrite.

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

// lines as a Windows editor saves them (CRLF), one name typed decomposed (zoe + U+0308)
var log = "2026-03-08 14:30 ERROR order=A-1042 user=ada\r\n"
        + "2026-03-08 14:31 INFO order=A-1043 user=grace\r\n"
        + "2026-03-08 14:35 ERROR order=A-1044 user=zoe\u0308\r\n";
foreach (Match entry in Patterns.LogEntry().Matches(log))
    if (entry.Groups["level"].ValueSpan is "ERROR")
        Console.WriteLine($"{entry.Groups["order"].Value} {entry.Groups["user"].Value.Normalize()}");
Console.WriteLine(Patterns.IsoDate().Replace("2026-03-08", "${d}/${m}/${y}"));

// a tag list typed by a user: (\w+\s?)* can split "aaaa…!" into words in 2^n ways
var hostile = new string('a', 40) + "!";
try { Patterns.TagsBacktracking().IsMatch(hostile); }
catch (RegexMatchTimeoutException) { Console.WriteLine("backtracking engine: timed out"); }
foreach (var input in new[] { hostile, "vip beta", "vip beta " })
{
    var linear = Patterns.TagsLinear().IsMatch(input);
    var atomic = Patterns.TagsAtomic().IsMatch(input);
    Console.WriteLine($"{input.Length,2} chars  non-backtracking: {linear}  atomic: {atomic}");
}

// [GeneratedRegex] writes each matcher as C# at build time: no pattern parsing at startup, trim-safe
static partial class Patterns
{
    // $ matches before \n only, so \r? lets CRLF lines match; \p{M} keeps combining accents in names
    [GeneratedRegex(
        @"^(?<date>[\d-]+) (?<time>[\d:]+) (?<level>[A-Z]+) "
            + @"order=(?<order>[A-Z]-\d+) user=(?<user>[\p{L}\p{M}]+)\r?$",
        RegexOptions.Multiline)]
    public static partial Regex LogEntry();

    [GeneratedRegex(@"^(?<y>\d{4})-(?<m>\d{2})-(?<d>\d{2})$")]
    public static partial Regex IsoDate();

    [GeneratedRegex(@"^(\w+\s?)*$", RegexOptions.None, matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 200)]
    public static partial Regex TagsBacktracking();

    // linear time; the generator hands this option to the runtime engine
    [GeneratedRegex(@"^(\w+\s?)*$", RegexOptions.NonBacktracking)]
    public static partial Regex TagsLinear();

    // the same language: the atomic group gives each run of letters one way to match
    [GeneratedRegex(@"^(?>\w+\s?)*$")]
    public static partial Regex TagsAtomic();
}
Result

A-1044 zoë
08/03/2026

41 chars  non-backtracking: False  atomic: False

 9 chars  non-backtracking: True  atomic: True

Pitfalls worth saying out loud

Most string bugs are culture or Unicode bugs that ASCII test data never finds.

  • Pass a StringComparison or StringComparer every time. The analyzer rules CA1307/CA1309/CA1310 flag the overloads that guess.
  • Test with real text: Zoë in NFC and NFD, 👩‍👩‍👧, 🇨🇴, straße, İstanbul, Arabic and Japanese — and under tr-TR as the current culture.
  • Pin the culture wherever text is formatted or parsed: CultureInfo.InvariantCulture for data and logs, the user's culture only for display.
  • += in a loop: strings are immutable, so each step copies the whole string. Use StringBuilder, string.Join or string.Create.
  • ToLower()/ToUpper() to make keys case-insensitive: they follow the current culture. Use OrdinalIgnoreCase (or ToUpperInvariant if you must normalize).
  • .Length as a user-facing limit, Substring for truncation, ToCharArray() to reverse: all three cut emoji and accents apart.
  • Asserting culture-formatted output against hard-coded text: it depends on the ICU version, so macOS (Apple ICU), Linux (vanilla ICU) and Windows can format the same culture differently (U+00A0, U+202F, ¥/￥). Assert against the formatter's own output.
  • A Regex without a timeout on untrusted input runs until it finishes. Set matchTimeoutMilliseconds, or AppContext data REGEX_DEFAULT_MATCH_TIMEOUT (a TimeSpan, set at startup before any Regex is used) for the whole process.
  • SearchValues.Create("…") (.NET 8) precomputes a character or string set for fast IndexOfAny/ContainsAny on spans.

System.Text.Json's defaults, against Newtonsoft.Json

System.Text.Json is built in and strict by default, so most migration surprises are a row of this table, and `JsonSerializerDefaults.Web` (what ASP.NET Core and `HttpClient`'s JSON helpers use) relaxes the first three: names, casing and numbers in strings.

BehaviourSystem.Text.JsonNewtonsoft.Json
property namesas declared; Web: camelCase; JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower and kebab built inas declared; CamelCasePropertyNamesContractResolver
reading namescase-sensitive; Web: case-insensitivecase-insensitive
"42" into an int, comments, trailing commasrejected unless NumberHandling, ReadCommentHandling, AllowTrailingCommasaccepted
memberspublic properties; fields with IncludeFields or [JsonInclude]; required and init honouredpublic properties and fields, private with [JsonProperty]

A record to JSON and back, with options you reuse

Create `JsonSerializerOptions` once and keep it, rename one member with `[JsonPropertyName]` when the policy would get it wrong, and keep one off the wire with `[JsonIgnore]`.

using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;

var order = new Order("o-1", "u-42", 59.90m, [new LineItem("sku-7", 2)]) { InternalNote = "VIP: call first" };
Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Serialize(order, Api.Json));

// The server sent different casing: the Web defaults read names case-insensitively.
const string Reply = """
    {"ID":"o-1","Customer_Id":"u-42","total":59.90,"lines":[{"sku":"sku-7","quantity":2}]}
    """;
var back = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Order>(Reply, Api.Json)!;
var note = back.InternalNote ?? "none";
Console.WriteLine($"{back.OrderId} for {back.CustomerId}: {back.Lines.Count} line(s), note: {note}");

static class Api
{
    // Created once: every new options instance rebuilds its metadata cache.
    public static readonly JsonSerializerOptions Json = new(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web)   // case-insensitive
    {
        PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower,
    };
}

record Order(
    [property: JsonPropertyName("id")] string OrderId,                // the one name the policy must not make
    string CustomerId,
    decimal Total,
    List<LineItem> Lines)
{
    [JsonIgnore] public string? InternalNote { get; init; }            // never leaves the process
}

record LineItem(string Sku, int Quantity);
Result
{"id":"o-1","customer_id":"u-42","total":59.90,"lines":[{"sku":"sku-7","quantity":2}]}
o-1 for u-42: 1 line(s), note: none

Required, missing, null and defaults — and unknown members kept

A missing member keeps its default, `required` or `[JsonRequired]` makes absence an error, a `null` reaches a non-nullable `string` unless you opt into `RespectNullableAnnotations` (.NET 9), and a relay keeps unknown members in `[JsonExtensionData]`.

using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;

var lenient = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web);
var strict = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web) { RespectNullableAnnotations = true };
var compact = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web)
{
    DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull,
};

Show("""{"id":"u-1","email":"ada@shop.example"}""", lenient);              // missing: defaults
Show("""{"email":"ada@shop.example"}""", lenient);                           // required id is missing
Show("""{"id":"u-1","email":"ada@shop.example","displayName":null}""", lenient);
Show("""{"id":"u-1","email":"ada@shop.example","displayName":null}""", strict);
Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Serialize(new Customer { Id = "u-1", Email = "ada@shop.example" }, compact));

// Unknown members, when you relay rather than validate: [JsonExtensionData] keeps them and writes them back.
var relayed = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Envelope>("""{"type":"order.paid","orderId":"o-1"}""", lenient)!;
Console.WriteLine($"{relayed.Extra!.Count} kept -> {JsonSerializer.Serialize(relayed, lenient)}");

static void Show(string json, JsonSerializerOptions options)
{
    try
    {
        var c = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Customer>(json, options)!;
        Console.WriteLine($"name={c.DisplayName ?? "(null!)"} phone={c.Phone ?? "-"} points={c.Points}");
    }
    catch (JsonException e) { Console.WriteLine($"rejected: {e.Message}"); }
}

record Customer
{
    public required string Id { get; init; }                 // C# required: honoured by the serializer
    [JsonRequired] public string Email { get; init; } = "";  // must be in the JSON, even with a default
    public string DisplayName { get; init; } = "Guest";      // missing: keeps the initializer
    public string? Phone { get; init; }                      // missing or null: null
    public int Points { get; init; }                         // missing: 0
}

record Envelope(string Type)
{
    [JsonExtensionData] public Dictionary<string, JsonElement>? Extra { get; set; }
}

Dates, and enums through a strict custom JsonConverter

Dates are ISO 8601 by default, and enums from untrusted input go through a small `JsonConverter<T>` with an exact allow-list of names, because `JsonStringEnumConverter` still accepts comma lists and C# names even with integers refused.

using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;

var options = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web);
options.Converters.Add(new ExactNames<Status>());
var shipment = new Shipment("o-1", Status.InTransit,
    PlacedAt: new DateTimeOffset(2026, 11, 16, 9, 30, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(1)),   // ISO 8601, offset kept
    DeliverBy: new DateOnly(2026, 11, 20));                                     // no time zone to get wrong
var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(shipment, options);
Console.WriteLine(json);
Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Shipment>(json, options) == shipment);

// JsonStringEnumConverter, even with allowIntegerValues: false, still reads "pending, delivered" as Delivered
// and accepts the C# name "InTransit"; ExactNames takes the wire names and nothing else.
foreach (var wrong in new[] { "\"teleported\"", "7", "\"7\"", "\"pending, delivered\"", "\"InTransit\"" })
{
    try { JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Shipment>(json.Replace("\"in_transit\"", wrong), options); }
    catch (JsonException e) { Console.WriteLine($"status {wrong}: rejected at {e.Path}"); }
}

enum Status { Pending, InTransit, Delivered }

record Shipment(string OrderId, Status Status, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, DateOnly DeliverBy);

// A custom converter: an exact allow-list of snake_case names (Unix-seconds dates are written the same way).
sealed class ExactNames<T> : JsonConverter<T> where T : struct, Enum
{
    static readonly Dictionary<string, T> ByName =
        Enum.GetValues<T>().ToDictionary(v => JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower.ConvertName(v.ToString()));

    public override T Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type type, JsonSerializerOptions options) =>
        reader.TokenType == JsonTokenType.String && ByName.TryGetValue(reader.GetString()!, out var value)
            ? value
            : throw new JsonException($"not a {typeof(T).Name}");

    public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, T value, JsonSerializerOptions options) =>
        writer.WriteStringValue(JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower.ConvertName(value.ToString()));
}

Polymorphic payloads with [JsonPolymorphic] and [JsonDerivedType]

Only the derived types you list can be created (an allow-list, unlike `$type`), and the discriminator must come first unless you set `AllowOutOfOrderMetadataProperties` (.NET 9).

using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;

var web = JsonSerializerOptions.Web;
List<Payment> payments = [new CardPayment(59.90m, "4242"), new PayPalPayment(12.00m, "ada@shop.example")];
Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Serialize(payments, web));

const string Received = """
    [{"method":"card","amount":5,"last4":"0005"},{"method":"paypal","amount":7,"email":"bob@shop.example"}]
    """;
foreach (var payment in JsonSerializer.Deserialize<List<Payment>>(Received, web)!)
    Console.WriteLine(payment switch
    {
        CardPayment card => $"card ending {card.Last4}: {card.Amount}",
        PayPalPayment paypal => $"PayPal {paypal.Email}: {paypal.Amount}",
        _ => "unknown",
    });

// What many other serializers write. An abstract base throws NotSupportedException here, a concrete one
// JsonException: catch both at an API boundary, or allow the order.
const string Reordered = """{"amount":5,"method":"card","last4":"0005"}""";
try { JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Payment>(Reordered, web); }
catch (NotSupportedException) { Console.WriteLine("discriminator not first: rejected"); }
var tolerant = new JsonSerializerOptions(web) { AllowOutOfOrderMetadataProperties = true };      // .NET 9
Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Payment>(Reordered, tolerant) is CardPayment);

try { JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Payment>("""{"method":"crypto","amount":1}""", web); }
catch (JsonException) { Console.WriteLine("unlisted type: rejected"); }

[JsonPolymorphic(TypeDiscriminatorPropertyName = "method")]
[JsonDerivedType(typeof(CardPayment), "card")]
[JsonDerivedType(typeof(PayPalPayment), "paypal")]
abstract record Payment(decimal Amount);

record CardPayment(decimal Amount, string Last4) : Payment(Amount);

record PayPalPayment(decimal Amount, string Email) : Payment(Amount);

Source generation with JsonSerializerContext, for trimming and Native AOT

The generator writes the metadata and a fast serializer at build time, so nothing is reflected at run time and the code trims and runs under Native AOT; pass `Context.Default.Options` where an API takes options.

using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;

List<Order> orders = [new("o-1", OrderStatus.Paid, 59.90m), new("o-2", OrderStatus.Pending, 12.00m)];

var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(orders, ShopJsonContext.Default.ListOrder);   // generated JsonTypeInfo
Console.WriteLine(json);
var back = JsonSerializer.Deserialize(json, ShopJsonContext.Default.ListOrder)!;
Console.WriteLine($"{back.Count} orders, first {back[0].Status}");

// Proof the generator ran: the fast-path serializer is generated code, not reflection.
Console.WriteLine($"generated fast path: {ShopJsonContext.Default.Order.SerializeHandler is not null}");

// Code that takes options (HttpClient's JSON helpers, ASP.NET Core): pass the context's own options.
Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Serialize(back[1], ShopJsonContext.Default.Options));
// Other options that merely use the context keep their own naming; the enum converter, baked into
// the generated metadata, still applies. Or add the context to the app's options' TypeInfoResolverChain.
var other = new JsonSerializerOptions { TypeInfoResolver = ShopJsonContext.Default };
Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Serialize(back[1], other));

enum OrderStatus { Pending, Paid, Shipped }
record Order(string Id, OrderStatus Status, decimal Total);

[JsonSourceGenerationOptions(
    PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonKnownNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower, UseStringEnumConverter = true)]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(List<Order>))]
partial class ShopJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext { }
Result

Without a model: JsonNode and JsonDocument — and streaming a big array

`JsonNode` to patch a document you do not own, `JsonDocument` to read a few values cheaply (dispose it), `DeserializeAsyncEnumerable` to process a large array one element at a time.

using System.Text;
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Nodes;

const string Webhook = """
    {"event":"order.updated","meta":{"v":3},
     "order":{"id":"o-1","status":"pending","lines":[{"sku":"sku-7","qty":2}]}}
    """;

var node = JsonNode.Parse(Webhook)!;                                         // mutable tree
node["order"]!["status"] = "paid";
node["order"]!["lines"]!.AsArray().Add(new JsonObject { ["sku"] = "sku-9", ["qty"] = 1 });
Console.WriteLine(node["order"]!.ToJsonString());

using (var doc = JsonDocument.Parse(Webhook))                         // read-only, from pooled buffers
{
    var root = doc.RootElement;
    var version = root.TryGetProperty("meta", out var meta) && meta.TryGetProperty("v", out var v)
        ? v.GetInt32()
        : 1;
    Console.WriteLine($"{root.GetProperty("event").GetString()} v{version}");
}

// A 10,000-order export: only one element is materialised at a time.
var export = new StringBuilder("[");
for (var i = 1; i <= 10_000; i++)
    export.Append(i > 1 ? "," : "").Append($$"""{"id":"o-{{i}}","totalCents":{{i % 100 * 10}}}""");
var bytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(export.Append(']').ToString());
await using var stream = new MemoryStream(bytes);                     // a response or file stream in the app

long count = 0, cents = 0;
var rows = JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsyncEnumerable<ExportRow>(stream, JsonSerializerOptions.Web);
await foreach (var row in rows)
{
    count++;
    cents += row!.TotalCents;
}
Console.WriteLine($"{count} orders, {cents / 100} total");

record ExportRow(string Id, int TotalCents);
Result
{"id":"o-1","status":"paid","lines":[{"sku":"sku-7","qty":2},{"sku":"sku-9","qty":1}]}
order.updated v3
10000 orders, 49500 total

Untrusted input: refuse unknown members, report the path, then validate

Deserializing proves the shape, not the meaning, so refuse a `null` body and unknown, missing, null and string-typed numeric members, tell the client where with `JsonException.Path`, and then validate the values.

using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;

var strict = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web)
{
    UnmappedMemberHandling = JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow,   // "isAdmin": true is refused, not ignored
    RespectRequiredConstructorParameters = true,                    // a missing "email" is refused, not null
    RespectNullableAnnotations = true,                              // "email": null is refused too
    NumberHandling = JsonNumberHandling.Strict,                     // "36" is not 36 (Web defaults allow it)
    MaxDepth = 16,
};

foreach (var body in new[]
{
    """{"email":"ada@shop.example","displayName":"Ada","age":36}""",
    """{"age":36}""",
    "null",
    """{"email":"ada@shop.example","displayName":"Ada","age":36,"isAdmin":true}""",
    """{"email":"ada@shop.example","displayName":"Ada","age":"36"}""",
    """{"email":"not-an-email","displayName":"","age":7}""",
})
    Console.WriteLine(Accept(body, strict));

static string Accept(string body, JsonSerializerOptions options)
{
    SignUp? request;
    try { request = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<SignUp>(body, options); }
    catch (JsonException e) { return $"400 at {e.Path}"; }              // its message can echo the input
    if (request is null) return "400 at $";                               // the body "null" is valid JSON
    var problems = new List<ValidationResult>();
    if (Validator.TryValidateObject(request, new(request), problems, validateAllProperties: true))
        return $"201 {request.DisplayName}";
    return $"422 {string.Join("; ", problems.Select(p => p.ErrorMessage))}";
}

record SignUp(
    [property: Required, EmailAddress] string Email,
    [property: Required, StringLength(40, MinimumLength = 1)] string DisplayName,
    [property: Range(13, 120)] int Age);
Result
201 Ada
400 at $
400 at $
400 at $.isAdmin
400 at $.age
422 The Email field is not a valid e-mail address.; The DisplayName field is required.; The field Age must be between 13 and 120.

XML: XmlSerializer for a typed model, XDocument for a quick read

`XmlSerializer` maps public classes with a parameterless constructor, LINQ to XML is shorter for a value or two, and untrusted XML goes through an `XmlReader` (DTDs prohibited), since `XDocument.Parse` and a `TextReader` accept a DTD and only cap its expansion and skip external entities.

using System.Xml;
using System.Xml.Linq;
using System.Xml.Serialization;

var order = new OrderXml { Id = "o-1", Status = "paid", Lines = [new() { Sku = "sku-7", Quantity = 2 }] };
var serializer = new XmlSerializer(typeof(OrderXml));                 // cache it: building one is expensive

using var writer = new StringWriter();
using (var xml = XmlWriter.Create(writer, new XmlWriterSettings { OmitXmlDeclaration = true }))
    serializer.Serialize(xml, order, new XmlSerializerNamespaces([XmlQualifiedName.Empty]));   // no xsi, xsd
Console.WriteLine(writer);

// Untrusted XML goes through an XmlReader: its default DtdProcessing.Prohibit refuses any DTD.
using var reader = XmlReader.Create(new StringReader(writer.ToString()));
var back = (OrderXml)serializer.Deserialize(reader)!;
Console.WriteLine($"{back.Id}: {back.Lines.Sum(l => l.Quantity)} item(s)");

var status = (string?)XDocument.Parse(writer.ToString()).Root!.Element("status");
Console.WriteLine($"status via XDocument: {status}");

[XmlRoot("order")]
public class OrderXml
{
    [XmlAttribute("id")] public string Id { get; set; } = "";
    [XmlElement("status")] public string Status { get; set; } = "";
    [XmlArray("lines"), XmlArrayItem("line")] public List<LineXml> Lines { get; set; } = [];
}

public class LineXml
{
    [XmlAttribute("sku")] public string Sku { get; set; } = "";
    [XmlAttribute("qty")] public int Quantity { get; set; }
}

Binary: a fixed layout with BinaryPrimitives

When size or speed matters (device sync, a cache, a socket protocol), a versioned fixed layout in network byte order with money as integer cents is a few lines, and the writer refuses what the reader would reject.

using System.Buffers.Binary;
using System.Text;

// An offline-sync record for a handheld scanner: 33 bytes instead of ~90 of JSON.
var line = new OrderLine(1042, Cents: 5990, DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(1_795_000_000), "sku-7");
var bytes = OrderLineCodec.Write(line);
Console.WriteLine($"{bytes.Length} bytes: {Convert.ToHexString(bytes)}");     // read it as the next card does

try { OrderLineCodec.Write(line with { Cents = -1 }); }
catch (ArgumentException e) { Console.WriteLine($"not written: {e.Message}"); }

record OrderLine(int OrderNumber, long Cents, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, string Sku);   // money in cents

static class OrderLineCodec
{
    public const byte Version = 1;
    public const int Size = 1 + 4 + 8 + 8 + 12;                           // version, number, cents, time, SKU

    public static byte[] Write(OrderLine line)
    {
        if (line.Cents < 0) throw new ArgumentException("a negative amount");
        if (line.Sku.Length > 12 || !Ascii.IsValid(line.Sku))
            throw new ArgumentException("a SKU is at most 12 ASCII characters");
        var buffer = new byte[Size];
        buffer[0] = Version;                                               // bump it when the layout changes
        BinaryPrimitives.WriteInt32BigEndian(buffer.AsSpan(1), line.OrderNumber);   // network byte order
        BinaryPrimitives.WriteInt64BigEndian(buffer.AsSpan(5), line.Cents);
        BinaryPrimitives.WriteInt64BigEndian(buffer.AsSpan(13), line.PlacedAt.ToUnixTimeSeconds());
        Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(line.Sku, buffer.AsSpan(21));                // the rest stays zero padding
        return buffer;
    }
}
Result
33 bytes: 01000004120000000000001766000000006AFD86C0736B752D3700000000000000
not written: a negative amount

Binary: reading an untrusted record

Check the length, the version and every field before trusting it, and fail with one exception type, `InvalidDataException`, for any corrupt input.

using System.Buffers.Binary;
using System.Text;

var bytes = Convert.FromHexString("01000004120000000000001766000000006AFD86C0736B752D3700000000000000");
var line = OrderLineReader.Read(bytes);                                 // the previous card's record
Console.WriteLine($"#{line.OrderNumber} {line.Sku} {line.Cents} cents at {line.PlacedAt:u}");

byte[] Patched(int at, long value)
{
    var copy = bytes.ToArray();
    BinaryPrimitives.WriteInt64BigEndian(copy.AsSpan(at), value);
    return copy;
}

byte[][] damagedRecords =
[
    bytes[..10], [2, .. bytes[1..]],                                     // truncated, an unknown version
    Patched(5, -1), Patched(13, long.MaxValue),                          // negative cents, an impossible time
    [.. bytes[..21], 0xFF, .. bytes[22..]],                              // a non-ASCII byte in the SKU
];
foreach (var damaged in damagedRecords)
{
    try { OrderLineReader.Read(damaged); }
    catch (InvalidDataException e) { Console.WriteLine($"rejected: {e.Message}"); }   // the only type thrown
}

record OrderLine(int OrderNumber, long Cents, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, string Sku);

static class OrderLineReader
{
    static readonly long MaxSeconds = DateTimeOffset.MaxValue.ToUnixTimeSeconds();

    public static OrderLine Read(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data)
    {
        if (data.Length != 33) throw new InvalidDataException($"expected 33 bytes, got {data.Length}");
        if (data[0] != 1) throw new InvalidDataException($"unknown version {data[0]}");
        var cents = BinaryPrimitives.ReadInt64BigEndian(data[5..]);
        if (cents < 0) throw new InvalidDataException("a negative amount");
        var seconds = BinaryPrimitives.ReadInt64BigEndian(data[13..]);
        if (seconds < 0 || seconds > MaxSeconds) throw new InvalidDataException("a time out of range");
        if (!Ascii.IsValid(data[21..])) throw new InvalidDataException("a SKU that is not ASCII");
        var sku = Encoding.ASCII.GetString(data[21..]).TrimEnd('\0');
        var placedAt = DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(seconds);
        return new(BinaryPrimitives.ReadInt32BigEndian(data[1..]), cents, placedAt, sku);
    }
}
Result

rejected: unknown version 2
rejected: a negative amount
rejected: a time out of range

Pitfalls worth saying out loud

And where a schema-first format fits.

  • new JsonSerializerOptions() inside a method called per request: every instance rebuilds its cache. Keep one static readonly instance (or JsonSerializerOptions.Web).
  • Trusting that a non-nullable string is never null after deserializing: it is not enforced unless RespectNullableAnnotations (an explicit null) and RespectRequiredConstructorParameters (a missing member) are both on (.NET 9) — or you validate.
  • Assuming .NET 9 refuses a duplicate key or a huge body: the last of two email members wins (.NET 10 adds AllowDuplicateProperties = false), and the whole body is parsed before validation, so cap it first (Kestrel MaxRequestBodySize, [RequestSizeLimit]).
  • TypeNameHandling in Newtonsoft.Json or BinaryFormatter on untrusted data: both can instantiate arbitrary types. BinaryFormatter is removed from .NET 9; use [JsonPolymorphic] with an allow-list.
  • DateTime without a kind on the wire: send DateTimeOffset (or UTC), and DateOnly for calendar dates.
  • Returning JsonException.Message to a client: it can quote the input. Return the Path and a fixed message.
  • Use source generation (JsonSerializerContext) in MAUI, Blazor WebAssembly and anything trimmed or AOT-compiled: reflection-based metadata may be trimmed away.
  • Treat the JSON shape as a contract: add members as optional, never repurpose a name, and version the payload when meaning changes.
  • Schema-first binary: Protobuf (Google.Protobuf, generated from .proto by Grpc.Tools) or MessagePack (MessagePack-CSharp, [MessagePackObject] with [Key(n)]) are smaller and faster; numbered fields make old and new versions compatible. Reach for them for gRPC, caches and device sync — keep JSON for public APIs.

Async/Await, Tasks & Cancellation

Sequential vs concurrent awaits, WhenAll and its exceptions, CancellationToken, IAsyncEnumerable and bridging callbacks.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12

Sources: Asynchronous programming with async and await — C# · Cancellation in managed threads — .NET

Sequential vs concurrent

A task starts when it is created; `await` only waits. Start both, then await both.

using System.Diagnostics;

static async Task<string> Load(string name)
{
    await Task.Delay(100);                         // frees the thread while waiting
    return name;
}

var clock = Stopwatch.StartNew();
var user = await Load("user");
var posts = await Load("posts");
var sequential = clock.ElapsedMilliseconds;

clock.Restart();
var both = await Task.WhenAll(Load("user"), Load("posts"));
var concurrent = clock.ElapsedMilliseconds;
Console.WriteLine($"{user} {posts} | {string.Join(" ", both)}");
// About 200 ms against about 100 ms; compared, not printed, so a busy machine cannot change the output
Console.WriteLine($"concurrent took well under the sequential time: {concurrent < sequential * 3 / 4}");
Result
user posts | user posts
concurrent took well under the sequential time: True

Cancellation with CancellationToken

Cancellation is a token you pass down; awaiting a cancelled operation throws `OperationCanceledException`.

static async Task Poll(CancellationToken token, Action<int> onTick)
{
    for (var i = 0; ; i++)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"tick {i}");
        onTick(i);
        await Task.Delay(50, token);           // a cancellation point
    }
}

// new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)) cancels on a deadline the same way
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource();
try
{
    await Poll(cts.Token, i => { if (i == 2) cts.Cancel(); });   // e.g. the user left the screen
}
catch (OperationCanceledException)
{
    Console.WriteLine("cancelled");
}

tick 0
tick 1
tick 2
cancelled

WhenAll and its exceptions

`await` rethrows the first failure only; the task's `Exception` holds all of them.

static async Task<int> Work(int n)
{
    await Task.Delay(10 * n);
    return n == 2 ? throw new InvalidOperationException($"job {n} failed") : n;
}

var all = Task.WhenAll(Work(1), Work(2), Work(3));
try
{
    await all;
}
catch (InvalidOperationException e)
{
    Console.WriteLine(e.Message);
    Console.WriteLine($"{all.Exception!.InnerExceptions.Count} failure(s) recorded");
}

job 2 failed
1 failure(s) recorded

Async streams

`IAsyncEnumerable` is the pull-based stream; `break` disposes the enumerator, so no further page is fetched.

using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

static async IAsyncEnumerable<int[]> Pages(int total, int size, [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken token = default)
{
    for (var offset = 0; offset < total; offset += size)
    {
        await Task.Delay(10, token);               // stand-in for a fetch
        yield return Enumerable.Range(offset, Math.Min(size, total - offset)).ToArray();
    }
}

var seen = 0;
await foreach (var page in Pages(7, 3))
{
    seen += page.Length;
    Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", page));
    if (seen >= 6) break;
}
Result
0,1,2
3,4,5

Bridging callbacks

`TaskCompletionSource` is `withCheckedContinuation`; `WaitAsync` adds a timeout to any task.

static void FetchTheme(Action<string> onDone) =>        // a callback API you do not own
    ThreadPool.QueueUserWorkItem(_ => onDone("dark"));

static Task<string> FetchThemeAsync()
{
    var tcs = new TaskCompletionSource<string>(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously);
    FetchTheme(value => tcs.SetResult(value));
    return tcs.Task;
}

Console.WriteLine(await FetchThemeAsync());
Console.WriteLine(await FetchThemeAsync().WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)));

Rules

What reviewers flag first.

  • async void outside event handlers: exceptions crash the process and nobody can await it.
  • .Result / .Wait() on a UI or legacy ASP.NET context deadlocks — await all the way up.
  • Accept a CancellationToken in every async API and pass it to everything you call.
  • ConfigureAwait(false) in library code that does not need the caller's context.
  • ValueTask only for hot paths that usually complete synchronously; await it exactly once.

Algorithmic Patterns & Complexity

The BCL's costs, then the patterns that solve most problems — PriorityQueue and BinarySearch included.

  • dotnet

Built-in costs

Two sorts with different guarantees — know which one you called.

NeedBuilt-inCost
stack / queueStack<T>, Queue<T>O(1)
priority queuePriorityQueue<TElement, TPriority>O(log n) enqueue / dequeue
sorted map / setSortedDictionary, SortedSetO(log n); SortedSet.GetViewBetween for ranges
sort in placeArray.Sort, List.SortO(n log n) introsort — not stable
sort a copyOrderByO(n log n) — stable
binary searchArray.BinarySearch, List.BinarySearchO(log n); ~result is the insertion point on a miss
build a stringStringBuilder, string.Join+= in a loop is O(n²)

Two pointers

On sorted input, move the pointer that brings the sum closer. O(n), O(1) space.

static (int, int)? PairWithSum(int[] sorted, int target)
{
    int lo = 0, hi = sorted.Length - 1;
    while (lo < hi)
    {
        var sum = sorted[lo] + sorted[hi];
        if (sum == target) return (lo, hi);
        if (sum < target) lo++; else hi--;
    }
    return null;
}

Console.WriteLine($"{PairWithSum([1, 3, 4, 6, 9], 10)} {PairWithSum([1, 2], 7)?.ToString() ?? "none"}");

Sliding window

Longest substring without repeats — grow the right edge, jump the left past the last repeat. O(n).

static int LongestUnique(string s)
{
    var lastSeen = new Dictionary<char, int>();
    int start = 0, best = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < s.Length; i++)
    {
        if (lastSeen.TryGetValue(s[i], out var prev) && prev >= start) start = prev + 1;
        lastSeen[s[i]] = i;
        best = Math.Max(best, i - start + 1);
    }
    return best;
}

Console.WriteLine($"{LongestUnique("abcabcbb")} {LongestUnique("pwwkew")}");
Result

Heap — top k

A min-heap of size k keeps the k largest; its root is the smallest of them. O(n log k).

static int[] TopK(IEnumerable<int> xs, int k)
{
    var heap = new PriorityQueue<int, int>();
    foreach (var x in xs)
    {
        heap.Enqueue(x, x);
        if (heap.Count > k) heap.Dequeue();
    }
    return [.. heap.UnorderedItems.Select(e => e.Element).OrderDescending()];
}

Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", TopK([5, 1, 9, 3, 7, 9, 2], 3)));

Breadth-first search on a grid

BFS finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

static int ShortestPath(string[] grid, (int R, int C) from, (int R, int C) to)
{
    var dist = new Dictionary<(int, int), int> { [from] = 0 };
    var queue = new Queue<(int R, int C)>([from]);
    while (queue.TryDequeue(out var cell))
    {
        var here = dist[cell];
        if (cell == to) return here;
        foreach (var (dr, dc) in new[] { (1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1) })
        {
            var next = (R: cell.R + dr, C: cell.C + dc);
            if (next.R < 0 || next.C < 0 || next.R >= grid.Length || next.C >= grid[0].Length
                || grid[next.R][next.C] == '#' || dist.ContainsKey(next)) continue;
            dist[next] = here + 1;
            queue.Enqueue(next);
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

Console.WriteLine(ShortestPath(["..#.", ".##.", "...."], (0, 0), (0, 3)));
Result
7

Hash map: counting, grouping, memory of the past

The default first idea, O(n) hash operations and O(n) space (anagram keys add a per-word sort) — two prices that use a gift card exactly, the first unique letter, anagram groups.

using System.Runtime.InteropServices;

// Two-sum on unsorted input: remember each value's index and look up the complement. O(n).
static (int, int)? TwoSum(int[] prices, int budget)
{
    var seen = new Dictionary<int, int>();               // price -> index
    for (var i = 0; i < prices.Length; i++)
    {
        if (seen.TryGetValue(budget - prices[i], out var j)) return (j, i);   // checked(...) near int limits
        seen.TryAdd(prices[i], i);                       // keep the first index of a repeated price
    }
    return null;
}

// First non-repeating character: count once, then scan in the original order.
static char? FirstUnique(string s)
{
    var counts = new Dictionary<char, int>();
    foreach (var c in s)
        CollectionsMarshal.GetValueRefOrAddDefault(counts, c, out _)++;   // one lookup, not two
    foreach (var c in s)
        if (counts[c] == 1) return c;
    return null;
}

// Group anagrams under a canonical key, the sorted letters: O(n · L log L) for n words of length L.
static IEnumerable<string[]> GroupAnagrams(string[] words) =>
    words.GroupBy(w => string.Concat(w.Order())).Select(g => g.ToArray());

Console.WriteLine($"two items for a 50 gift card: {TwoSum([30, 45, 15, 20], 50)}");
Console.WriteLine($"first unique letter of 'swiss': {FirstUnique("swiss")}");
var groups = GroupAnagrams(["eat", "tea", "tan", "ate", "nat", "bat"]);
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", groups.Select(g => $"[{string.Join(",", g)}]")));

Prefix sums & difference arrays

Many range-sum queries over daily revenue in O(1) each (sums in `long`: totals outgrow `int`), and many range updates (seats booked on a span of flights) in O(1) each.

// Range sums over daily revenue: O(n) to build, then O(1) per query.
int[] revenue = [120, 80, 0, 200, 50, 90, 300];
var prefix = new long[revenue.Length + 1];   // prefix[i] = sum of the first i days; long: totals outgrow int
for (var i = 0; i < revenue.Length; i++) prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + revenue[i];
long RangeSum(int from, int to) => prefix[to + 1] - prefix[from];   // inclusive days
Console.WriteLine($"days 1-3: {RangeSum(1, 3)}, days 0-6: {RangeSum(0, 6)}");

// How many runs of consecutive days sum exactly to 250? Prefix sums + a hash map, O(n).
static int SubarraysSumming(int[] xs, int k)
{
    var seen = new Dictionary<long, int> { [0] = 1 };    // prefix value -> how many times seen
    long running = 0;
    var total = 0;
    foreach (var x in xs)
    {
        running += x;
        total += seen.GetValueOrDefault(running - k);
        seen[running] = seen.GetValueOrDefault(running) + 1;
    }
    return total;
}
Console.WriteLine($"runs summing to 250: {SubarraysSumming(revenue, 250)}");

// Difference array: seat bookings over ranges of flights, O(1) per booking, one pass at the end.
(int First, int Last, int Seats)[] bookings = [(1, 2, 10), (2, 3, 20), (2, 5, 25)];
var diff = new int[5 + 2];                               // flights 1..5, plus one past the end
foreach (var (first, last, seats) in bookings) { diff[first] += seats; diff[last + 1] -= seats; }
var perFlight = new int[5];
for (int f = 1, running = 0; f <= 5; f++) perFlight[f - 1] = running += diff[f];
Console.WriteLine($"seats per flight: {string.Join(",", perFlight)}");

Sort then sweep: intervals

Merge overlapping bookings and count the rooms a day needs — sorting first turns both into one linear pass, O(n log n).

// Merge overlapping calendar bookings, then find how many rooms the day needs. O(n log n).
Booking[] day = [new(9, 10), new(13, 15), new(9, 12), new(14, 16), new(11, 12)];
Console.WriteLine($"busy: {string.Join(" ", Merge(day))}");
Console.WriteLine($"rooms needed: {MinRooms(day)}");

static List<Booking> Merge(IEnumerable<Booking> bookings)
{
    var merged = new List<Booking>();
    foreach (var b in bookings.OrderBy(b => b.Start))
    {
        if (merged.Count > 0 && b.Start <= merged[^1].End)                       // overlaps the last one
            merged[^1] = merged[^1] with { End = Math.Max(merged[^1].End, b.End) };
        else
            merged.Add(b);
    }
    return merged;
}

// Sweep line: +1 at every start, -1 at every end, walked in time order; the peak is the answer.
static int MinRooms(IEnumerable<Booking> bookings)
{
    var events = bookings.SelectMany(b => new[] { (At: b.Start, Delta: 1), (At: b.End, Delta: -1) })
        .OrderBy(e => e.At).ThenBy(e => e.Delta);       // an end before a start at the same hour
    int current = 0, peak = 0;
    foreach (var (_, delta) in events) peak = Math.Max(peak, current += delta);
    return peak;
}

record struct Booking(int Start, int End)
{
    public override readonly string ToString() => $"{Start}-{End}";
}

Stack & monotonic stack

Matching brackets, and "how long until a bigger value" (daily temperatures, next greater element) in one O(n) pass.

// Validate the brackets in a template expression before evaluating it. O(n).
static bool IsBalanced(string s)
{
    var openerOf = new Dictionary<char, char> { [')'] = '(', [']'] = '[', ['}'] = '{' };
    var stack = new Stack<char>();
    foreach (var c in s)
    {
        if (c is '(' or '[' or '{') stack.Push(c);
        else if (openerOf.TryGetValue(c, out var opener) && (!stack.TryPop(out var top) || top != opener))
            return false;
    }
    return stack.Count == 0;
}

// Daily temperatures: how many days until a warmer one? A stack of indices, values decreasing. O(n).
static int[] DaysUntilWarmer(int[] temps)
{
    var answer = new int[temps.Length];                  // 0 when no warmer day comes
    var waiting = new Stack<int>();
    for (var i = 0; i < temps.Length; i++)
    {
        while (waiting.TryPeek(out var day) && temps[day] < temps[i])
            answer[waiting.Pop()] = i - day;             // today is the answer for that day
        waiting.Push(i);
    }
    return answer;
}

Console.WriteLine($"{IsBalanced("{items[(i + 1)]}")} {IsBalanced("(]")} {IsBalanced("((")}");
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", DaysUntilWarmer([73, 74, 75, 71, 69, 72, 76, 73])));

Fast & slow pointers (linked lists)

Find a playlist's middle track, detect a loop and the track where it starts (Floyd) — O(n) time and O(1) space.

// A playlist as a singly linked list: find the middle track, detect a loop and where it starts.
var playlist = new Track("intro")
    { Next = new("verse") { Next = new("chorus") { Next = new("bridge") { Next = new("outro") } } } };
Console.WriteLine($"middle: {Middle(playlist)?.Title}, loop: {CycleStart(playlist)?.Title ?? "none"}");

var looped = new Track("intro") { Next = new("verse") { Next = new("chorus") } };
looped.Next!.Next!.Next = looped.Next;                   // chorus -> verse: a repeat-forever bug
Console.WriteLine($"looped list: loop starts at {CycleStart(looped)?.Title}");

static Track? Middle(Track? head)                        // slow moves 1, fast moves 2
{
    Track? slow = head, fast = head;
    while (fast?.Next is not null) (slow, fast) = (slow!.Next, fast.Next.Next);
    return slow;
}

// Floyd, O(n) time and O(1) space: once slow and fast meet, a pointer from the head and one from the
// meeting point, both moving 1, meet at the loop's first node.
static Track? CycleStart(Track? head)
{
    Track? slow = head, fast = head;
    while (fast?.Next is not null)
    {
        (slow, fast) = (slow!.Next, fast.Next.Next);
        if (!ReferenceEquals(slow, fast)) continue;      // identity, not equality
        var start = head;
        while (!ReferenceEquals(start, slow)) (start, slow) = (start!.Next, slow!.Next);
        return start;
    }
    return null;                                         // fast fell off the end: no loop
}

sealed class Track(string title)
{
    public string Title { get; } = title;
    public Track? Next { get; set; }
}

looped list: loop starts at verse

Trees: DFS on a binary search tree

Recursion for depth — in-order gives a BST sorted, and a range passed down validates it; recursion depth is the tree's height, so a sorted-insert tree overflows the stack.

// A category tree stored as a binary search tree by id: insert, in-order DFS, validation.
TreeNode? root = null;
foreach (var id in new[] { 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80, 30 }) root = Insert(root, id);

var sorted = new List<int>();
InOrder(root, sorted);
Console.WriteLine($"in-order: {string.Join(",", sorted)}");
var badEdit = new TreeNode(50) { Left = new(30) { Right = new(60) } };   // 60 sits left of 50
Console.WriteLine($"valid BST: {IsValid(root)}, after a bad edit: {IsValid(badEdit)}");

// Recursion depth = tree height: fine when balanced; sorted inserts make a list and overflow the stack
// (fatal in .NET) — use SortedSet<T> or an explicit stack there.
static TreeNode Insert(TreeNode? node, int value)
{
    if (node is null) return new TreeNode(value);
    if (value < node.Value) node.Left = Insert(node.Left, value);
    else if (value > node.Value) node.Right = Insert(node.Right, value);
    return node;                                         // equal: ids are unique, keep one
}

static void InOrder(TreeNode? node, List<int> into)      // left, self, right = sorted for a BST
{
    if (node is null) return;
    InOrder(node.Left, into);
    into.Add(node.Value);
    InOrder(node.Right, into);
}

// Pass the allowed range down; comparing with the parent alone misses 60 under 30 under 50.
static bool IsValid(TreeNode? node, long min = long.MinValue, long max = long.MaxValue)
{
    if (node is null) return true;
    if (node.Value <= min || node.Value >= max) return false;
    return IsValid(node.Left, min, node.Value) && IsValid(node.Right, node.Value, max);
}

sealed class TreeNode(int value)
{
    public int Value { get; } = value;
    public TreeNode? Left { get; set; }
    public TreeNode? Right { get; set; }
}

Trees: BFS level order

A queue for breadth: drain exactly one level per outer loop to print a category tree by depth, with memory bounded by the widest level.

// Show a category tree level by level (breadcrumb depth, an org chart): BFS drains one level per loop.
var root = new TreeNode("shop")
{
    Left = new("audio") { Left = new("cables"), Right = new("speakers") },
    Right = new("video") { Right = new("cameras") },
};
var levels = LevelOrder(root);
for (var depth = 0; depth < levels.Count; depth++)
    Console.WriteLine($"depth {depth}: {string.Join(", ", levels[depth])}");

static List<List<string>> LevelOrder(TreeNode? root)
{
    var levels = new List<List<string>>();
    var queue = new Queue<TreeNode>();
    if (root is not null) queue.Enqueue(root);
    while (queue.Count > 0)
    {
        var level = new List<string>();
        for (var remaining = queue.Count; remaining > 0; remaining--)   // exactly this level's nodes
        {
            var node = queue.Dequeue();
            level.Add(node.Name);
            if (node.Left is not null) queue.Enqueue(node.Left);
            if (node.Right is not null) queue.Enqueue(node.Right);
        }
        levels.Add(level);
    }
    return levels;
}
// No recursion, so depth is not limited by the stack; memory is the widest level.

sealed class TreeNode(string name)
{
    public string Name { get; } = name;
    public TreeNode? Left { get; set; }
    public TreeNode? Right { get; set; }
}

depth 1: audio, video

Graphs: BFS and DFS

Degrees of separation in a follower graph (BFS) and everyone reachable from a user (DFS) — an adjacency list, a visited set, a queue or a stack.

// A follower graph: degrees of separation (BFS), and who is reachable at all (iterative DFS). O(V + E).
var follows = new Dictionary<string, string[]>
{
    ["ana"] = ["ben", "cy"], ["ben"] = ["dee"], ["cy"] = ["dee", "eli"],
    ["dee"] = ["fay"], ["eli"] = [], ["fay"] = [], ["gus"] = ["ana"],
};
var toGus = Distance(follows, "ana", "gus")?.ToString() ?? "unreachable";
Console.WriteLine($"ana -> fay: {Distance(follows, "ana", "fay")} hops, ana -> gus: {toGus}");
Console.WriteLine($"reachable from cy: {string.Join(",", Reachable(follows, "cy").Order())}");

// Shortest path in an UNWEIGHTED graph is BFS; mark visited when enqueuing, not when dequeuing.
static int? Distance(Dictionary<string, string[]> graph, string from, string to)
{
    var distance = new Dictionary<string, int> { [from] = 0 };
    var queue = new Queue<string>([from]);
    while (queue.TryDequeue(out var node))
    {
        if (node == to) return distance[node];
        foreach (var next in graph.GetValueOrDefault(node, []))
            if (distance.TryAdd(next, distance[node] + 1)) queue.Enqueue(next);
    }
    return null;
}

// DFS with an explicit stack: no recursion depth limit on a deep graph.
static HashSet<string> Reachable(Dictionary<string, string[]> graph, string start)
{
    var visited = new HashSet<string>();
    var stack = new Stack<string>([start]);
    while (stack.TryPop(out var node))
    {
        if (!visited.Add(node)) continue;
        foreach (var next in graph.GetValueOrDefault(node, [])) stack.Push(next);
    }
    return visited;
}
// Weighted edges? Dijkstra is this BFS with a PriorityQueue keyed by distance.

Topological sort

A build order for projects with dependencies, with cycle detection for free — Kahn's algorithm, O(V + E), or O(V log V + E) with the priority queue that keeps the order stable.

// Build order for projects with dependencies (Kahn's algorithm); a cycle means no valid order. O(V + E).
(string Project, string DependsOn)[] edges = [("api", "core"), ("web", "api"), ("web", "ui"), ("ui", "core"),
                                              ("tests", "web")];
Console.WriteLine($"build order: {string.Join(" -> ", BuildOrder(edges) ?? ["cycle"])}");
var withCycle = BuildOrder([.. edges, ("core", "tests")]);
Console.WriteLine($"with a cycle: {string.Join(" -> ", withCycle ?? ["cycle"])}");

static List<string>? BuildOrder((string Project, string DependsOn)[] edges)
{
    var dependents = new Dictionary<string, List<string>>();
    var waitingOn = new Dictionary<string, int>();       // in-degree: unbuilt dependencies
    foreach (var (project, dependsOn) in edges)
    {
        waitingOn.TryAdd(dependsOn, 0);
        waitingOn[project] = waitingOn.GetValueOrDefault(project) + 1;
        if (!dependents.TryGetValue(dependsOn, out var list)) dependents[dependsOn] = list = [];
        list.Add(project);
    }

    // A priority queue instead of a queue: among the ready ones, alphabetical, so the order is stable.
    var ready = new PriorityQueue<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
    foreach (var (project, count) in waitingOn) if (count == 0) ready.Enqueue(project, project);

    var order = new List<string>();
    while (ready.TryDequeue(out var project, out _))
    {
        order.Add(project);
        foreach (var next in dependents.GetValueOrDefault(project, []))
            if (--waitingOn[next] == 0) ready.Enqueue(next, next);
    }
    return order.Count == waitingOn.Count ? order : null;   // leftovers are on a cycle or wait on one
}

build order: core -> api -> ui -> web -> tests
with a cycle: cycle

Backtracking

Every combination of gift-card denominations for an amount — choose, explore, un-choose, and prune early; zero coins are dropped first (the search would never end) and repeats too (they would repeat results).

// Which gift-card denominations add up exactly to the amount? Choose, explore, un-choose.
// Exponential in amount / smallest coin; sorting lets the loop stop at the first coin that is too big.
static List<List<int>> CombinationsSumming(int[] denominations, int amount)
{
    var coins = denominations.Where(d => d > 0).Distinct().Order().ToArray();   // 0 never shrinks the amount;
                                                                                // a repeat duplicates results
    var results = new List<List<int>>();
    var current = new List<int>();

    void Explore(int start, int remaining)
    {
        if (remaining == 0)
        {
            results.Add([.. current]);                   // copy: current keeps changing
            return;
        }
        for (var i = start; i < coins.Length && coins[i] <= remaining; i++)
        {
            current.Add(coins[i]);                       // choose
            Explore(i, remaining - coins[i]);            // explore (i, not i + 1: a card may repeat)
            current.RemoveAt(current.Count - 1);         // un-choose
        }
    }

    Explore(0, amount);
    return results;
}

var combinations = CombinationsSumming([10, 25, 5, 5, 0], 30);
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", combinations.Select(c => $"[{string.Join("+", c)}]")));

Backtracking: permutations

Every seating order for a table — the same choose, explore, un-choose skeleton with a `used[]` mask, O(n!).

// Every seating order for three guests: permutations, with a used[] mask so each guest appears once. O(n!).
static List<string> Permutations(string[] guests)
{
    var results = new List<string>();
    var used = new bool[guests.Length];
    var current = new List<string>();

    void Explore()
    {
        if (current.Count == guests.Length)
        {
            results.Add(string.Join("", current));
            return;
        }
        for (var i = 0; i < guests.Length; i++)
        {
            if (used[i]) continue;
            used[i] = true;                              // choose
            current.Add(guests[i]);
            Explore();                                   // explore
            current.RemoveAt(current.Count - 1);         // un-choose
            used[i] = false;
        }
    }

    Explore();
    return results;
}

Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", Permutations(["A", "B", "C"])));
// Subsets are the same skeleton without the mask: record current on every call, explore from i + 1.

ABC ACB BAC BCA CAB CBA

Dynamic programming

Overlapping subproblems with optimal substructure — the best non-adjacent haul, "did you mean?" edit distance, fewest coins bottom-up, where a top-down memo would recurse amount / smallest coin deep.

// 1-D: the most you can collect from houses in a row without robbing two neighbours. O(n), O(1) space.
static int Rob(int[] houses)
{
    int skip = 0, take = 0;                              // best so far without / with the last house
    foreach (var h in houses) (skip, take) = (Math.Max(skip, take), skip + h);
    return Math.Max(skip, take);
}

// 2-D: edit distance for "did you mean?". dp[i, j] = edits turning the first i of a into the first j of b.
static int EditDistance(string a, string b)
{
    var dp = new int[a.Length + 1, b.Length + 1];
    for (var i = 0; i <= a.Length; i++) dp[i, 0] = i;   // delete everything
    for (var j = 0; j <= b.Length; j++) dp[0, j] = j;   // insert everything
    for (var i = 1; i <= a.Length; i++)
        for (var j = 1; j <= b.Length; j++)
            dp[i, j] = a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]
                ? dp[i - 1, j - 1]                       // a free match
                : 1 + Math.Min(dp[i - 1, j - 1],         // replace
                               Math.Min(dp[i - 1, j],    // delete
                                        dp[i, j - 1]));  // insert
    return dp[a.Length, b.Length];
}

// Fewest coins, flattened bottom-up: best[a] = fewest coins for amount a. A top-down memo reads closer
// to the recurrence, but its recursion depth is amount / smallest coin — a stack overflow for big amounts.
static int FewestCoins(int[] coins, int amount)
{
    var best = new int[amount + 1];
    Array.Fill(best, int.MaxValue);                      // int.MaxValue: cannot be made (yet)
    best[0] = 0;
    for (var a = 1; a <= amount; a++)
        foreach (var coin in coins)
            if (coin > 0 && coin <= a && best[a - coin] != int.MaxValue)
                best[a] = Math.Min(best[a], best[a - coin] + 1);
    return best[amount];
}

Console.WriteLine($"rob: {Rob([2, 7, 9, 3, 1])}");
Console.WriteLine($"edit distance: {EditDistance("recieve", "receive")} {EditDistance("kitten", "sitting")}");
// (a swapped pair costs 2 here; Damerau-Levenshtein counts it as 1)
Console.WriteLine($"fewest coins for 63: {FewestCoins([1, 5, 10, 21, 25, 0], 63)}");

Union-Find (disjoint set)

Which servers share a cluster, and which cable is redundant — connectivity in near O(1) per operation with path compression and union by rank.

// Servers joined by network cables: how many clusters, and which cable closes a loop?
(int, int)[] cables = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (3, 4), (2, 0), (5, 6)];
var network = new UnionFind(7);
foreach (var (a, b) in cables)
    if (!network.Union(a, b)) Console.WriteLine($"cable {a}-{b} is redundant");
bool Connected(int a, int b) => network.Find(a) == network.Find(b);
Console.WriteLine($"{network.Components} clusters; 0-2 connected: {Connected(0, 2)}, 0-3: {Connected(0, 3)}");

sealed class UnionFind
{
    private readonly int[] _parent;
    private readonly int[] _rank;
    public int Components { get; private set; }

    public UnionFind(int count)
    {
        _parent = [.. Enumerable.Range(0, count)];       // everyone starts as their own root
        _rank = new int[count];
        Components = count;
    }

    public int Find(int x)
    {
        if (_parent[x] != x) _parent[x] = Find(_parent[x]);   // path compression: point straight at the root
        return _parent[x];
    }

    /// <summary>False when a and b were already connected.</summary>
    public bool Union(int a, int b)
    {
        var (ra, rb) = (Find(a), Find(b));
        if (ra == rb) return false;
        if (_rank[ra] < _rank[rb]) (ra, rb) = (rb, ra);  // union by rank: attach the shorter tree
        _parent[rb] = ra;
        if (_rank[ra] == _rank[rb]) _rank[ra]++;
        Components--;
        return true;
    }
}
// Also solves: Kruskal's minimum spanning tree, merging accounts that share an email.
