Trie (prefix tree)

Autocomplete for a search box in O(prefix length), independent of how many names the catalogue holds.

// Autocomplete for a product search box: O(length of the prefix), whatever the catalogue size.
var catalogue = new Trie();
string[] products = ["cable", "camera", "camping stove", "candle", "car charger", "tablet"];
foreach (var name in products) catalogue.Insert(name);

Console.WriteLine($"cam: {string.Join(", ", catalogue.Complete("cam"))}");
Console.WriteLine($"ca, first 3: {string.Join(", ", catalogue.Complete("ca").Take(3))}");

sealed class Trie
{
    private sealed class Node
    {
        public SortedDictionary<char, Node> Children { get; } = [];   // sorted: completions come out A-Z
        public bool IsWord { get; set; }
    }

    private readonly Node _root = new();

    public void Insert(string word)
    {
        var node = _root;
        foreach (var c in word)
        {
            if (!node.Children.TryGetValue(c, out var next)) node.Children[c] = next = new Node();
            node = next;
        }
        node.IsWord = true;
    }

    public IEnumerable<string> Complete(string prefix) =>
        Find(prefix) is { } start ? Walk(start, prefix) : [];   // lazy: Take(n) stops the walk early

    private Node? Find(string prefix)
    {
        var node = _root;
        foreach (var c in prefix)
            if (!node.Children.TryGetValue(c, out node)) return null;
        return node;
    }

    private static IEnumerable<string> Walk(Node node, string path)
    {
        if (node.IsWord) yield return path;
        foreach (var (c, child) in node.Children)
            foreach (var word in Walk(child, path + c)) yield return word;
    }
}

cam: camera, camping stove
ca, first 3: cable, camera, camping stove

Bit manipulation & cyclic sort

Find the one unpaired reading, enumerate subsets, find the first missing ticket number — O(1)-space tricks, within 32-bit (`int`) or 64-bit (`long`) masks.

using System.Numerics;

// XOR: every sensor reported twice except one; pairs cancel out. O(n) time, O(1) space.
int[] reports = [4, 1, 2, 1, 2];
Console.WriteLine($"unpaired: {reports.Aggregate(0, (acc, x) => acc ^ x)}");

// The everyday tricks, with the BCL's intrinsics where they exist (TrailingZeroCount(0) is 32).
var x = 0b1011_0100;
Console.WriteLine($"lowest bit cleared: {Convert.ToString(x & (x - 1), 2)}, lowest bit: {x & -x}");
var (ones, zeros) = (BitOperations.PopCount((uint)x), BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount(x));
Console.WriteLine($"popcount: {ones}, trailing zeros: {zeros}, pow2(64): {BitOperations.IsPow2(64)}");

// Every subset of three toppings, as a bitmask from 0 to 2^n - 1.
// int masks: n <= 30 (1 << 31 is negative, 1 << 32 is 1); 1L << i up to 62; beyond that, recurse.
string[] toppings = ["ham", "egg", "kale"];
var subsets = Enumerable.Range(0, 1 << toppings.Length)
    .Select(mask => "{" + string.Join(",", toppings.Where((_, i) => (mask & (1 << i)) != 0)) + "}");
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", subsets));

// Cyclic sort: ticket numbers should be 1..n, so put each at index value - 1; the first gap is the answer.
// O(n) time, O(1) space — and it reorders the array in place: pass a copy if the caller needs it.
static int FirstMissing(int[] tickets)
{
    for (var i = 0; i < tickets.Length;)
    {
        var target = tickets[i] - 1;
        if (target >= 0 && target < tickets.Length && tickets[target] != tickets[i])
            (tickets[i], tickets[target]) = (tickets[target], tickets[i]);
        else
            i++;
    }
    for (var i = 0; i < tickets.Length; i++)
        if (tickets[i] != i + 1) return i + 1;
    return tickets.Length + 1;
}
Console.WriteLine($"first missing ticket: {FirstMissing([3, 4, -1, 1])} {FirstMissing([1, 2, 3])}");

first missing ticket: 2 4

Working a problem out loud

The habits that matter more than the language.

  • State the brute force and its cost first, then the bottleneck the better pattern removes.
  • Name the edge cases before coding: empty input, one element, duplicates, int overflow (checked makes it throw).
  • Relying on Array.Sort keeping equal elements in order — use OrderBy when stability matters.
  • Span<T> slices without copying — the cheap way to pass a window of an array.

Streaming & Time-Series Patterns

Unbounded data, bounded memory: windows and watermarks, sketches, rate limits and backpressure — over IAsyncEnumerable, Channel<T> and Rx.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12
  • dotnet >=8
  • .NET (the base class library)

Sources: Generate and consume async streams — C# · System.Threading.Channels — .NET · What is TimeProvider? — .NET

The constraints that define the field

Every card below answers one of these.

  • You see each item once, in order, and cannot keep them all — so answers are incremental, approximate, or over a window.
  • Bounded memory is the whole game: O(1) or O(window) per stream, never O(stream).
  • Time is two things: *event time* (when it happened) and *processing time* (when you saw it). They diverge; a watermark says how late you still accept data.
  • Exact vs approximate: a sketch trades a percent of accuracy for orders of magnitude of memory. State the error bound out loud.
  • In .NET a stream is an IAsyncEnumerable<T> (pull: the consumer sets the pace), a Channel<T> (a bounded queue between producer and consumer), an IObservable<T> with System.Reactive (push, no backpressure), or a PipeReader for raw bytes.
  • Inject the clock and the randomness: a TimeProvider and a seeded Random. DateTime.UtcNow inside the algorithm makes it untestable and unreplayable.

Windowing a stream

Almost every streaming requirement is one of these windows plus a lateness policy.

WindowShapeAnswersGroup by
Tumblingfixed size, no overlap: [0, 60s), [60s, 120s)orders per minute, a billing periodt - t % size
Hoppingfixed size advancing by a smaller hop; an event falls in size / hop windowsa 5-minute error rate refreshed every 10 severy hop start in (t - size, t]
Sessionper key, closed by a gap of inactivitya user's visit, a burst of typingthe key, extended while the next event is within the gap
Count (sliding)the last n eventsthe average of the last 100 requestsposition: a ring buffer
Late eventsits window has already closed: window end ≤ watermark (highest event time − allowed lateness)what happens to a delayed uploaddrop and count, hold longer, or reopen the window and re-emit

Ring buffer — a fixed-size sliding window

A moving average of the last k request latencies: O(1) per event, O(k) memory — add the new value, subtract the evicted one.

using static System.FormattableString;

// A moving average of the last 4 request latencies (ms): O(1) per event.
var window = new RingBuffer<double>(capacity: 4);
var sum = 0.0;
foreach (var latency in new double[] { 120, 80, 100, 300, 90, 110 })
{
    if (window.Append(latency) is double evicted) sum -= evicted;   // subtract what left the window
    sum += latency;
    var average = sum / window.Count;
    Console.WriteLine(Invariant($"+{latency} ms -> avg {average:F1} over [{string.Join(", ", window)}]"));
}

sealed class RingBuffer<T>(int capacity) : IEnumerable<T> where T : struct
{
    private readonly T[] _items = new T[capacity];
    private int _head;                                   // where the next item goes
    public int Count { get; private set; }

    /// <summary>Adds an item and returns the one it evicted, if the buffer was full.</summary>
    public T? Append(T item)
    {
        T? evicted = Count == _items.Length ? _items[_head] : null;
        _items[_head] = item;
        _head = (_head + 1) % _items.Length;
        Count = Math.Min(Count + 1, _items.Length);
        return evicted;
    }

    public IEnumerator<T> GetEnumerator()
    {
        var start = (_head - Count + _items.Length) % _items.Length;   // the oldest item
        for (var i = 0; i < Count; i++) yield return _items[(start + i) % _items.Length];
    }

    System.Collections.IEnumerator System.Collections.IEnumerable.GetEnumerator() => GetEnumerator();
}
Result

+80 ms -> avg 100.0 over [120, 80]
+100 ms -> avg 100.0 over [120, 80, 100]
+300 ms -> avg 150.0 over [120, 80, 100, 300]
+90 ms -> avg 142.5 over [80, 100, 300, 90]
+110 ms -> avg 150.0 over [100, 300, 90, 110]

Tumbling windows with a watermark

Revenue per minute by event time: a window closes once the watermark passes its end, so a delayed order still counts — up to the allowed lateness.

// Revenue per minute by event time: 1-minute windows that still accept orders up to 10 s late.
var perMinute = new TumblingWindows(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1), allowedLateness: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
(int Second, int Cents)[] arrivals = [(5, 1200), (20, 800), (58, 450), (62, 2000), (50, 300), (75, 990),
                                      (130, 1500), (55, 700)];
foreach (var (second, cents) in arrivals)
    foreach (var window in perMinute.Add(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(second), cents))
        Console.WriteLine($"after {second}s: {window}");

foreach (var window in perMinute.Flush()) Console.WriteLine($"at the end: {window}");
Console.WriteLine($"late orders dropped: {perMinute.Late}");

sealed class TumblingWindows(TimeSpan size, TimeSpan allowedLateness)
{
    private readonly SortedDictionary<TimeSpan, Window> _open = [];   // window start -> totals, oldest first
    private TimeSpan _watermark = TimeSpan.MinValue;                  // highest event time - allowed lateness

    public int Late { get; private set; }

    public List<Window> Add(TimeSpan at, long cents)
    {
        var start = TimeSpan.FromTicks(at.Ticks - at.Ticks % size.Ticks);
        if (start + size <= _watermark)                  // its window is final: count it, never reopen
        {
            Late++;
            return [];
        }
        var open = _open.GetValueOrDefault(start) ?? new Window(start, size, 0, 0);
        _open[start] = open with { Orders = open.Orders + 1, Cents = open.Cents + cents };
        if (at - allowedLateness > _watermark) _watermark = at - allowedLateness;
        return Close(end => end <= _watermark);         // the windows the watermark just passed
    }

    public List<Window> Flush() => Close(_ => true);    // end of stream: everything still open is final

    private List<Window> Close(Func<TimeSpan, bool> isDue)
    {
        var closed = _open.Values.Where(w => isDue(w.Start + size)).ToList();
        foreach (var w in closed) _open.Remove(w.Start);
        return closed;
    }
}

record Window(TimeSpan Start, TimeSpan Size, int Orders, long Cents)
{
    public override string ToString() =>
        $"[{Start.TotalSeconds}s, +{Size.TotalSeconds}s) count {Orders}, ${Cents / 100}.{Cents % 100:D2}";
}

Running statistics — Welford & EMA

Mean, variance and a smoothed level in O(1) memory — enough for latency anomaly alerts without keeping a single sample.

using static System.FormattableString;

// Flag a latency as an anomaly when it is more than 2 standard deviations from the running mean.
var stats = new RunningStats();
var ema = new Ema(period: 3);
foreach (var latency in new double[] { 100, 104, 98, 101, 97, 103, 250, 99 })
{
    var z = stats.ZScore(latency);                       // against what came BEFORE this value
    var level = ema.Add(latency);
    var flag = Math.Abs(z) > 2 ? "  ANOMALY" : "";
    Console.WriteLine(Invariant($"{latency} ms: ema {level:F1}, z {z:F1}{flag}"));
    stats.Add(latency);
}

// Welford's online mean and variance: numerically stable, O(1) memory.
sealed class RunningStats
{
    private double _m2;                                  // sum of squared distances from the mean
    public long Count { get; private set; }
    public double Mean { get; private set; }

    public void Add(double x)
    {
        Count++;
        var delta = x - Mean;
        Mean += delta / Count;
        _m2 += delta * (x - Mean);                       // uses the UPDATED mean
    }

    public double Variance => Count > 1 ? _m2 / (Count - 1) : 0;
    public double StandardDeviation => Math.Sqrt(Variance);
    public double ZScore(double x) => StandardDeviation > 0 ? (x - Mean) / StandardDeviation : 0;
}

// Exponential moving average: no window and no history, one multiply per event.
sealed class Ema(int period)
{
    private readonly double _alpha = 2.0 / (period + 1);
    private double? _value;
    public double Add(double x)
    {
        _value = _value is double previous ? _alpha * x + (1 - _alpha) * previous : x;
        return _value.Value;
    }
}

Reservoir sampling

A uniform sample of k items from a stream of unknown length — which requests to trace, which log lines to upload.

using static System.FormattableString;

// Keep a uniform sample of 5 request ids from a stream of unknown length, to upload for tracing.
var sampler = new Reservoir<string>(capacity: 5, new Random(42));   // seeded: a replay picks the same ids
for (var i = 1; i <= 10_000; i++) sampler.Add($"req-{i}");
Console.WriteLine($"seen {sampler.Seen}, kept {string.Join(" ", sampler.Sample)}");

// Fairness check: over many runs, every position is kept about k/n of the time.
var keptFirst = 0;
var rng = new Random(7);
for (var run = 0; run < 20_000; run++)
{
    var r = new Reservoir<int>(capacity: 2, rng);
    for (var x = 0; x < 10; x++) r.Add(x);
    if (r.Sample.Contains(0)) keptFirst++;
}
Console.WriteLine(Invariant($"item 0 kept in {keptFirst * 100.0 / 20_000:F1}% of runs (expect 20.0%)"));

/// <summary>Algorithm R: O(k) memory, one random draw per item.</summary>
sealed class Reservoir<T>(int capacity, Random random)
{
    private readonly List<T> _sample = new(capacity);
    public long Seen { get; private set; }
    public IReadOnlyList<T> Sample => _sample;

    public void Add(T item)
    {
        Seen++;
        if (_sample.Count < capacity) { _sample.Add(item); return; }
        var j = random.NextInt64(Seen);                  // keep with probability k / n
        if (j < capacity) _sample[(int)j] = item;
    }
}

Count-Min Sketch — approximate frequencies

How often did key X appear, for any number of keys, in width × depth counters: never under, and over by more than ε·N only with probability δ.

using System.Text;

// Requests per client across 50,000 requests from ~44,000 clients, in 5 x 2,719 counters.
var sketch = new CountMinSketch(width: 2_719, depth: 5);   // width = e / 0.001 (epsilon), depth = ln(1 / 1%)
var exact = new Dictionary<string, int>();               // only to measure the error here
var random = new Random(1);
for (var i = 0; i < 50_000; i++)
{
    var client = i % 10 == 0 ? "client-hot" : $"client-{random.Next(1_000_000)}";
    sketch.Add(client);
    exact[client] = exact.GetValueOrDefault(client) + 1;
}
var errors = exact.Select(kv => sketch.Estimate(kv.Key) - kv.Value).ToList();
Console.WriteLine($"{exact.Count} distinct clients, {5 * 2_719} counters");
Console.WriteLine($"client-hot: estimate {sketch.Estimate("client-hot")}, exact {exact["client-hot"]}");
Console.WriteLine($"under-counts: {errors.Count(d => d < 0)}, max over: {errors.Max()} (bound 50)");

sealed class CountMinSketch(int width, int depth)
{
    private readonly long[,] _table = new long[depth, width];

    public void Add(string key)
    {
        var hash = StableHash(key);                      // hash once; each row derives its own column
        for (var row = 0; row < depth; row++) _table[row, Column(hash, row)]++;
    }

    // The smallest row counter: never too low; more than epsilon*N too high with probability at most delta.
    public long Estimate(string key)
    {
        var hash = StableHash(key);
        return Enumerable.Range(0, depth).Min(row => _table[row, Column(hash, row)]);
    }

    // Double hashing: h1 + row * h2 gives every row its own hash from one 64-bit value.
    private int Column(ulong hash, int row) =>
        (int)(((uint)hash + (ulong)row * ((uint)(hash >> 32) | 1)) % (ulong)width);

    // FNV-1a: string.GetHashCode() is randomized per process, so a saved or merged sketch would be garbage.
    private static ulong StableHash(string key)
    {
        var hash = 14695981039346656037UL;
        foreach (var b in Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(key)) hash = (hash ^ b) * 1099511628211UL;
        return hash;
    }
}

under-counts: 0, max over: 22 (bound 50)

Bloom filter — approximate membership

"Definitely not seen" or "probably seen" in about 10 bits per key — idempotency checks without keeping every id.

using System.Collections;
using System.Text;
using static System.FormattableString;

// "Have I already processed this webhook delivery id?" for 10,000 ids, in about 12 KB.
var seen = new BloomFilter(expectedCount: 10_000, falsePositiveRate: 0.01);
for (var i = 0; i < 10_000; i++) seen.Add($"delivery-{i}");

var missed = Enumerable.Range(0, 10_000).Count(i => !seen.MightContain($"delivery-{i}"));
var falsePositives = Enumerable.Range(10_000, 10_000).Count(i => seen.MightContain($"delivery-{i}"));
Console.WriteLine($"{seen.BitCount} bits, {seen.HashCount} hashes");
Console.WriteLine(Invariant($"false negatives: {missed}, false positives: {falsePositives / 100.0:F2}%"));

sealed class BloomFilter
{
    private readonly BitArray _bits;
    public int BitCount { get; }
    public int HashCount { get; }

    public BloomFilter(int expectedCount, double falsePositiveRate)
    {
        // m = -n ln p / (ln 2)^2 bits, k = (m / n) ln 2 hash functions
        var ln2 = Math.Log(2);
        BitCount = (int)Math.Ceiling(-expectedCount * Math.Log(falsePositiveRate) / (ln2 * ln2));
        HashCount = Math.Max(1, (int)Math.Round((double)BitCount / expectedCount * ln2));
        _bits = new BitArray(BitCount);
    }

    public void Add(string key) { foreach (var p in Positions(key)) _bits[p] = true; }

    /// <summary>false: definitely never added. true: probably added.</summary>
    public bool MightContain(string key) => Positions(key).All(p => _bits[p]);

    private IEnumerable<int> Positions(string key)
    {
        var hash = 14695981039346656037UL;               // FNV-1a: stable across processes
        foreach (var b in Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(key)) hash = (hash ^ b) * 1099511628211UL;
        var (h1, h2) = ((uint)hash, (uint)(hash >> 32) | 1);
        for (var i = 0; i < HashCount; i++) yield return (int)((h1 + (ulong)i * h2) % (ulong)BitCount);
    }
}

Heavy hitters — Misra–Gries

The top endpoints, clients or search terms over a stream, in k counters; every key above n/(k+1) is guaranteed to be kept.

// The hottest API endpoints over a stream, tracking at most 3 counters.
var hitters = new HeavyHitters<string>(capacity: 3);
string[] traffic = ["/search", "/cart", "/search", "/login", "/search", "/cart", "/img/1",
                    "/search", "/img/2", "/cart", "/search", "/img/3", "/cart", "/search"];
foreach (var path in traffic) hitters.Add(path);

foreach (var (path, count) in hitters.Top()) Console.WriteLine($"{path} >= {count}");
// /search is 6 of 14 and /cart 4 of 14: anything above n/(k+1) = 3.5 is guaranteed to survive.

/// <summary>Misra–Gries: counts are lower bounds; true count - estimate <= n / (k + 1).</summary>
sealed class HeavyHitters<TKey>(int capacity) where TKey : notnull
{
    private readonly Dictionary<TKey, long> _counters = new(capacity);

    public void Add(TKey key)
    {
        if (_counters.TryGetValue(key, out var count)) _counters[key] = count + 1;
        else if (_counters.Count < capacity) _counters[key] = 1;
        else
        {
            // No room: decrement everyone (the newcomer included, implicitly); evict the zeros.
            foreach (var k in _counters.Keys.ToList())
                if (--_counters[k] == 0) _counters.Remove(k);
        }
    }

    public IEnumerable<(TKey Key, long Count)> Top() =>
        _counters.OrderByDescending(kv => kv.Value).ThenBy(kv => kv.Key).Select(kv => (kv.Key, kv.Value));
}
Result
/search >= 4
/cart >= 2

Streaming quantiles

p50/p95/p99 latency from a bounded sample, without storing the stream; in production record a `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` `Histogram<T>` and let the exporter compute percentiles.

using static System.FormattableString;

// p50 / p95 / p99 of 100,000 request latencies from a bounded sample of 2,000.
var random = new Random(3);
var estimator = new QuantileEstimator(sampleSize: 2_000, new Random(9));
var all = new List<double>();                            // kept here only to show the error
for (var i = 0; i < 100_000; i++)
{
    var latency = 40 + 2_000 * Math.Pow(random.NextDouble(), 6);   // mostly fast, a long tail
    estimator.Add(latency);
    all.Add(latency);
}
all.Sort();
foreach (var q in new[] { 0.50, 0.95, 0.99 })
{
    var (estimate, exact) = (estimator.Quantile(q), QuantileEstimator.Interpolate(all, q));
    Console.WriteLine(Invariant($"p{q * 100:F0}: estimate {estimate,6:F0} ms, exact {exact,6:F0} ms"));
}
Console.WriteLine(Invariant($"mean: {all.Average():F0} ms -- the average hides the tail"));

sealed class QuantileEstimator(int sampleSize, Random random)
{
    private readonly List<double> _sample = new(sampleSize);
    private long _seen;

    public void Add(double x)                            // reservoir sampling keeps the sample uniform
    {
        _seen++;
        if (_sample.Count < sampleSize) { _sample.Add(x); return; }
        var j = random.NextInt64(_seen);
        if (j < sampleSize) _sample[(int)j] = x;
    }

    public double Quantile(double q) => Interpolate([.. _sample.Order()], q);

    public static double Interpolate(IReadOnlyList<double> sorted, double q)
    {
        if (sorted.Count == 0) return double.NaN;        // nothing seen yet
        var position = q * (sorted.Count - 1);
        var (lower, upper) = ((int)Math.Floor(position), (int)Math.Ceiling(position));
        return sorted[lower] + (sorted[upper] - sorted[lower]) * (position - lower);
    }
}
Result

Rate limiting — token bucket

A burst of 3, then a steady 5 per second, in O(1) memory; production code can use `TokenBucketRateLimiter` from `System.Threading.RateLimiting` (`dotnet add package System.Threading.RateLimiting`; in-box in ASP.NET Core apps).

// One client sends a request every 100 ms; the bucket allows a burst of 3, then 5 per second.
var clock = new ManualClock();
var bucket = new TokenBucket(capacity: 3, refillPerSecond: 5, clock);
var outcome = "";
for (var i = 0; i < 12; i++)
{
    outcome += bucket.TryAcquire() ? "+" : "-";
    clock.Advance(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(100));
}
Console.WriteLine($"token bucket {outcome}");

/// <summary>Bursts up to capacity, then the sustained refill rate; O(1) memory.</summary>
sealed class TokenBucket(double capacity, double refillPerSecond, TimeProvider time)
{
    // A copy of capacity: using the parameter in both an initializer and a method triggers warning CS9124.
    private readonly double _capacity = capacity;
    private double _tokens = capacity;
    private long _last = time.GetTimestamp();            // monotonic: a wall-clock jump cannot refill it
    private readonly object _gate = new();

    public bool TryAcquire()
    {
        lock (_gate)
        {
            var now = time.GetTimestamp();
            var refill = time.GetElapsedTime(_last, now).TotalSeconds * refillPerSecond;
            _tokens = Math.Min(_capacity, _tokens + refill);
            _last = now;
            if (_tokens < 1) return false;
            _tokens -= 1;
            return true;
        }
    }
}

/// <summary>A test clock: time moves only when the test says so.</summary>
sealed class ManualClock : TimeProvider
{
    private long _ticks;
    public void Advance(TimeSpan by) => _ticks += by.Ticks;
    public override long TimestampFrequency => TimeSpan.TicksPerSecond;
    public override long GetTimestamp() => _ticks;
}

Rate limiting — sliding-window log

The same requests against at most 5 in any 1-second window: exact, a hard wall after the burst instead of the bucket's smoothing, and O(limit) memory.

// The same client, a request every 100 ms, against at most 5 requests in any 1-second window.
var clock = new ManualClock();
var limiter = new SlidingWindowLog(limit: 5, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1), clock);
var outcome = "";
for (var i = 0; i < 12; i++)
{
    outcome += limiter.TryAcquire() ? "+" : "-";
    clock.Advance(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(100));
}
Console.WriteLine($"sliding window {outcome}");

/// <summary>At most limit requests in any window: an exact count, in O(limit) memory.</summary>
sealed class SlidingWindowLog(int limit, TimeSpan window, TimeProvider time)
{
    private readonly Queue<long> _accepted = new();
    private readonly object _gate = new();

    public bool TryAcquire()
    {
        lock (_gate)
        {
            var now = time.GetTimestamp();
            while (_accepted.TryPeek(out var oldest) && time.GetElapsedTime(oldest, now) >= window)
                _accepted.Dequeue();                     // evict what left the window
            if (_accepted.Count >= limit) return false;
            _accepted.Enqueue(now);
            return true;
        }
    }
}

/// <summary>A test clock: time moves only when the test says so.</summary>
sealed class ManualClock : TimeProvider
{
    private long _ticks;
    public void Advance(TimeSpan by) => _ticks += by.Ticks;
    public override long TimestampFrequency => TimeSpan.TicksPerSecond;
    public override long GetTimestamp() => _ticks;
}

Live debounce and sample, cancellable

Search-as-you-type on live input: System.Reactive's `Throttle` (a debounce) and `Sample` run on an injected scheduler's timers, and disposing the subscription cancels what is pending (in depth, and by hand with a `TimeProvider`: see the Timing Operators sheet).

using System.Reactive.Linq;
using Microsoft.Reactive.Testing;
using static Microsoft.Reactive.Testing.ReactiveTest;

// Live keystrokes on a virtual clock, and the source never completes — like a search box left open.
var scheduler = new TestScheduler();
var ms = TimeSpan.TicksPerMillisecond;
var keystrokes = scheduler.CreateHotObservable(
    OnNext(0 * ms, "c"), OnNext(90 * ms, "ca"), OnNext(170 * ms, "cab"),
    OnNext(600 * ms, "cabl"), OnNext(680 * ms, "cable"), OnNext(1_300 * ms, "cable u"));

// Rx.NET's Throttle is a DEBOUNCE: a timer fires once the input has been quiet for 300 ms.
var searched = new List<string>();
var search = keystrokes
    .Throttle(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(300), scheduler)   // in an app: .ObserveOn the UI thread after this
    .Subscribe(query => searched.Add($"{scheduler.Clock / ms}:{query}"));

// Sample: the latest value on every 500 ms tick, if one arrived since the last tick (a live chart).
var sampled = new List<string>();
using var chart = keystrokes
    .Sample(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500), scheduler)
    .Subscribe(value => sampled.Add($"{scheduler.Clock / ms}:{value}"));

scheduler.AdvanceTo(1_400 * ms);
search.Dispose();                                    // the page closes: the pending "cable u" never runs
scheduler.AdvanceTo(5_000 * ms);
Console.WriteLine($"debounce 300 | {string.Join("  ", searched)}");
Console.WriteLine($"sample   500 | {string.Join("  ", sampled)}");

sample   500 | 500:cab  1000:cable  1500:cable u

Debounce & throttle over recorded events

Over recorded, timestamped events (replayed logs, tests), where each operator decides on event time only as the next event arrives — for live input see the live debounce card.

// Recorded keystrokes, event time in ms. Debounce keeps the LAST of a burst, throttle the FIRST.
Timed<string>[] typed = [new(0, "c"), new(90, "ca"), new(170, "cab"),
                         new(600, "cabl"), new(680, "cable"), new(1300, "cable u")];
Console.WriteLine($"debounce 300 | {await Show(Debounce(Replay(typed), quietMs: 300))}");
Console.WriteLine($"throttle 500 | {await Show(Throttle(Replay(typed), intervalMs: 500))}");

static async IAsyncEnumerable<Timed<T>> Debounce<T>(IAsyncEnumerable<Timed<T>> source, long quietMs)
{
    Timed<T>? pending = null;
    await foreach (var e in source)
    {
        if (pending is not null && e.AtMs - pending.AtMs >= quietMs) yield return pending;
        pending = e;
    }
    if (pending is not null) yield return pending;       // the recording ended: nothing newer can come
}

static async IAsyncEnumerable<Timed<T>> Throttle<T>(IAsyncEnumerable<Timed<T>> source, long intervalMs)
{
    var openAt = long.MinValue;
    await foreach (var e in source)
    {
        if (e.AtMs < openAt) continue;
        yield return e;
        openAt = e.AtMs + intervalMs;
    }
}

static async IAsyncEnumerable<T> Replay<T>(IEnumerable<T> items)
{
    foreach (var item in items)
    {
        await Task.Yield();
        yield return item;
    }
}

static async Task<string> Show(IAsyncEnumerable<Timed<string>> events)
{
    var shown = new List<string>();
    await foreach (var e in events) shown.Add($"{e.AtMs}:{e.Value}");
    return string.Join("  ", shown);
}

record Timed<T>(long AtMs, T Value);

Backpressure & buffering policy

When production outruns consumption you choose what to lose: a bounded `Channel<T>` states it with `BoundedChannelFullMode`.

using System.Threading.Channels;

// A sensor produces 10 readings before the uploader reads any: each policy keeps different ones.
BoundedChannelFullMode[] lossy = [BoundedChannelFullMode.DropOldest, BoundedChannelFullMode.DropNewest,
                                  BoundedChannelFullMode.DropWrite];
foreach (var mode in lossy)
{
    var dropped = new List<int>();
    var channel = Channel.CreateBounded<int>(new BoundedChannelOptions(3) { FullMode = mode }, dropped.Add);
    for (var reading = 1; reading <= 10; reading++) channel.Writer.TryWrite(reading);
    channel.Writer.Complete();
    var kept = new List<int>();
    await foreach (var reading in channel.Reader.ReadAllAsync()) kept.Add(reading);
    Console.WriteLine($"{mode,-10} kept [{string.Join(",", kept)}] dropped {dropped.Count}");
}

// Wait (the default) is real backpressure: the producer's write does not complete until there is room.
var orders = Channel.CreateBounded<string>(new BoundedChannelOptions(1) { SingleReader = true });
await orders.Writer.WriteAsync("order-1");
var second = orders.Writer.WriteAsync("order-2").AsTask();
Console.WriteLine($"second write completed while full: {second.IsCompleted}");
Console.WriteLine($"consumer took {await orders.Reader.ReadAsync()}");
await second;                                            // now there was room
Console.WriteLine($"second write completed after a read: {second.IsCompleted}, queued {orders.Reader.Count}");
Result

DropNewest kept [1,2,10] dropped 7
DropWrite  kept [1,2,3] dropped 7
second write completed while full: False
consumer took order-1
second write completed after a read: True, queued 1

Batching, chunking and coalescing

Amortise per-item cost over recorded events; live, System.Reactive's `Buffer(TimeSpan, int)` flushes on a timer, but its windows start at subscription and it emits empty lists, so add `.Where(b => b.Count > 0)`.

// Telemetry upload over a recorded stream: a batch at 3 events, or once the oldest pending event is
// 1 s old (replay: the age rule is checked when the next event arrives, so a quiet stream waits).
Timed<string>[] events = [new(0, "open"), new(100, "scroll"), new(150, "tap"), new(300, "tap"),
                          new(1_500, "scroll"), new(1_600, "close")];
await foreach (var batch in Batch(Replay(events), maxSize: 3, maxAgeMs: 1_000))
    Console.WriteLine($"upload [{string.Join(", ", batch.Select(e => $"{e.AtMs}:{e.Value}"))}]");

// Coalescing: only the latest quantity per product needs saving; 5 edits become 2 writes.
(string Sku, int Quantity)[] edits = [("mug", 1), ("tee", 2), ("mug", 2), ("mug", 3), ("tee", 1)];
var latest = new Dictionary<string, int>();
foreach (var (sku, quantity) in edits) latest[sku] = quantity;
var saves = latest.OrderBy(kv => kv.Key).Select(kv => $"{kv.Key}={kv.Value}");
Console.WriteLine($"save {string.Join(", ", saves)}");

// In memory, fixed-size batches are built in: orders.Chunk(100).

static async IAsyncEnumerable<List<Timed<T>>> Batch<T>(
    IAsyncEnumerable<Timed<T>> source, int maxSize, long maxAgeMs)
{
    var buffer = new List<Timed<T>>(maxSize);
    await foreach (var e in source)
    {
        if (buffer.Count > 0 && e.AtMs - buffer[0].AtMs >= maxAgeMs)   // too old to keep waiting
        {
            yield return buffer;
            buffer = new(maxSize);
        }
        buffer.Add(e);
        if (buffer.Count < maxSize) continue;
        yield return buffer;                             // full
        buffer = new(maxSize);
    }
    if (buffer.Count > 0) yield return buffer;           // flush the tail
}

static async IAsyncEnumerable<T> Replay<T>(IEnumerable<T> items)
{
    foreach (var item in items)
    {
        await Task.Yield();
        yield return item;
    }
}

record Timed<T>(long AtMs, T Value);

Deduplication with a TTL

Webhooks and queues deliver at least once, so the consumer forgets ids after a TTL in bounded memory — past `capacity` ids per TTL the oldest are forgotten early and their redeliveries processed again, so size it to peak rate × TTL.

// A webhook provider retries deliveries: process each id once within 10 minutes, in bounded memory.
var recent = new RecentSet<string>(ttl: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10), capacity: 10_000);
var start = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 11, 16, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
(int Minute, string Id)[] deliveries = [(0, "evt-1"), (1, "evt-2"), (2, "evt-1"),
                                       (9, "evt-2"), (13, "evt-1"), (14, "evt-2")];
foreach (var (minute, id) in deliveries)
{
    var isNew = recent.TryAdd(id, start.AddMinutes(minute));
    Console.WriteLine($"+{minute,2} min {id}: {(isNew ? "process" : "duplicate, skip")}");
}

// Full at capacity 2: a repeat of the oldest id is still a duplicate; only a new id evicts the oldest.
var small = new RecentSet<string>(ttl: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10), capacity: 2);
foreach (var (second, id) in new[] { (0, "a"), (1, "b"), (2, "a"), (3, "c"), (4, "a") })
{
    var isNew = small.TryAdd(id, start.AddSeconds(second));
    Console.WriteLine($"capacity 2, +{second}s {id}: {(isNew ? "process" : "duplicate, skip")}");
}

/// <summary>Remembers keys for a time-to-live, evicting oldest first; O(1) amortised per key.</summary>
sealed class RecentSet<TKey>(TimeSpan ttl, int capacity) where TKey : notnull
{
    private readonly Dictionary<TKey, DateTimeOffset> _seenAt = [];
    private readonly Queue<(TKey Key, DateTimeOffset At)> _order = new();

    /// <summary>True the first time a key is seen inside the window.</summary>
    public bool TryAdd(TKey key, DateTimeOffset now)
    {
        while (_order.TryPeek(out var oldest) && now - oldest.At >= ttl) Forget();   // expired ids first
        if (_seenAt.ContainsKey(key)) return false;      // a redelivery inside the window
        if (_order.Count >= capacity) Forget();          // full: drop the oldest early (size: rate x TTL)
        _seenAt[key] = now;
        _order.Enqueue((key, now));
        return true;
    }

    private void Forget() => _seenAt.Remove(_order.Dequeue().Key);   // a key is queued once while it is seen
}

Merging ordered streams & change detection

A k-way merge with `PriorityQueue` keeps event-time order across sources (ties by source, so a replay is reproducible); hysteresis turns a noisy signal into clean transitions.

// Merge three servers' logs, each already sorted by time, into one ordered stream: O(n log k).
(int AtMs, string Line)[][] logs =
[
    [(10, "api: GET /cart"), (40, "api: POST /pay"), (90, "api: GET /done")],
    [(20, "db: SELECT cart"), (40, "db: INSERT payment")],
    [(41, "pay: charge ok")],
];
foreach (var (at, line) in MergeSorted(logs)) Console.WriteLine($"{at}ms {line}");

// Change detection with hysteresis: alert above 80% CPU, clear only below 60%, so 79-81 noise cannot flap.
var alarm = new Hysteresis(enter: 80, exit: 60);
foreach (var cpu in new[] { 50, 79, 81, 79, 82, 70, 59, 61, 85 })
    if (alarm.Update(cpu) is bool on) Console.WriteLine($"cpu {cpu}% -> alert {(on ? "raised" : "cleared")}");

// Over live sources: take IEnumerator<T>s and dispose them all in finally (MergeRuns on the Files sheet).
static IEnumerable<(int AtMs, string Line)> MergeSorted((int AtMs, string Line)[][] sources)
{
    // Priority (time, source): equal timestamps come out in source order, so a replay is reproducible.
    var heads = new PriorityQueue<(int Source, int Index), (int AtMs, int Source)>();
    for (var s = 0; s < sources.Length; s++)
        if (sources[s].Length > 0) heads.Enqueue((s, 0), (sources[s][0].AtMs, s));
    while (heads.TryDequeue(out var head, out _))
    {
        var source = sources[head.Source];
        yield return source[head.Index];                 // always the global minimum
        var next = head.Index + 1;
        if (next < source.Length) heads.Enqueue((head.Source, next), (source[next].AtMs, head.Source));
    }
}

sealed class Hysteresis(double enter, double exit)
{
    public bool IsOn { get; private set; }

    /// <summary>The new state on a transition; null when nothing changed.</summary>
    public bool? Update(double value)
    {
        if (!IsOn && value > enter) return IsOn = true;
        if (IsOn && value < exit) return IsOn = false;
        return null;
    }
}

Streaming pitfalls

The mistakes that only show up under production load.

  • Unbounded buffers: Channel.CreateUnbounded, a ConcurrentQueue or Rx's Buffer on a hot source grow until the process dies. Bound them and state the full mode.
  • Recomputing the whole window per event (O(n·k) instead of O(n)) — slide it: add the new value, subtract the evicted one.
  • Using processing time when the business asks about event time. Network and device delays reorder everything.
  • Assuming exactly-once delivery. Design for at-least-once and make the consumer idempotent.
  • Summing squares for variance — it loses precision. Use Welford.
  • Hashing with string.GetHashCode() for anything saved, shared or merged: it is randomized per process. Use a stable hash (FNV-1a, or XxHash64 from the System.IO.Hashing package).
  • Blocking the producer to do per-event work. Hand off to a bounded Channel<T> and batch on the consumer side.
  • A seeded Random replays the same sequence on one runtime, but the algorithm may change between .NET versions: persist the sample, not the seed.
  • Decide the lateness policy explicitly: drop, hold until a watermark, or re-open the window and re-emit.
  • Instrument the stream itself: input rate, drop count (the itemDropped callback), queue depth (ChannelReader.Count), end-to-end lag.

Design for testability — inject TimeProvider

Code that asks a `TimeProvider` for the time can be tested without sleeping.

var clock = new ManualClock(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
var session = new Session(clock, TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30));
Console.WriteLine(session.Expired);
clock.Advance(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30));       // the test owns time
Console.WriteLine(session.Expired);

class Session(TimeProvider time, TimeSpan ttl)
{
    private readonly DateTimeOffset started = time.GetUtcNow();
    public bool Expired => time.GetUtcNow() - started >= ttl;
}

// FakeTimeProvider (Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing) does this, plus timers
class ManualClock(DateTimeOffset start) : TimeProvider
{
    private DateTimeOffset now = start;
    public override DateTimeOffset GetUtcNow() => now;
    public void Advance(TimeSpan by) => now += by;
}

An xUnit test class

`[Theory]` runs once per `[InlineData]` row; `Assert.Throws` checks the exception type exactly.

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using Xunit;

public static class Slug
{
    public static string From(string title)
    {
        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(title);
        return Regex.Replace(title.Trim().ToLowerInvariant(), "[^a-z0-9]+", "-").Trim('-');
    }
}

public class SlugTests
{
    [Theory]
    [InlineData("  Hello, World!  ", "hello-world")]
    [InlineData("--x--", "x")]
    public void JoinsWordsWithSingleHyphens(string title, string expected) =>
        Assert.Equal(expected, Slug.From(title));

    [Fact]
    public void RejectsBlankTitles() => Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => Slug.From("   "));
}

Test doubles — which one when

Prefer state over interaction — a fake you can read back survives refactoring — and verify calls only when the call itself is the behaviour.

DoubleWhat it isReach for it whenIn .NET
fakea working, simplified implementationthe default for repositories, clocks, caches, queuesa class over a Dictionary; the ManualClock above; FakeTimeProvider
stubreturns canned answers, records nothingforcing a branch: a declined card, a 503, an empty pagea lambda, a tiny class, or an HttpMessageHandler returning a fixed response
spya stub that also records how it was calledan outgoing side effect is the behaviour: one receipt e-mail, one audit entrya lambda or a class adding each call to a List
mockexpectations a framework verifiesa hand-written double would be large, and the interaction is what mattersMoq: mock.Verify(r => r.SendAsync("ada@example.com", "A-1042"), Times.Once()); NSubstitute: await receipts.Received(1).SendAsync("ada@example.com", "A-1042")
dummypassed to satisfy a signature, never useda constructor needs a logger the test ignoresNullLogger<T>.Instance

A fake, a stub and a spy — written by hand

Put each seam in the constructor, and the doubles are a few lines each, need no framework, and fail with a readable message.

foreach (var (approved, order) in new[]
{
    (true, new Order("A-1042", "ada@example.com", 25.50m)),
    (false, new Order("A-1043", "grace@example.com", 9.99m)),
})
{
    var orders = new InMemoryOrders();                                 // fake: works, but in memory

    Func<string, decimal, Task<bool>> charge = (_, _) => Task.FromResult(approved);   // stub: canned answer

    // spy: records each call so the test can check what went out, and for which order
    var sent = new List<(string Email, string Order)>();
    Func<string, string, Task> sendReceipt = (email, number) =>
    {
        sent.Add((email, number));
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    };

    await new Checkout(orders, charge, sendReceipt).PlaceAsync(order);
    var saved = orders.ByNumber[order.Number];
    Console.WriteLine($"{order.Number}: paid={saved.Paid} | sent: [{string.Join(", ", sent)}]");
}

record Order(string Number, string Email, decimal Total, bool Paid = false);

interface IOrderRepository { Task SaveAsync(Order order); }

sealed class Checkout(
    IOrderRepository orders, Func<string, decimal, Task<bool>> charge, Func<string, string, Task> sendReceipt)
{
    public async Task PlaceAsync(Order order)
    {
        var paid = await charge(order.Number, order.Total);
        await orders.SaveAsync(order with { Paid = paid });
        if (paid) await sendReceipt(order.Email, order.Number);
    }
}

sealed class InMemoryOrders : IOrderRepository
{
    public Dictionary<string, Order> ByNumber { get; } = new(StringComparer.Ordinal);    // read by the test

    public Task SaveAsync(Order order)
    {
        ByNumber[order.Number] = order;
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}
Result
A-1042: paid=True | sent: [(ada@example.com, A-1042)]
A-1043: paid=False | sent: []

Async tests and controlled time — FakeTimeProvider

Advance `FakeTimeProvider` in steps smaller than the interval you are testing, because `Advance` jumps the clock first and then fires what is due, which hides a wrong interval.

using Microsoft.Extensions.Time.Testing;

var start = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 3, 8, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
foreach (var (settlesOnPoll, timeoutSeconds) in new[] { (3, 30), (int.MaxValue, 12) })
{
    var time = new FakeTimeProvider(start);
    var polls = new List<string>();
    var poller = new PaymentPoller(time, _ =>
    {
        polls.Add(FormattableString.Invariant($"{(time.GetUtcNow() - start).TotalSeconds}s"));
        return Task.FromResult(polls.Count >= settlesOnPoll ? "paid" : "pending");
    });

    var waiting = poller.WaitUntilSettledAsync(
        every: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), timeout: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(timeoutSeconds));
    Console.Write($"done before time moves: {waiting.IsCompleted}; ");

    // one second at a time, smaller than the 5 s interval: Advance moves the clock first, then fires
    // what is due, so only a step shorter than the interval shows when each poll really happened.
    // The poller's continuations run inside Advance here; code using ConfigureAwait(false) under a
    // test framework's context must reach its next Task.Delay before each step
    for (var second = 0; second < 60; second++) time.Advance(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1));

    // a broken poller fails here after 5 real seconds instead of hanging the run
    var outcome = await waiting.WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
    Console.WriteLine($"{outcome} after polls at {string.Join(", ", polls)}");
}

sealed class PaymentPoller(TimeProvider time, Func<CancellationToken, Task<string>> getStatus)
{
    public async Task<string> WaitUntilSettledAsync(TimeSpan every, TimeSpan timeout)
    {
        // the deadline's timer, like Task.Delay's, comes from the injected clock (.NET 8)
        using var deadline = new CancellationTokenSource(timeout, time);
        try
        {
            string status;
            while ((status = await getStatus(deadline.Token)) == "pending")
                await Task.Delay(every, time, deadline.Token);
            return status;
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException) when (deadline.IsCancellationRequested) { return "timed out"; }
    }
}
Result
done before time moves: False; paid after polls at 0s, 5s, 10s
done before time moves: False; timed out after polls at 0s, 5s, 10s

The same as xUnit v3 tests — an async theory that runs as a program

An xUnit v3 test project is an executable, so `dotnet run` (or the built `.dll`) runs the tests and its exit code says whether they passed.

using Microsoft.Extensions.Time.Testing;
using Xunit;

public class PaymentPollerTests
{
    [Theory]
    [InlineData(3, 30, "paid")]
    [InlineData(int.MaxValue, 12, "timed out")]
    public async Task Polls_until_settled_or_timed_out(int settlesOnPoll, int timeoutSeconds, string outcome)
    {
        var time = new FakeTimeProvider();
        var polls = new List<TimeSpan>();
        var poller = new PaymentPoller(time, _ =>
        {
            polls.Add(time.GetUtcNow() - time.Start);
            return Task.FromResult(polls.Count >= settlesOnPoll ? "paid" : "pending");
        });

        var run = poller.WaitUntilSettledAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), TimeSpan.FromSeconds(timeoutSeconds));
        Assert.False(run.IsCompleted);
        for (var second = 0; second < 60; second++) time.Advance(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1));   // < the interval

        var actual = await run.WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), TestContext.Current.CancellationToken);
        Assert.Equal(outcome, actual);
        Assert.Equal([0.0, 5.0, 10.0], polls.Select(at => at.TotalSeconds));      // every 5 s from the start
    }
}

// the class under test, as in the card above
sealed class PaymentPoller(TimeProvider time, Func<CancellationToken, Task<string>> getStatus)
{
    public async Task<string> WaitUntilSettledAsync(TimeSpan every, TimeSpan timeout)
    {
        using var deadline = new CancellationTokenSource(timeout, time);
        try
        {
            string status;
            while ((status = await getStatus(deadline.Token)) == "pending")
                await Task.Delay(every, time, deadline.Token);
            return status;
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException) when (deadline.IsCancellationRequested) { return "timed out"; }
    }
}
Result

The runner reports Total: 2, Errors: 0, Failed: 0 and the process exits with code 0. Changing an expected outcome, halving the poll interval (polls at 0, 3, 6 s) or dropping the deadline's token from Task.Delay makes it exit with code 1.

An integration test across a real HTTP boundary

Start a server on `127.0.0.1` port `0` inside the test, so the real `HttpClient` exercises sockets, status codes, URL escaping and JSON decoding with no network and nothing left running.

using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Json;
using System.Net.Sockets;
using System.Text;

using var listener = new TcpListener(IPAddress.Loopback, 0);      // a real socket; port 0 = any free port
listener.Start();
var server = ServeAsync(listener, requests: 2).WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));   // never hang the run

using var http = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new($"http://{listener.LocalEndpoint}/") };
http.Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);                                   // nor hang on a silent server

var order = await FindAsync(http, "A-1042");
Console.WriteLine(FormattableString.Invariant($"{order?.Number} {order?.Total}"));
Console.WriteLine(await FindAsync(http, "A/9999") is null ? "404 → null" : "unexpected order");
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" | ", await server));     // what crossed the wire: "/" arrives escaped

static async Task<Order?> FindAsync(HttpClient http, string number)
{
    using var response = await http.GetAsync($"orders/{Uri.EscapeDataString(number)}");
    if (response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.NotFound) return null;
    response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
    return await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<Order>();
}

static async Task<List<string>> ServeAsync(TcpListener listener, int requests)   // a minimal HTTP/1.1 server
{
    var seen = new List<string>();
    while (seen.Count < requests)
    {
        using var connection = await listener.AcceptTcpClientAsync();
        using var reader = new StreamReader(connection.GetStream(), Encoding.ASCII);
        var requestLine = await reader.ReadLineAsync() ?? "";
        while (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(await reader.ReadLineAsync())) { }        // skip the headers
        seen.Add(requestLine);

        var found = requestLine.StartsWith("GET /orders/A-1042 ", StringComparison.Ordinal);
        var body = found ? """{"number":"A-1042","total":25.50}""" : "";
        var reply = $"HTTP/1.1 {(found ? "200 OK" : "404 Not Found")}\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n"
            + "Connection: close\r\n"
            + FormattableString.Invariant($"Content-Length: {body.Length}\r\n\r\n{body}");   // protocol text
        await connection.GetStream().WriteAsync(Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(reply));
    }
    return seen;
}

record Order(string Number, decimal Total);
Result
A-1042 25.50
404 → null
GET /orders/A-1042 HTTP/1.1 | GET /orders/A%2F9999 HTTP/1.1

ASP.NET Core in memory — TestServer, and WebApplicationFactory in a test project

Host the real pipeline (routing, binding, serialization) on an in-memory `TestServer` and replace only the outermost dependency — in a test project, `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` with `ConfigureTestServices` does the same for your existing app, as in `isolate-network-and-state` on the UI & End-to-End Testing sheet.

using System.Net.Http.Json;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;

// the app's real pipeline (routing, binding, JSON) hosted in memory: no port, no network
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder();
builder.WebHost.UseTestServer();
builder.Logging.ClearProviders();                         // keep the host's logs off the test output
// only the outermost dependency is replaced; WebApplicationFactory<Program> does the same in a test project
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IOrderRepository>(new InMemoryOrders([new("A-1042", 25.50m)]));

await using var app = builder.Build();
app.MapGet("/orders/{number}", (string number, IOrderRepository orders) =>
    orders.Find(number) is { } order ? Results.Ok(order) : Results.NotFound());
await app.StartAsync();

using var client = app.GetTestClient();
var order = await client.GetFromJsonAsync<Order>("/orders/A-1042");
var missing = await client.GetAsync("/orders/A-9999");
Console.WriteLine(FormattableString.Invariant($"{order?.Number} {order?.Total}"));
Console.WriteLine($"{(int)missing.StatusCode} {missing.StatusCode}");

record Order(string Number, decimal Total);

interface IOrderRepository { Order? Find(string number); }

sealed class InMemoryOrders(IEnumerable<Order> seed) : IOrderRepository
{
    private readonly Dictionary<string, Order> byNumber =
        seed.ToDictionary(order => order.Number, StringComparer.Ordinal);

    public Order? Find(string number) => byNumber.GetValueOrDefault(number);
}
Result
A-1042 25.50
404 NotFound

Principles worth stating

The same in every language.

  • Fakes you own (an in-memory repository, a TimeProvider) over mocks of code you do not.
  • Pass CancellationToken and TimeProvider in — both make async tests deterministic.
  • Thread.Sleep / Task.Delay in tests, and tests that share static state.
  • ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace (.NET 8) is the one-line guard clause.

Clean Code in C#

Names that follow the .NET guidelines, small methods, option records over flags, XML docs, exceptions versus Try and result types, guard clauses, strongly typed ids and clean tests — each before/after proved to behave the same.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12
  • dotnet >=8
  • .NET (any app model; the examples are console apps)

Sources: Naming guidelines — Framework design guidelines · C# identifier naming rules and conventions · Best practices for exceptions — .NET · Unit testing best practices — .NET

Uncle Bob rule → C# idiom

The classic rules still hold; the compiler and the BCL already enforce or encode most of them.

Clean Code ruleThe C# way to satisfy it
Avoid null<Nullable>enable</Nullable>; ? only where absence is real; ??, ?., is not null; return [], never a null list
Don't return error codesexceptions for the exceptional; the TryX(…, out T) pattern when failing is ordinary; a small result record when the caller needs the reason
Prefer polymorphism to switchan interface or virtual method when the set of kinds is open; a switch expression over a closed record hierarchy when it is not
Encapsulate conditionalsa named property or method: order.IsRefundable
Avoid output argumentsreturn a value, a record or a tuple; out only for the Try-pattern
No flag argumentsan enum, named arguments, or an options record with defaults
Avoid primitive obsessionreadonly record struct OrderId, created by one parser at the boundary
Validate argumentsArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(x), ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(s), ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfNegative(n)
Separate construction from useconstructor injection; the composition root (Program.cs) registers the services
Comments explain why/// XML docs on public API (IntelliSense shows them); // why beside surprising code; never // what

Naming

Follow the .NET guidelines — `PascalCase` types, members and constants, `camelCase` locals and parameters, `I` on interfaces, `Async` on awaitable methods, `Is`/`Has`/`Can` on booleans, no abbreviations or Hungarian prefixes.

Don't
var list1 = new List<O>
{
    new("A-1", 42.00m, 2, 3),
    new("A-2", 15.00m, 1, 12),
    new("A-3", 99.00m, 2, 45),
};

var flag = Proc(list1).Count > 0;
Console.WriteLine($"{string.Join(",", Proc(list1))} {flag}");

static List<string> Proc(List<O> a)
{
    var r = new List<string>();
    foreach (var o in a)
        if (o.s == 2 && o.d < 30) r.Add(o.i);   // 2? 30?
    return r;
}

record O(string i, decimal t, int s, int d);
Do
Order[] orders =
[
    new("A-1", 42.00m, OrderStatus.Delivered, AgeInDays: 3),
    new("A-2", 15.00m, OrderStatus.Placed, AgeInDays: 12),
    new("A-3", 99.00m, OrderStatus.Delivered, AgeInDays: 45),
];

var refundableIds = RefundPolicy.RefundableOrderIds(orders);
var hasRefundableOrders = refundableIds.Count > 0;
Console.WriteLine($"{string.Join(",", refundableIds)} {hasRefundableOrders}");

enum OrderStatus { Placed, Delivered }

record Order(string Id, decimal Total, OrderStatus Status, int AgeInDays);

static class RefundPolicy
{
    public const int RefundWindowDays = 30;        // PascalCase, not REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS

    public static IReadOnlyList<string> RefundableOrderIds(IEnumerable<Order> orders) =>
        orders.Where(order => order.Status == OrderStatus.Delivered && order.AgeInDays < RefundWindowDays)
              .Select(order => order.Id)
              .ToList();
}
Result
A-1 True

Small methods, one level of abstraction

When a method needs blank lines or comments to separate its steps, each step wants to be a method with that name.

Before
using System.Globalization;

var cart = new Cart(CustomerTier.Pro,
[
    new CartItem("mug", 12.00m, Quantity: 2, OnSale: true),
    new CartItem("lamp", 99.00m, Quantity: 1, OnSale: false),
]);
var receipt = Checkout(cart);
Console.WriteLine(string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
    $"total {receipt.Total:0.00}, tax {receipt.Tax:0.00}"));

static Receipt Checkout(Cart cart)
{
    var total = 0m;
    foreach (var item in cart.Items)
    {
        var price = item.UnitPrice;
        if (item.OnSale) price *= 0.8m;
        if (cart.Tier == CustomerTier.Pro) price *= 0.9m;
        total += price * item.Quantity;
    }
    if (total > 100m) total -= 5m;
    var tax = Math.Round(total * 0.21m, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);
    return new Receipt(total + tax, tax);
}

enum CustomerTier { Free, Pro }
record CartItem(string Sku, decimal UnitPrice, int Quantity, bool OnSale);
record Cart(CustomerTier Tier, IReadOnlyList<CartItem> Items);
record Receipt(decimal Total, decimal Tax);
After
using System.Globalization;

var cart = new Cart(CustomerTier.Pro,
[
    new CartItem("mug", 12.00m, Quantity: 2, OnSale: true),
    new CartItem("lamp", 99.00m, Quantity: 1, OnSale: false),
]);
var receipt = Pricing.Checkout(cart);
Console.WriteLine(string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
    $"total {receipt.Total:0.00}, tax {receipt.Tax:0.00}"));

static class Pricing
{
    private const decimal SaleMultiplier = 0.8m, ProMultiplier = 0.9m;
    private const decimal BulkThreshold = 100m, BulkDiscount = 5m, TaxRate = 0.21m;

    public static Receipt Checkout(Cart cart)                // reads like the spec
    {
        var subtotal = cart.Items.Sum(item => LinePrice(item, cart.Tier));
        var discounted = ApplyBulkDiscount(subtotal);
        var tax = TaxOn(discounted);
        return new Receipt(discounted + tax, tax);
    }

    private static decimal LinePrice(CartItem item, CustomerTier tier) =>
        item.UnitPrice
        * (item.OnSale ? SaleMultiplier : 1m)
        * (tier == CustomerTier.Pro ? ProMultiplier : 1m)
        * item.Quantity;

    private static decimal ApplyBulkDiscount(decimal subtotal) =>
        subtotal > BulkThreshold ? subtotal - BulkDiscount : subtotal;

    // Tax law rounds half-cents up; Math.Round alone would round 0.125 to even (0.12)
    private static decimal TaxOn(decimal amount) =>
        Math.Round(amount * TaxRate, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);
}

enum CustomerTier { Free, Pro }
record CartItem(string Sku, decimal UnitPrice, int Quantity, bool OnSale);
record Cart(CustomerTier Tier, IReadOnlyList<CartItem> Items);
record Receipt(decimal Total, decimal Tax);
Result
total 122.67, tax 21.29

Arguments: an enum and an options record over bool flags

`Describe(order, true, false)` says nothing at the call site; an enum names the choice, and an options record with `init` properties can gain settings without breaking compiled callers.

Flags
using System.Globalization;

var order = new Order("A-1", 42.50m, "shipped");
Console.WriteLine(OrderText.Describe(order, true, false));     // which bool is which?
Console.WriteLine(OrderText.Describe(order, false, true));

record Order(string Id, decimal Total, string Status);

static class OrderText
{
    public static string Describe(Order order, bool compact, bool includeTotal)
    {
        if (compact) return order.Id;
        var text = $"Order {order.Id} is {order.Status}";
        return includeTotal
            ? text + string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $" ({order.Total:0.00} EUR)")
            : text;
    }
}
Named options
using System.Globalization;

var order = new Order("A-1", 42.50m, "shipped");
Console.WriteLine(OrderText.Describe(order, new() { Style = OrderTextStyle.Compact }));
Console.WriteLine(OrderText.Describe(order, new() { IncludeTotal = true }));
// Two settings? Named optional parameters read the same: Describe(order, includeTotal: true)

record Order(string Id, decimal Total, string Status);

enum OrderTextStyle { Sentence, Compact }

// init properties, not positional parameters: a new setting does not change the constructor,
// so callers compiled against the old package keep working
sealed record DescribeOptions
{
    public OrderTextStyle Style { get; init; } = OrderTextStyle.Sentence;
    public bool IncludeTotal { get; init; }
}

static class OrderText
{
    public static string Describe(Order order, DescribeOptions options) => options switch
    {
        { Style: OrderTextStyle.Compact } => order.Id,
        { IncludeTotal: true } => $"{Sentence(order)} {Total(order)}",
        _ => Sentence(order),
    };

    private static string Sentence(Order order) => $"Order {order.Id} is {order.Status}";
    private static string Total(Order order) =>
        string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"({order.Total:0.00} EUR)");
}
Result
A-1
Order A-1 is shipped (42.50 EUR)

Comments that earn their place, and XML docs

Delete comments that repeat the code and code that is commented out; keep the one that explains a surprise, and document public API with `///`.

Noise
Console.WriteLine(Session.IsSignedIn(new ApiResponse(200, """{"user":"ada"}""")));
Console.WriteLine(Session.IsSignedIn(new ApiResponse(200, "")));
Console.WriteLine(Session.IsSignedIn(new ApiResponse(401, "")));

record ApiResponse(int Status, string Body);

static class Session
{
    // checks if signed in
    public static bool IsSignedIn(ApiResponse response)
    {
        // if the status is 200
        if (response.Status == 200)
        {
            // and the body is not empty
            return response.Body.Length > 0;
        }
        // otherwise return false
        return false;

        // old version, kept just in case
        // return response.Status == 200;
    }
}
Useful
Console.WriteLine(Session.IsSignedIn(new ApiResponse(200, """{"user":"ada"}""")));
Console.WriteLine(Session.IsSignedIn(new ApiResponse(200, "")));
Console.WriteLine(Session.IsSignedIn(new ApiResponse(401, "")));

record ApiResponse(int Status, string Body);

static class Session
{
    /// <summary>Whether a <c>GET /session</c> response means the user is still signed in.</summary>
    /// <param name="response">The session endpoint's response.</param>
    /// <returns><see langword="true"/> only for a 200 that carries a session body.</returns>
    public static bool IsSignedIn(ApiResponse response)
    {
        // The gateway answers an expired token with an empty 200 instead of a 401
        // (ticket OPS-4821), so the status code alone cannot be trusted.
        var hasSessionBody = response.Body.Length > 0;
        return response.Status == 200 && hasSessionBody;
    }
}

Exceptions, Try-pattern and result types over sentinel values

Throw for the exceptional (a bug, a missing config file); use `TryParse` when failure is ordinary; return a small result hierarchy when the caller must know why.

Sentinels
using System.Globalization;

foreach (var input in new[] { "3", "three", "250" })
{
    var quantity = ParseQuantity(input);
    if (quantity == -1) Console.WriteLine($"{input}: not a whole number");
    else if (quantity == -2) Console.WriteLine($"{input}: must be 1 to 99");
    else Console.WriteLine($"{input}: ok, {quantity}");
    // Forget one check and -1 flows into the cart total.
}

// -1 = not a number, -2 = out of range. Every caller has to remember.
static int ParseQuantity(string input)
{
    try
    {
        var n = int.Parse(input, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        return n is >= 1 and <= 99 ? n : -2;
    }
    catch (FormatException)
    {
        return -1;                     // an exception used as control flow
    }
}
Result type
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Globalization;

foreach (var input in new[] { "3", "three", "250" })
{
    var message = QuantityResult.Parse(input) switch
    {
        QuantityResult.Ok(var quantity) => $"ok, {quantity}",
        QuantityResult.NotAWholeNumber => "not a whole number",
        QuantityResult.OutOfRange(_, var min, var max) => $"must be {min} to {max}",
        _ => throw new UnreachableException(),
    };
    Console.WriteLine($"{input}: {message}");
}

abstract record QuantityResult
{
    public sealed record Ok(int Quantity) : QuantityResult;
    public sealed record NotAWholeNumber(string Input) : QuantityResult;
    public sealed record OutOfRange(int Value, int Min, int Max) : QuantityResult;

    private QuantityResult() { }                         // closed: only the three above

    public static QuantityResult Parse(string input)
    {
        if (!int.TryParse(input, NumberStyles.Integer, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var n))
            return new NotAWholeNumber(input);           // the Try-pattern: no exception thrown
        return n is >= 1 and <= 99 ? new Ok(n) : new OutOfRange(n, 1, 99);
    }
}
Result
3: ok, 3
three: not a whole number
250: must be 1 to 99

Guard clauses and early return

Throw on a caller's bug with `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull`, return early on the expected edge cases, and keep the happy path at the left margin.

Nested
var payment = new Payment("pay_1", 42.50m);
Console.WriteLine(Webhooks.Handle(new WebhookEvent("payment.succeeded", SignatureValid: true, payment)));
Console.WriteLine(Webhooks.Handle(new WebhookEvent("payment.succeeded", SignatureValid: false, payment)));
Console.WriteLine(Webhooks.Handle(new WebhookEvent("refund.created", SignatureValid: true, null)));
try { Webhooks.Handle(null!); }
catch (ArgumentNullException e) { Console.WriteLine($"bug: {e.ParamName} was null"); }

record Payment(string Id, decimal Amount);
record WebhookEvent(string Type, bool SignatureValid, Payment? Payment);

static class Webhooks
{
    public static string Handle(WebhookEvent webhookEvent)
    {
        if (webhookEvent != null)
        {
            if (webhookEvent.SignatureValid)
            {
                if (webhookEvent.Type == "payment.succeeded" && webhookEvent.Payment != null)
                {
                    return $"fulfil {webhookEvent.Payment.Id}";
                }
                else
                {
                    return $"ignored: {webhookEvent.Type}";
                }
            }
            else
            {
                return "rejected: bad signature";
            }
        }
        throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(webhookEvent));
    }
}
Flat
var payment = new Payment("pay_1", 42.50m);
Console.WriteLine(Webhooks.Handle(new WebhookEvent("payment.succeeded", SignatureValid: true, payment)));
Console.WriteLine(Webhooks.Handle(new WebhookEvent("payment.succeeded", SignatureValid: false, payment)));
Console.WriteLine(Webhooks.Handle(new WebhookEvent("refund.created", SignatureValid: true, null)));
try { Webhooks.Handle(null!); }
catch (ArgumentNullException e) { Console.WriteLine($"bug: {e.ParamName} was null"); }

record Payment(string Id, decimal Amount);
record WebhookEvent(string Type, bool SignatureValid, Payment? Payment);

static class Webhooks
{
    public static string Handle(WebhookEvent webhookEvent)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(webhookEvent);      // names the parameter for you

        if (!webhookEvent.SignatureValid) return "rejected: bad signature";
        if (webhookEvent is not { Type: "payment.succeeded", Payment: { } paid })
            return $"ignored: {webhookEvent.Type}";

        return $"fulfil {paid.Id}";
    }
}

rejected: bad signature
ignored: refund.created

Strongly typed ids over primitives

Two `string` ids are interchangeable to the compiler; a `readonly record struct` makes swapping them a compile error, with value equality and no allocation.

var order = OrderId.Parse("ord_42");
var customer = new CustomerId(7);

Console.WriteLine(Receipts.Describe(order, customer));
// Receipts.Describe(customer, order);   // error CS1503: cannot convert from 'CustomerId' to 'OrderId'
Console.WriteLine(order == OrderId.Parse("ord_42"));
Console.WriteLine(OrderId.TryParse("42", out _));
Console.WriteLine(new OrderId().IsValid);           // compiles, so validity is checked at the edges

static class Receipts
{
    public static string Describe(OrderId order, CustomerId customer) => $"receipt for {order} to {customer}";
}

readonly record struct CustomerId(int Value)
{
    public override string ToString() => $"cus_{Value}";
}

// Parse once at the boundary; everything downstream can trust the type.
readonly record struct OrderId
{
    public string Value { get; }
    private OrderId(string value) => Value = value;

    public static OrderId Parse(string raw) =>
        TryParse(raw, out var id) ? id : throw new FormatException($"'{raw}' is not an order id");

    public static bool TryParse(string? raw, out OrderId id)
    {
        if (raw is not { Length: > 4 } || !raw.StartsWith("ord_", StringComparison.Ordinal))
        {
            id = default;
            return false;
        }
        id = new OrderId(raw);
        return true;
    }

    // default(OrderId) and new OrderId() skip Parse: a struct always has a parameterless constructor.
    // Check IsValid where one can arrive (a default field, deserialization — which needs a JsonConverter).
    public bool IsValid => Value is not null;

    public override string ToString() => Value;
}
Result
receipt for ord_42 to cus_7

A clean test: arrange, act, assert

Name the behaviour, build inputs with a factory and inject a `FakeTimeProvider`, so the test is fast, independent and repeatable.

using Microsoft.Extensions.Time.Testing;
using Xunit;

namespace Shop.Tests;

// Production code, shown for context
public enum RefundDecision { Eligible, NotDelivered, WindowClosed }

public sealed record Order(string Id, DateTimeOffset? DeliveredAt);

public sealed class RefundPolicy(TimeProvider clock)
{
    public RefundDecision Check(Order order) => order.DeliveredAt switch
    {
        null => RefundDecision.NotDelivered,
        DateTimeOffset at when clock.GetUtcNow() - at <= TimeSpan.FromDays(30) => RefundDecision.Eligible,
        _ => RefundDecision.WindowClosed,
    };
}

public class RefundPolicyTests
{
    private static readonly DateTimeOffset Now = new(2026, 11, 16, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
    private readonly RefundPolicy policy = new(new FakeTimeProvider(Now));   // xUnit: a new instance per test

    private static Order DeliveredDaysAgo(int days) => new("ord_1", Now.AddDays(-days));

    [Fact]
    public void Rejects_an_order_delivered_more_than_30_days_ago()
    {
        var order = DeliveredDaysAgo(31);                      // Arrange

        var decision = policy.Check(order);                    // Act

        Assert.Equal(RefundDecision.WindowClosed, decision);   // Assert
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData(0)]
    [InlineData(30)]
    public void Accepts_an_order_inside_the_window(int days) =>
        Assert.Equal(RefundDecision.Eligible, policy.Check(DeliveredDaysAgo(days)));
}
Result

dotnet test reports three passing tests (one fact, two theory cases) and exits with status 0.

Smell checklist, and F.I.R.S.T. tests

Name the smell out loud in review; it turns a taste argument into a shared vocabulary.

  • Long method / god class — many reasons to change and no honest name; a partial class or a #region hides it, it does not fix it.
  • Deep nesting — invert the condition, return early, and let a switch expression replace the if/else ladder.
  • Duplicated logic — the third copy is when you extract; two copies may still be a coincidence.
  • Primitive obsession — string for an id, an email or a currency; give it a readonly record struct.
  • Boolean blindness — IsLoading, HasError, IsEmpty encoding one state; use an enum or a record hierarchy.
  • Null-forgiving ! and catch (Exception) { } — each one silences the compiler or the failure instead of handling it.
  • Feature envy — a method that mostly reads another class's properties belongs on that class.
  • Temporal coupling — Initialize() must run before Start(); make the constructor or a factory return a ready object.
  • F.I.R.S.T. tests are Fast (no network, no Task.Delay), Independent (no shared mutable statics, any order), Repeatable (inject TimeProvider, ids and randomness), Self-validating (an Assert, never a log to eyeball) and Timely (written with the change).
  • The boy scout rule — leave the file cleaner than you found it, in small commits that keep the tests green.

SOLID in C#

The five principles as before/after refactors in C#'s own idiom — interfaces and constructor injection, polymorphism versus pattern matching, variance, role interfaces and the DI container as composition root — each pair proved to print the same.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12
  • dotnet >=8
  • .NET (any app model; the examples are console apps)

Sources: Architectural principles — .NET application architecture guide · Dependency injection — .NET · Covariance and contravariance in generics — .NET

The one-line versions

Say the name, then the smell it prevents.

  • Single Responsibility — a class has one reason to change. Smell: one service that parses, calculates, formats and sends.
  • Open/Closed — add behaviour by adding a class, not by editing a shipped switch. Smell: every promotion touches the same method.
  • Liskov Substitution — anything typed as the base keeps the base's promises. Smell: is SubType checks in the caller, or an override that throws NotSupportedException.
  • Interface Segregation — depend on the narrowest interface you use. Smell: test fakes full of throw new NotImplementedException().
  • Dependency Inversion — logic depends on an interface it owns; the composition root passes the implementation in. Smell: new SmtpClient(), DateTime.Now or a static singleton inside business code.
  • In .NET the principles meet in one place: constructor injection plus Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection — the container is where implementations are chosen, and nowhere else.

S — Single Responsibility

Split by reason to change — the file format, the business rule, the layout — so each one is a small type you can test and change alone.

Violates
using System.Globalization;
using System.Text;

string[] lines = ["A-1,ada,42.50,delivered", "A-2,grace,15.00,cancelled", "A-3,linus,15.00,delivered"];
Console.Write(new DailyReport().Build(lines));

// Parses, filters, aggregates and formats: four reasons to change, one class.
class DailyReport
{
    public string Build(IEnumerable<string> csvLines)
    {
        var (revenue, cancelled) = (0m, 0);
        var perCustomer = new SortedDictionary<string, decimal>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
        foreach (var line in csvLines)
        {
            var parts = line.Split(',');
            if (parts[3] == "cancelled")
            {
                cancelled++;
                continue;
            }
            if (parts[3] != "delivered") throw new FormatException($"bad status: {parts[3]}");
            var total = decimal.Parse(parts[2], CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
            revenue += total;
            perCustomer[parts[1]] = perCustomer.GetValueOrDefault(parts[1]) + total;
        }

        var text = new StringBuilder();
        foreach (var (customer, spent) in perCustomer)
            text.AppendLine(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"{customer}: {spent:0.00} EUR");
        text.AppendLine(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"revenue {revenue:0.00} EUR ({cancelled} cancelled)");
        return text.ToString();
    }
}
Respects
using System.Globalization;
using static System.FormattableString;

string[] lines = ["A-1,ada,42.50,delivered", "A-2,grace,15.00,cancelled", "A-3,linus,15.00,delivered"];
var orders = lines.Select(Order.Parse).ToList();
Console.WriteLine(ReportFormatter.Format(SalesSummary.Of(orders)));

enum OrderStatus { Delivered, Cancelled }

record Order(string Id, string Customer, decimal Total, OrderStatus Status)
{
    public static Order Parse(string line) =>                                // the file format
        line.Split(',') is [var id, var customer, var total, var status]
            ? new(id, customer, decimal.Parse(total, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), ParseStatus(status))
            : throw new FormatException($"bad order line: {line}");

    private static OrderStatus ParseStatus(string status) => status switch
    {
        "delivered" => OrderStatus.Delivered,
        "cancelled" => OrderStatus.Cancelled,
        _ => throw new FormatException($"bad status: {status}"),
    };
}

record SalesSummary(IReadOnlyDictionary<string, decimal> PerCustomer, decimal Revenue, int Cancelled)
{
    public static SalesSummary Of(IReadOnlyList<Order> orders)              // the business rule
    {
        var delivered = orders.Where(o => o.Status == OrderStatus.Delivered).ToList();
        var perCustomer = delivered.GroupBy(o => o.Customer)
                                   .ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.Sum(o => o.Total));
        var cancelled = orders.Count(o => o.Status == OrderStatus.Cancelled);
        return new(perCustomer, delivered.Sum(o => o.Total), cancelled);
    }
}

static class ReportFormatter                                                  // the layout
{
    public static string Format(SalesSummary summary) => string.Join(Environment.NewLine,
        summary.PerCustomer.OrderBy(p => p.Key, StringComparer.Ordinal)
            .Select(p => Invariant($"{p.Key}: {p.Value:0.00} EUR"))
            .Append(Invariant($"revenue {summary.Revenue:0.00} EUR ({summary.Cancelled} cancelled)")));
}
Result
ada: 42.50 EUR
linus: 15.00 EUR
revenue 57.50 EUR (1 cancelled)
