O — Open/Closed: polymorphism for an open set

Adding Black Friday edits the shipped `switch` on the left and only adds a class on the right; keep a `switch` expression for a set that is closed by nature, such as an order's states.

Violates
using System.Globalization;

var cart = new Cart(Subtotal: 120m, ItemCount: 3, Coupon: "WELCOME10");
string[] activePromotions = ["bulk", "coupon"];
Print(Checkout.Discount(cart, activePromotions));
Print(Checkout.Discount(cart, [.. activePromotions, "black-friday"]));      // the new promotion

static void Print(decimal amount) => Console.WriteLine(amount.ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));

record Cart(decimal Subtotal, int ItemCount, string? Coupon);

static class Checkout
{
    public static decimal Discount(Cart cart, IEnumerable<string> promotions)
    {
        var discount = 0m;
        foreach (var promotion in promotions)
        {
            discount += promotion switch
            {
                "bulk" => cart.ItemCount >= 3 ? 5m : 0m,
                "coupon" => cart.Coupon == "WELCOME10" ? cart.Subtotal * 0.10m : 0m,
                "black-friday" => cart.Subtotal * 0.20m,                     // edited shipped code
                _ => throw new ArgumentException($"unknown promotion '{promotion}'", nameof(promotions)),
            };
        }
        return discount;
    }
}
Respects
using System.Globalization;

var cart = new Cart(Subtotal: 120m, ItemCount: 3, Coupon: "WELCOME10");
IDiscountRule[] activeRules =
    [new BulkDiscount(MinItems: 3, Amount: 5m), new CouponDiscount("WELCOME10", Rate: 0.10m)];
Print(Checkout.Discount(cart, activeRules));
Print(Checkout.Discount(cart, [.. activeRules, new BlackFridayDiscount(Rate: 0.20m)]));   // new promotion

static void Print(decimal amount) => Console.WriteLine(amount.ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));

record Cart(decimal Subtotal, int ItemCount, string? Coupon);

interface IDiscountRule
{
    decimal DiscountFor(Cart cart);
}

sealed record BulkDiscount(int MinItems, decimal Amount) : IDiscountRule
{
    public decimal DiscountFor(Cart cart) => cart.ItemCount >= MinItems ? Amount : 0m;
}

sealed record CouponDiscount(string Code, decimal Rate) : IDiscountRule
{
    public decimal DiscountFor(Cart cart) => cart.Coupon == Code ? cart.Subtotal * Rate : 0m;
}

static class Checkout                                     // unchanged by the new promotion
{
    public static decimal Discount(Cart cart, IEnumerable<IDiscountRule> rules) =>
        rules.Sum(rule => rule.DiscountFor(cart));
}

// Added code only: a new class, and one more rule where the rules are chosen.
sealed record BlackFridayDiscount(decimal Rate) : IDiscountRule
{
    public decimal DiscountFor(Cart cart) => cart.Subtotal * Rate;
}

41.00

L — Liskov Substitution: keep the contract

If the caller must ask which subtype it was handed, substitution is broken; the fix keeps the base class and puts every legitimate outcome into `Refund`'s return type.

Violates
using System.Globalization;

Console.WriteLine(Refunds.RefundOrder(new CardPayment("4242"), 42.50m));
Console.WriteLine(Refunds.RefundOrder(new GiftCardPayment(), 42.50m));

abstract class PaymentMethod
{
    public abstract string Refund(decimal amount);
}

sealed class CardPayment(string last4) : PaymentMethod
{
    public override string Refund(decimal amount) =>
        string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"refunded {amount} to card ending {last4}");
}

sealed class GiftCardPayment : PaymentMethod
{
    public override string Refund(decimal amount) =>
        throw new NotSupportedException("gift cards cannot be refunded");   // breaks the base's promise
}

static class Refunds
{
    public static string RefundOrder(PaymentMethod method, decimal amount)
    {
        // The smell: the caller has to know which subtype it was given.
        if (method is GiftCardPayment)
            return string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"issued {amount} as store credit");
        return method.Refund(amount);
    }
}
Respects
using System.Globalization;

Console.WriteLine(Refunds.RefundOrder(new CardPayment("4242"), 42.50m));
Console.WriteLine(Refunds.RefundOrder(new GiftCardPayment(), 42.50m));

abstract record RefundOutcome
{
    private RefundOutcome() { }                                   // closed: only the two below
    public sealed record ToOriginalMethod(string Description) : RefundOutcome;
    public sealed record StoreCredit(decimal Amount) : RefundOutcome;
}

// The contract: every payment method answers every valid refund, and never throws for one.
abstract class PaymentMethod
{
    public abstract RefundOutcome Refund(decimal amount);
}

sealed class CardPayment(string last4) : PaymentMethod
{
    public override RefundOutcome Refund(decimal amount) => new RefundOutcome.ToOriginalMethod(
        string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"refunded {amount} to card ending {last4}"));
}

sealed class GiftCardPayment : PaymentMethod
{
    public override RefundOutcome Refund(decimal amount) => new RefundOutcome.StoreCredit(amount);
}

static class Refunds
{
    public static string RefundOrder(PaymentMethod method, decimal amount) => method.Refund(amount) switch
    {
        RefundOutcome.ToOriginalMethod(var description) => description,
        RefundOutcome.StoreCredit(var credit) =>
            string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"issued {credit} as store credit"),
        _ => throw new InvalidOperationException("unknown refund outcome"),
    };
}
Result
refunded 42.50 to card ending 4242
issued 42.50 as store credit

Liskov in the type system: variance

Generic variance (`out` produces, `in` consumes) is substitution the compiler checks; array covariance and `ICollection<T>` on arrays are the BCL's own run-time violations.

// Array covariance compiles, then fails at run time: a CardPayment[] is not really a PaymentMethod[]
PaymentMethod[] methods = new CardPayment[2];
try { methods[0] = new GiftCardPayment(); }
catch (ArrayTypeMismatchException) { Console.WriteLine("array covariance: ArrayTypeMismatchException"); }

// An array "is" an ICollection<T>, but Add breaks that interface's promise
ICollection<string> tags = new[] { "gift" };
try { tags.Add("sale"); }
catch (NotSupportedException) { Console.WriteLine("ICollection<T>.Add on an array: NotSupportedException"); }

// Generic variance is checked: IReadOnlyList<out T> only hands Ts out, Action<in T> only takes them in
IReadOnlyList<CardPayment> cards = [new CardPayment("4242"), new CardPayment("1881")];
IReadOnlyList<PaymentMethod> readable = cards;          // safe, so it compiles
// List<PaymentMethod> writable = new List<CardPayment>();   // error CS0029: List<T> is invariant
Action<PaymentMethod> audit = method => Console.WriteLine($"audit {method.Label}");
Action<CardPayment> auditCard = audit;                  // a handler of any method handles a card
foreach (var card in cards) auditCard(card);
Console.WriteLine(readable.Count);

abstract record PaymentMethod(string Label);
sealed record CardPayment(string Last4) : PaymentMethod($"card {Last4}");
sealed record GiftCardPayment() : PaymentMethod("gift card");
Result
array covariance: ArrayTypeMismatchException
ICollection<T>.Add on an array: NotSupportedException
audit card 4242
audit card 1881
2

I — Interface Segregation: small role interfaces

Split the fat repository into the roles consumers use; the real class implements several, each consumer and each fake implements one.

Violates
var printer = new LabelPrinter(new FakeOrders());
Console.WriteLine(printer.LabelFor("A-1"));
Console.WriteLine(printer.LabelFor("A-9"));

record Order(string Id, string ShipTo);

interface IOrderRepository
{
    Order? Find(string id);
    IReadOnlyList<Order> ListAll();
    void Save(Order order);
    void Delete(string id);
    string ExportCsv();
}

class LabelPrinter(IOrderRepository orders)            // uses one member, depends on five
{
    public string LabelFor(string id) =>
        orders.Find(id) is { } order ? $"ship {order.Id} to {order.ShipTo}" : $"no order {id}";
}

class FakeOrders : IOrderRepository                    // the smell: a fake full of throws
{
    public Order? Find(string id) => id == "A-1" ? new Order("A-1", "Ada, 12 Analytical St") : null;
    public IReadOnlyList<Order> ListAll() => throw new NotImplementedException();
    public void Save(Order order) => throw new NotImplementedException();
    public void Delete(string id) => throw new NotImplementedException();
    public string ExportCsv() => throw new NotImplementedException();
}
Respects
var printer = new LabelPrinter(new FakeOrders());
Console.WriteLine(printer.LabelFor("A-1"));
Console.WriteLine(printer.LabelFor("A-9"));

record Order(string Id, string ShipTo);

interface IOrderReader
{
    Order? Find(string id);
}

interface IOrderWriter
{
    void Save(Order order);
    void Delete(string id);
}

// The database-backed repository implements both roles; consumers ask for one:
// sealed class SqlOrderRepository : IOrderReader, IOrderWriter { ... }

class LabelPrinter(IOrderReader orders)
{
    public string LabelFor(string id) =>
        orders.Find(id) is { } order ? $"ship {order.Id} to {order.ShipTo}" : $"no order {id}";
}

class FakeOrders : IOrderReader
{
    public Order? Find(string id) => id == "A-1" ? new Order("A-1", "Ada, 12 Analytical St") : null;
}

D — Dependency Inversion: constructor injection

The policy declares the interface it needs and receives it, with `TimeProvider` for the clock; the concrete mailer is chosen outside.

Violates
var reminders = new PaymentReminders();
var placed = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 1, 2, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
reminders.SendFor(new Order("A-1", "ada@example.com", placed, Paid: false));
reminders.SendFor(new Order("A-2", "grace@example.com", placed, Paid: true));

record Order(string Id, string Email, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, bool Paid);

class PaymentReminders
{
    private readonly SmtpMailer mailer = new();          // concrete, built inside: a test cannot replace it

    public void SendFor(Order order)
    {
        var overdue = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - order.PlacedAt > TimeSpan.FromDays(3);   // real clock
        if (!order.Paid && overdue) mailer.Send(order.Email, $"order {order.Id} is awaiting payment");
    }
}

class SmtpMailer
{
    public void Send(string to, string body) => Console.WriteLine($"to {to}: {body}");   // SMTP stand-in
}
Respects
var clock = new FixedClock(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 1, 10, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
var reminders = new PaymentReminders(new ConsoleMailer(), clock);   // production: SMTP, TimeProvider.System
var placed = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 1, 2, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
reminders.SendFor(new Order("A-1", "ada@example.com", placed, Paid: false));
reminders.SendFor(new Order("A-2", "grace@example.com", placed, Paid: true));

record Order(string Id, string Email, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, bool Paid);

interface IMailer                                        // owned by the policy, not by the SMTP code
{
    void Send(string to, string body);
}

sealed class PaymentReminders(IMailer mailer, TimeProvider clock)
{
    public void SendFor(Order order)
    {
        var overdue = clock.GetUtcNow() - order.PlacedAt > TimeSpan.FromDays(3);
        if (!order.Paid && overdue) mailer.Send(order.Email, $"order {order.Id} is awaiting payment");
    }
}

sealed class ConsoleMailer : IMailer
{
    public void Send(string to, string body) => Console.WriteLine($"to {to}: {body}");
}

sealed class FixedClock(DateTimeOffset now) : TimeProvider
{
    public override DateTimeOffset GetUtcNow() => now;
}
Result
to ada@example.com: order A-1 is awaiting payment

The DI container is the composition root

Register implementations once at startup; constructors only declare what they need, and the Black Friday extension from the Open/Closed card is one more registration.

using System.Globalization;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddSingleton<IMailer, ConsoleMailer>();
services.AddSingleton<IDiscountRule>(new BulkDiscount(MinItems: 3, Amount: 5m));
services.AddSingleton<IDiscountRule>(new BlackFridayDiscount(Rate: 0.20m));      // the extension
services.AddTransient<Checkout>();

// ValidateOnBuild checks that every registration's dependencies can be resolved (it creates nothing),
// so a missing one fails at startup, not on first use.
using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(new ServiceProviderOptions { ValidateOnBuild = true });
provider.GetRequiredService<Checkout>().Complete(new Cart("ada@example.com", Subtotal: 120m, ItemCount: 3));

record Cart(string Email, decimal Subtotal, int ItemCount);

interface IMailer { void Send(string to, string body); }

interface IDiscountRule { decimal DiscountFor(Cart cart); }

sealed class ConsoleMailer : IMailer
{
    public void Send(string to, string body) => Console.WriteLine($"to {to}: {body}");
}

sealed record BulkDiscount(int MinItems, decimal Amount) : IDiscountRule
{
    public decimal DiscountFor(Cart cart) => cart.ItemCount >= MinItems ? Amount : 0m;
}

sealed record BlackFridayDiscount(decimal Rate) : IDiscountRule
{
    public decimal DiscountFor(Cart cart) => cart.Subtotal * Rate;
}

// IEnumerable<IDiscountRule> receives every registration, in registration order.
sealed class Checkout(IEnumerable<IDiscountRule> rules, IMailer mailer)
{
    public void Complete(Cart cart)
    {
        var total = cart.Subtotal - rules.Sum(rule => rule.DiscountFor(cart));
        mailer.Send(cart.Email, string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"paid {total:0.00} EUR"));
    }
}
Result
to ada@example.com: paid 91.00 EUR

Composition over inheritance: decorators

Each concern wraps an interface instead of extending a class, so caching and auditing combine in any order without a subclass per combination.

Inheritance
using System.Globalization;

var catalog = new AuditedCachedPriceCatalog();
Console.WriteLine(catalog.PriceOf("mug").ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
Console.WriteLine(catalog.PriceOf("mug").ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));

class PriceCatalog
{
    public virtual decimal PriceOf(string sku)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"database lookup: {sku}");
        return sku == "mug" ? 12.00m : 99.00m;
    }
}

class CachedPriceCatalog : PriceCatalog
{
    private readonly Dictionary<string, decimal> cache = new();
    public override decimal PriceOf(string sku)
    {
        if (!cache.TryGetValue(sku, out var price)) cache[sku] = price = base.PriceOf(sku);
        return price;
    }
}

// Auditing without caching is yet another subclass: every combination is a new class.
class AuditedCachedPriceCatalog : CachedPriceCatalog
{
    public override decimal PriceOf(string sku)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"audit: {sku}");
        return base.PriceOf(sku);
    }
}
Composition
using System.Globalization;

IPriceCatalog catalog = new AuditedCatalog(new CachedCatalog(new DatabaseCatalog()));
Console.WriteLine(catalog.PriceOf("mug").ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
Console.WriteLine(catalog.PriceOf("mug").ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));

interface IPriceCatalog { decimal PriceOf(string sku); }

sealed class DatabaseCatalog : IPriceCatalog
{
    public decimal PriceOf(string sku)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"database lookup: {sku}");
        return sku == "mug" ? 12.00m : 99.00m;
    }
}

sealed class CachedCatalog(IPriceCatalog inner) : IPriceCatalog
{
    private readonly Dictionary<string, decimal> cache = new();
    public decimal PriceOf(string sku)
    {
        if (!cache.TryGetValue(sku, out var price)) cache[sku] = price = inner.PriceOf(sku);
        return price;
    }
}

// Any subset, any order: new AuditedCatalog(new DatabaseCatalog()) needs no new class.
sealed class AuditedCatalog(IPriceCatalog inner) : IPriceCatalog
{
    public decimal PriceOf(string sku)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"audit: {sku}");
        return inner.PriceOf(sku);
    }
}

database lookup: mug

Related principles an interviewer may also ask

Each one is a trade-off; say when you would break it.

  • DRY — one source of truth for each piece of knowledge; but prefer duplication over the wrong abstraction, and wait for the third copy.
  • KISS — a switch expression over a closed enum beats a plugin system nobody plugs into; a static method beats a service with no state.
  • YAGNI — do not add a generic type parameter or an interface until a second caller or a test needs it.
  • Composition over inheritance — decorators and injected collaborators; keep inheritance for framework base classes (ContentPage, ControllerBase, BackgroundService) and sealed everything else by default.
  • Law of Demeter — order.Customer.Address.Country.Code couples you to four types; ask for order.ShippingCountry or take the value as a parameter.
  • Tell, don't ask — call cart.ApplyCoupon(code) rather than reading its properties and deciding outside.
  • SOLID as ceremony — an IOrderService with exactly one implementation and no test double is indirection, not Dependency Inversion.
  • The service locator — injecting IServiceProvider and calling GetService inside logic hides the dependencies again; inject what you use.
  • Captive dependency — a singleton that takes a scoped service keeps one instance forever. ValidateScopes alone reports it only on first resolution and ValidateOnBuild alone not at all; set both to fail at startup (the generic host sets both in Development).

Functional Programming in C#

Pure functions and LINQ, Func and local functions, composition and currying, records with `with`, a hand-rolled Result, closed hierarchies with switch expressions, deferred queries, Lazy<T>, memoization and immutable collections.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12
  • dotnet >=8
  • .NET (any app model; the examples are console apps)

Sources: Pattern matching overview — C# · Language Integrated Query (LINQ) — C# · Records — C# reference · System.Collections.Immutable — .NET API

Core ideas

C# is multi-paradigm; these are the functional habits that pay off in everyday code.

  • Pure functions — same input, same output, no side effects: a static method that reads only its parameters is trivially testable and safe to call from any thread.
  • Immutability by default — record, init, readonly record struct, with and the immutable collections; mutate only local state you own.
  • Functions are values — Func<>, Action<>, lambdas, method groups and local functions.
  • Declarative over imperative — a LINQ pipeline says *what*; a loop with an accumulator says *how*.
  • Expressions over statements — switch expressions, property patterns and the ternary produce a value instead of assigning one in branches.
  • Functional core, imperative shell — pure logic in the middle, I/O (database, HTTP, UI) at the edges.
  • There is no built-in Option or Result and no |> operator; when you want the whole paradigm on .NET, that is F#.

Imperative → declarative with LINQ

The query reads as the requirement — delivered orders, revenue per customer, top two — and has no mutable accumulator to get wrong.

Imperative
using System.Globalization;

Order[] orders =
[
    new("ada", OrderStatus.Delivered, 42.50m), new("grace", OrderStatus.Cancelled, 99.00m),
    new("linus", OrderStatus.Placed, 15.00m), new("ada", OrderStatus.Delivered, 15.00m),
    new("grace", OrderStatus.Delivered, 30.00m), new("linus", OrderStatus.Delivered, 9.90m),
];

var totals = new Dictionary<string, decimal>();
foreach (var order in orders)
{
    if (order.Status != OrderStatus.Delivered) continue;
    totals.TryGetValue(order.Customer, out var sum);
    totals[order.Customer] = sum + order.Total;
}
var ranking = new List<KeyValuePair<string, decimal>>(totals);
// List<T>.Sort is unstable: without the second key, equal revenues come out in any order
ranking.Sort((a, b) => a.Value != b.Value ? b.Value.CompareTo(a.Value) : string.CompareOrdinal(a.Key, b.Key));
for (var i = 0; i < Math.Min(2, ranking.Count); i++)
{
    var (customer, revenue) = ranking[i];
    Console.WriteLine(string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"{customer} {revenue:0.00}"));
}

enum OrderStatus { Placed, Delivered, Cancelled }
record Order(string Customer, OrderStatus Status, decimal Total);
Declarative
using System.Globalization;

Order[] orders =
[
    new("ada", OrderStatus.Delivered, 42.50m), new("grace", OrderStatus.Cancelled, 99.00m),
    new("linus", OrderStatus.Placed, 15.00m), new("ada", OrderStatus.Delivered, 15.00m),
    new("grace", OrderStatus.Delivered, 30.00m), new("linus", OrderStatus.Delivered, 9.90m),
];

var topCustomers = orders
    .Where(order => order.Status == OrderStatus.Delivered)
    .GroupBy(order => order.Customer)
    .Select(group => (Customer: group.Key, Revenue: group.Sum(order => order.Total)))
    .OrderByDescending(row => row.Revenue)
    .ThenBy(row => row.Customer, StringComparer.Ordinal)    // the same tie-break as the loop
    .Take(2);

foreach (var (customer, revenue) in topCustomers)
    Console.WriteLine(string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"{customer} {revenue:0.00}"));

enum OrderStatus { Placed, Delivered, Cancelled }
record Order(string Customer, OrderStatus Status, decimal Total);
Result
ada 57.50
grace 30.00

Func, Action, delegates and local functions

`Func<T, TResult>` returns and `Action<T>` does not; a named `delegate` names a domain idea, and a local function keeps a helper next to its only caller.

using System.Globalization;

Order[] orders = [new("A-1", 42.50m), new("A-2", 120.00m), new("A-3", 250.00m)];

Func<decimal, string> eur = amount => string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"{amount:0.00} EUR");
Action<string> print = Console.WriteLine;              // a method group converts to a delegate

var threshold = 100m;
bool IsLarge(Order order) => order.Total >= threshold; // a local function; this one captures `threshold`

foreach (var order in orders.Where(IsLarge)) print($"{order.Id} {eur(order.Total)}");

// `static` forbids captures, so the lambda can never allocate a closure by accident
PriceRule weekendSale = static total => total * 0.9m;
PriceRule[] rules = [weekendSale, static total => total - 5m];
print(eur(ApplyAll(rules, 120m)));

static decimal ApplyAll(IEnumerable<PriceRule> rules, decimal total) =>
    rules.Aggregate(total, (running, rule) => rule(running));

// A named delegate documents intent and allows ref/out parameters and attributes;
// the design guidelines still prefer Func/Action for public callbacks.
delegate decimal PriceRule(decimal total);

record Order(string Id, decimal Total);

The higher-order operations to know cold

Every one is an extension method on `IEnumerable<T>` in `System.Linq`; most are deferred until enumerated.

IdeaLINQWatch out
mapSelect(x => …), Select((x, i) => …)Index() (.NET 9) yields (Index, Item) pairs
filterWhere, OfType<T>()OfType<T>() also drops nulls
flatMapSelectManyflattens one level, e.g. orders → lines
reduce / foldAggregate(seed, (acc, x) => …); Sum, Min, Max, AverageAggregate without a seed throws on an empty sequence
groupGroupBy (deferred), ToLookup (immediate)CountBy, AggregateBy (.NET 9) skip the intermediate groups
sortOrderBy/ThenBy, Order() (.NET 7)stable; List<T>.Sort is not
findFirst, FirstOrDefault, Single, Any, AllSingle throws on a second match — use it to assert uniqueness
by keyDistinctBy, MinBy, MaxBy, ExceptBy (.NET 6)no need for a custom comparer
zip and batchZip, Chunk(size)Chunk gives arrays: handy for batching API calls
materializeToList, ToArray, ToDictionary, ToHashSetthe point where a deferred query runs

Composition, currying and partial application

Build a pipeline from small functions with a `Then` extension, and fix arguments early with closures; C# has no built-in compose operator.

using System.Globalization;

Func<decimal, decimal> applyCoupon = total => total - 10m;
Func<decimal, decimal> addVat = total => total * 1.21m;
Func<decimal, string> format = total => total.ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);

var checkoutTotal = applyCoupon.Then(addVat).Then(format);   // left to right, like the requirement
Console.WriteLine(checkoutTotal(110m));

// Currying: one argument at a time, so a function is configured now and applied later
Func<decimal, Func<decimal, decimal>> discountBy = rate => total => total * (1 - rate);
var tenPercentOff = discountBy(0.10m);
Console.WriteLine(format(tenPercentOff(200m)));

// Partial application: fix the first argument of a two-argument function with a closure
Func<string, int, string> shippingLabel = (country, parcels) => $"{parcels} parcel(s) to {country}";
Func<int, string> toSpain = parcels => shippingLabel("ES", parcels);
Console.WriteLine(toSpain(2));

static class FunctionExtensions
{
    public static Func<T, TResult> Then<T, TMiddle, TResult>(
        this Func<T, TMiddle> first, Func<TMiddle, TResult> second) =>
        value => second(first(value));
}

180.00

Immutability: records, `with`, immutable and frozen collections

`with` copies and changes; an immutable collection's `Add` returns a new collection; `FrozenDictionary` is for data built once and read often.

using System.Collections.Frozen;
using System.Collections.Immutable;
using System.Globalization;

var placed = new Order("A-1", [new Line("mug", 2)], OrderStatus.Placed);
var shipped = placed with { Status = OrderStatus.Shipped };                  // a copy; `placed` is untouched
var amended = placed with { Lines = placed.Lines.Add(new Line("lamp", 1)) }; // Add returns a new list

Console.WriteLine($"{placed.Status} {shipped.Status} | lines {placed.Lines.Count} {amended.Lines.Count}");
Console.WriteLine(shipped with { Status = OrderStatus.Placed } == placed);      // value equality

// ...but records compare a collection property by reference, not by contents
var rebuilt = new Order("A-1", [new Line("mug", 2)], OrderStatus.Placed);
Console.WriteLine(rebuilt == placed);

// Built once at startup, read on every request: lookups are optimised when it is frozen
FrozenDictionary<string, decimal> vatByCountry =
    new Dictionary<string, decimal> { ["ES"] = 0.21m, ["DE"] = 0.19m, ["FR"] = 0.20m }.ToFrozenDictionary();
Console.WriteLine(vatByCountry["DE"].ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));

enum OrderStatus { Placed, Shipped }
record Line(string Sku, int Quantity);
record Order(string Id, ImmutableList<Line> Lines, OrderStatus Status);

Option and Result as containers

C# has no built-in Option or Result: `T?` and `TryGetValue` are the everyday Option, and a closed two-case record hierarchy with `Match`, `Bind` and `Map` is a Result.

using System.Globalization;

var prices = new Dictionary<string, decimal> { ["mug"] = 12.00m, ["lamp"] = 99.00m };

foreach (var input in new[] { "mug x2", "lamp x0", "mug two", "desk x1" })
{
    var withVat = ParseLine(input)
        .Bind(line => prices.TryGetValue(line.Sku, out var price)     // TryGetValue: the BCL's Option
            ? Result<decimal>.Ok(price * line.Quantity)
            : Result<decimal>.Fail($"unknown product '{line.Sku}'"))
        .Map(total => total * 1.21m);
    var text = withVat.Match(
        total => total.ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture),
        reason => reason);
    Console.WriteLine($"{input}: {text}");
}

static Result<CartLine> ParseLine(string input) => input.Split(" x") switch
{
    [var sku, var raw] when int.TryParse(raw, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var n) => n > 0
        ? Result<CartLine>.Ok(new CartLine(sku, n))
        : Result<CartLine>.Fail("quantity must be at least 1"),
    _ => Result<CartLine>.Fail("expected 'sku xN'"),
};

record CartLine(string Sku, int Quantity);

abstract record Result<T>
{
    private Result() { }                                   // closed: Success and Failure only
    public sealed record Success(T Value) : Result<T>;
    public sealed record Failure(string Reason) : Result<T>;

    public static Result<T> Ok(T value) => new Success(value);
    public static Result<T> Fail(string reason) => new Failure(reason);

    public TOut Match<TOut>(Func<T, TOut> ok, Func<string, TOut> fail) => this switch
    {
        Success(var value) => ok(value),
        Failure(var reason) => fail(reason),
        _ => throw new InvalidOperationException("unreachable: the hierarchy is closed"),
    };

    // A failure short-circuits: the rest of the chain never runs
    public Result<TNext> Bind<TNext>(Func<T, Result<TNext>> next) => Match(next, Result<TNext>.Fail);
    public Result<TNext> Map<TNext>(Func<T, TNext> transform) =>
        Bind(value => Result<TNext>.Ok(transform(value)));
}

Make illegal states unrepresentable

Three independent fields allow eight combinations for three real states; a closed record hierarchy plus a `switch` expression allows exactly the three.

Flags
OrdersScreen[] states =
[
    new() { IsLoading = true },
    new() { Error = "offline" },
    new() { Orders = ["A-1", "A-2"] },
    new() { Orders = [] },
];
foreach (var state in states) Console.WriteLine(Render(state));
// Also compiles — what should the screen show?
// new OrdersScreen { IsLoading = true, Error = "offline", Orders = ["A-1"] };

static string Render(OrdersScreen state)
{
    if (state.IsLoading) return "spinner";
    if (state.Error != null) return $"error banner: {state.Error}";
    if (state.Orders == null || state.Orders.Count == 0) return "empty state";
    return $"list of {state.Orders.Count}";
}

class OrdersScreen
{
    public bool IsLoading { get; init; }
    public string? Error { get; init; }
    public List<string>? Orders { get; init; }
}
Closed hierarchy
OrdersScreen[] states =
[
    new OrdersScreen.Loading(),
    new OrdersScreen.Failed("offline"),
    new OrdersScreen.Loaded(["A-1", "A-2"]),
    new OrdersScreen.Loaded([]),
];
foreach (var state in states) Console.WriteLine(Render(state));
// A failed state that also has orders cannot be written down.

static string Render(OrdersScreen state) => state switch
{
    OrdersScreen.Loading => "spinner",
    OrdersScreen.Failed(var message) => $"error banner: {message}",
    OrdersScreen.Loaded { Orders.Count: 0 } => "empty state",
    OrdersScreen.Loaded(var orders) => $"list of {orders.Count}",
    _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(state)),
};

abstract record OrdersScreen
{
    private OrdersScreen() { }                     // no other subtypes can exist
    public sealed record Loading : OrdersScreen;
    public sealed record Failed(string Message) : OrdersScreen;
    public sealed record Loaded(IReadOnlyList<string> Orders) : OrdersScreen;
}

error banner: offline
list of 2
empty state

Laziness and memoization

A LINQ query or `yield` iterator is a recipe that runs when enumerated; `Lazy<T>` computes once on first use; memoize a pure, expensive function with a cache.

using System.Collections.Concurrent;

static IEnumerable<int> OrderPages()                     // yield: each page is produced on demand
{
    for (var page = 1; ; page++)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"fetch page {page}");
        yield return page;
    }
}

var firstTwo = OrderPages().Take(2);                     // nothing fetched yet
Console.WriteLine("query built");
foreach (var page in firstTwo) Console.WriteLine($"render page {page}");

var taxTable = new Lazy<string[]>(() =>
{
    Console.WriteLine("load tax table");
    return ["ES", "DE"];
});
Console.WriteLine($"created: {taxTable.IsValueCreated}");
// Loads once and is thread-safe; it also caches a factory exception (see the trade-offs)
Console.WriteLine($"{taxTable.Value.Length} countries, {taxTable.Value.Length} again");

var shippingQuote = Memoize((string country) =>
{
    Console.WriteLine($"quote {country}");
    return country == "ES" ? 495 : 995;
});
Console.WriteLine($"{shippingQuote("ES")} {shippingQuote("ES")} {shippingQuote("DE")}");

// GetOrAdd may run the factory twice under a race; fine for a pure function
static Func<TIn, TOut> Memoize<TIn, TOut>(Func<TIn, TOut> compute) where TIn : notnull
{
    var cache = new ConcurrentDictionary<TIn, TOut>();
    return input => cache.GetOrAdd(input, compute);
}

Trade-offs to say out loud

Functional style is a tool; know what it costs on the CLR.

  • Allocation — every LINQ operator allocates an enumerator and usually a delegate, and a capturing lambda allocates a closure; in a hot loop, write the for loop or use Span<T>.
  • Multiple enumeration — a deferred query re-runs (and re-queries the database) each time it is enumerated; call ToList() once (analyzer CA1851 flags it).
  • Closures capture variables, not values — a lambda sees later changes to a captured local; mark lambdas static when they should capture nothing.
  • with is a shallow copy — the new record shares its lists with the old one; use immutable collections for members, or copy them.
  • Lazy<T> caches a factory exception — in the default mode one transient failure is permanent; use LazyThreadSafetyMode.PublicationOnly or retry outside it when the load can fail.
  • A memo cache grows forever — the Memoize above never evicts; bound it, or use MemoryCache with a size limit or an expiry.
  • Immutable collections are not free — ImmutableList<T> is a tree (O(log n) indexing); prefer ImmutableArray<T> for read-mostly data and FrozenDictionary for build-once lookups.
  • Readability — a ten-step chain is hard to debug; name intermediate queries. Libraries such as LanguageExt add a whole dialect: adopt one only if the team will read it.
  • Where it shines — pure domain logic, validation pipelines, reducers and view-state mapping: deterministic, parallel-safe and trivially unit-tested.

Architectural Approaches

MVC, MVVM, MVU and clean/onion/hexagonal layering for .NET apps and services — a testable view model, a repository and use case wired with Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection, service lifetimes, navigation as a service, a reducer, and vertical slices.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12
  • dotnet >=8
  • .NET; the patterns apply to .NET MAUI, WPF, WinUI, Blazor and ASP.NET Core (the examples are console apps)

Sources: Common web application architectures — .NET architecture guide · Model-View-ViewModel — .NET MAUI enterprise application patterns · Dependency injection — .NET

The approaches compared

The presentation patterns (MVC, MVVM, MVU) and the layering patterns (clean, onion, hexagonal) answer different questions — most apps use one of each.

ApproachData flowWhere logic livesTestabilityAt home in
MVCinput → controller → model → controller picks a viewcontrollers calling servicescontrollers with fake services; views need an integration testASP.NET Core MVC; Razor Pages (the page model plays the controller)

MVVM done properly

The view model owns one state value, reports a failure and shows it, treats a user's cancellation as a return to what was on screen, and takes its dependencies as parameters — overlapping loads are the next card, and INotifyPropertyChanged is on the MVVM State sheet (`cs-mvvm-state`).

using System.Globalization;
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.ComponentModel;
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Input;

Func<CancellationToken, Task<decimal[]>> backend = _ => Task.FromResult<decimal[]>([42.50m, 15.00m]);
var viewModel = new OrdersViewModel(ct => backend(ct), e => Console.WriteLine($"reported: {e.Message}"));
viewModel.PropertyChanged += (_, _) => Console.WriteLine(viewModel.State);    // what a binding would see
await viewModel.LoadCommand.ExecuteAsync(null);                               // the view's command

backend = ct => new TaskCompletionSource<decimal[]>().Task.WaitAsync(ct);     // a backend that hangs...
var refresh = viewModel.LoadCommand.ExecuteAsync(null);
viewModel.LoadCommand.Cancel();                                               // ...so the user cancels
await refresh;

backend = _ => Task.FromException<decimal[]>(new HttpRequestException("503 Service Unavailable"));
await viewModel.LoadCommand.ExecuteAsync(null);                               // the next refresh fails

partial class OrdersViewModel(
    Func<CancellationToken, Task<decimal[]>> loadOrderTotals, Action<Exception> report) : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty] private OrdersState state = new Loading();   // generates State and its notification

    [RelayCommand]                                    // generates LoadCommand, cancellable through its token
    private async Task LoadAsync(CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var previous = State;
        State = new Loading();
        try
        {
            var totals = await loadOrderTotals(ct);
            var sum = totals.Sum().ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
            State = new Loaded($"{totals.Length} orders, {sum} EUR");
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException) { State = previous; }   // the user's choice: not an error
        catch (Exception e)                           // this screen's top-level handler: report, then show it
        {
            report(e);
            State = new Failed("Could not load your orders.");
        }
    }
}

abstract record OrdersState;

sealed record Loading : OrdersState;

sealed record Loaded(string Summary) : OrdersState;

sealed record Failed(string Message) : OrdersState;

Stale responses: only the newest request may write

Requests overlap whenever the user is faster than the network, so a view model numbers each one and drops an answer that is no longer the newest (cancelling the superseded request's token also saves the bandwidth).

// A search box's view model: one request per keystroke, and the answers can arrive in any order.
var pending = new Dictionary<string, TaskCompletionSource<string[]>>();

Task<string[]> Search(string query)                    // a fake backend: the demo releases each reply by hand
{
    pending[query] = new TaskCompletionSource<string[]>(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously);
    return pending[query].Task;
}

var viewModel = new SearchViewModel(Search, show: text => Console.WriteLine($"shown: {text}"));
var typing = new[] { viewModel.OnInputAsync("mu"), viewModel.OnInputAsync("mug") };

pending["mug"].SetResult(["mug", "travel mug"]);                 // the newer query answers first...
pending["mu"].SetResult(["mug", "muffin tin", "mustard"]);       // ...the older one lands late: dropped
await Task.WhenAll(typing);
Console.WriteLine("rendered once, for the newest query");

sealed class SearchViewModel(Func<string, Task<string[]>> search, Action<string> show)
{
    private int latest;

    public async Task OnInputAsync(string query)
    {
        var request = ++latest;
        var results = await search(query);
        if (request != latest) return;                 // a newer query was typed: this answer is stale
        show($"{query} -> {string.Join(", ", results)}");
    }
}
Result
shown: mug -> mug, travel mug
rendered once, for the newest query

Repository + use case, wired by the container

The domain declares the port, the use case depends only on it and is resolved inside a scope once per request, and the composition root picks the adapter — the in-memory one is the store itself, an EF Core one is scoped like its `DbContext`.

using System.Collections.Concurrent;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

var services = new ServiceCollection();
// The adapter is the store, so a thread-safe singleton; EF Core: AddDbContext + a scoped EfOrderRepository
services.AddSingleton<IOrderRepository, InMemoryOrderRepository>();
services.AddScoped<CancelOrder>();
using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(validateScopes: true);

foreach (var id in new[] { "A-1", "A-1", "A-9" })
{
    await using var scope = provider.CreateAsyncScope();     // one per request, as in ASP.NET Core
    Console.WriteLine(await scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<CancelOrder>().ExecuteAsync(id));
}

sealed record Order(string Id, bool IsCancelled);                      // Domain: the entity and its port

interface IOrderRepository
{
    Task<Order?> FindAsync(string id, CancellationToken ct);
    Task SaveAsync(Order order, CancellationToken ct);
}

sealed class CancelOrder(IOrderRepository orders)                      // Application: one use case
{
    public async Task<string> ExecuteAsync(string id, CancellationToken ct = default)
    {
        var order = await orders.FindAsync(id, ct);
        if (order is null) return $"{id}: not found";
        if (order.IsCancelled) return $"{id}: already cancelled";
        await orders.SaveAsync(order with { IsCancelled = true }, ct);
        return $"{id}: cancelled";
    }
}

sealed class InMemoryOrderRepository : IOrderRepository              // Infrastructure: implements the port
{
    private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, Order> orders = new() { ["A-1"] = new("A-1", false) };

    public Task<Order?> FindAsync(string id, CancellationToken ct) =>
        Task.FromResult(orders.GetValueOrDefault(id));

    public Task SaveAsync(Order order, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        orders[order.Id] = order;
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}
Result
A-1: cancelled
A-1: already cancelled
A-9: not found

Service lifetimes and the captive-dependency trap

Singleton is one per container, scoped one per scope and transient one per resolution — and a singleton must never hold a scoped service, which only `ValidateScopes` plus `ValidateOnBuild` report at startup.

using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddSingleton<PriceCache>();         // one for the whole app
services.AddScoped<CartSession>();           // one per request (ASP.NET Core), per circuit (Blazor Server)
services.AddTransient<ReceiptBuilder>();     // a new instance on every resolution

using (var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(new ServiceProviderOptions { ValidateScopes = true }))
{
    using var first = provider.CreateScope();
    using var second = provider.CreateScope();
    var (a, b) = (first.ServiceProvider, second.ServiceProvider);
    Console.WriteLine($"singleton, two scopes: {Same<PriceCache>(a, b)}");
    Console.WriteLine($"scoped, one scope:     {Same<CartSession>(a, a)}");
    Console.WriteLine($"scoped, two scopes:    {Same<CartSession>(a, b)}");
    Console.WriteLine($"transient, twice:      {Same<ReceiptBuilder>(a, a)}");
}

// The trap: a singleton holding a scoped service keeps the first cart forever, for every user.
services.AddSingleton<CheckoutTotals>();
foreach (var (scopes, onBuild) in new[] { (true, false), (false, true), (true, true) })
{
    var options = new ServiceProviderOptions { ValidateScopes = scopes, ValidateOnBuild = onBuild };
    try
    {
        using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(options);
        Console.WriteLine($"ValidateScopes={scopes}, ValidateOnBuild={onBuild}: starts");
    }
    catch (AggregateException e)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"both: fails at startup: {e.InnerExceptions[0].InnerException?.Message}");
    }
}
// ValidateScopes alone throws only when CheckoutTotals is first resolved; the generic host sets both in
// Development. Related: a transient IDisposable resolved from the root lives until the root is disposed.

static bool Same<T>(IServiceProvider x, IServiceProvider y) where T : notnull =>
    ReferenceEquals(x.GetRequiredService<T>(), y.GetRequiredService<T>());

sealed class PriceCache;
sealed class CartSession;
sealed class ReceiptBuilder;
sealed class CheckoutTotals(CartSession cart) { public CartSession Cart => cart; }

scoped, one scope:     True
scoped, two scopes:    False

ValidateScopes=True, ValidateOnBuild=False: starts
ValidateScopes=False, ValidateOnBuild=True: starts
both: fails at startup: Cannot consume scoped service 'CartSession' from singleton 'CheckoutTotals'.

Navigation as its own concern

View models ask an `INavigator` for a route; one adapter per UI stack knows Shell, `NavigationManager` or `Frame`, and tests record the requests.

var navigator = new RecordingNavigator();
var viewModel = new OrderListViewModel(navigator);
await viewModel.OpenOrderAsync("A-1");
await viewModel.OpenOrderAsync("B&7");          // escaped, so it cannot break the route
await viewModel.CheckoutAsync(cartIsEmpty: true);
await viewModel.CheckoutAsync(cartIsEmpty: false);

interface INavigator
{
    Task GoToAsync(string route, IDictionary<string, object>? parameters = null);
}

static class Routes
{
    public const string OrderDetail = "orders/detail", Checkout = "checkout", EmptyCart = "cart/empty";
}

sealed class OrderListViewModel(INavigator navigator)
{
    public Task OpenOrderAsync(string orderId) =>
        navigator.GoToAsync(Routes.OrderDetail, new Dictionary<string, object> { ["id"] = orderId });

    public Task CheckoutAsync(bool cartIsEmpty) =>
        navigator.GoToAsync(cartIsEmpty ? Routes.EmptyCart : Routes.Checkout);   // a testable decision
}

// The app registers one adapter per stack instead:
//   .NET MAUI Shell: Shell.Current.GoToAsync(route, parameters)   (routes: Routing.RegisterRoute)
//   Blazor:          navigationManager.NavigateTo($"/{route}?id={Uri.EscapeDataString(id)}")
//   WinUI:           frame.Navigate(typeof(OrderDetailPage), parameters)   — WPF: frame.Navigate(page)
sealed class RecordingNavigator : INavigator
{
    public Task GoToAsync(string route, IDictionary<string, object>? parameters = null)
    {
        var pairs = parameters?.Select(p => $"{p.Key}={Uri.EscapeDataString(p.Value.ToString() ?? "")}");
        var query = pairs is null ? "" : "?" + string.Join("&", pairs);
        Console.WriteLine($"navigate {route}{query}");
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}

Unidirectional flow: the store is a fold

State changes only through a pure reducer, so replaying the same actions always yields the same screens; stores, effects and Fluxor are on the Unidirectional State sheet (`cs-unidirectional`).

using System.Globalization;

CartAction[] actions =
[
    new CartAction.Add("mug", 12.00m),
    new CartAction.Add("lamp", 99.00m),
    new CartAction.ApplyCoupon("FREESTUFF"),                 // not a valid code: the reducer ignores it
    new CartAction.ApplyCoupon("WELCOME10"),
    new CartAction.Remove("mug"),
];

var state = new CartState([], Coupon: null);
foreach (var action in actions)
{
    state = CartReducer.Reduce(state, action);
    Console.WriteLine(state.Describe());
}

record CartLine(string Sku, decimal Price);

record CartState(IReadOnlyList<CartLine> Lines, string? Coupon)
{
    public decimal Total => Lines.Sum(line => line.Price) * (Coupon is null ? 1m : 0.9m);
    public string Describe() => string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
        $"[{string.Join(", ", Lines.Select(line => line.Sku))}] {Total:0.00}{CouponLabel}");

    private string CouponLabel => Coupon is null ? "" : $" ({Coupon})";
}

abstract record CartAction
{
    public sealed record Add(string Sku, decimal Price) : CartAction;
    public sealed record Remove(string Sku) : CartAction;
    public sealed record ApplyCoupon(string Code) : CartAction;
}

static class CartReducer
{
    private static readonly HashSet<string> KnownCoupons = ["WELCOME10"];

    public static CartState Reduce(CartState state, CartAction action) => action switch
    {
        CartAction.Add(var sku, var price) => state with { Lines = [.. state.Lines, new(sku, price)] },
        CartAction.Remove(var sku) => state with { Lines = [.. state.Lines.Where(line => line.Sku != sku)] },
        CartAction.ApplyCoupon(var code) when KnownCoupons.Contains(code) => state with { Coupon = code },
        _ => state,                                          // an unknown coupon changes nothing
    };
}
Result

[mug, lamp] 111.00
[mug, lamp] 111.00
[mug, lamp] 99.90 (WELCOME10)
[lamp] 89.10 (WELCOME10)

Vertical slices and CQRS, in outline

Each feature is a request and its handler, owning its data access; commands change state and queries only read, and a mediator later adds one dispatch point and pipeline behaviours without changing the slices.

using System.Collections.Concurrent;
using System.Globalization;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddSingleton<OrderStore>();                                            // shared, so thread-safe
services.AddScoped<IHandler<PlaceOrder, string>, PlaceOrderHandler>();          // Features/PlaceOrder/
services.AddScoped<IHandler<CustomerOrders, string[]>, CustomerOrdersHandler>(); // Features/CustomerOrders/
using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(validateScopes: true);

await using var request = provider.CreateAsyncScope();
var place = request.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IHandler<PlaceOrder, string>>();
Console.WriteLine(await place.HandleAsync(new PlaceOrder("A-1", "ada", 42.50m)));
Console.WriteLine(await place.HandleAsync(new PlaceOrder("A-2", "ada", 15.00m)));
var history = request.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IHandler<CustomerOrders, string[]>>();
Console.WriteLine(string.Join("; ", await history.HandleAsync(new CustomerOrders("ada"))));

interface IHandler<in TRequest, TResponse>
{
    Task<TResponse> HandleAsync(TRequest request, CancellationToken ct = default);
}

sealed record Order(string Id, string Customer, decimal Total);

sealed class OrderStore { public ConcurrentDictionary<string, Order> Orders { get; } = new(); }

// Command: changes state and returns as little as possible.
sealed record PlaceOrder(string Id, string Customer, decimal Total);

sealed class PlaceOrderHandler(OrderStore store) : IHandler<PlaceOrder, string>
{
    public Task<string> HandleAsync(PlaceOrder command, CancellationToken ct = default) =>
        Task.FromResult(store.Orders.TryAdd(command.Id, new(command.Id, command.Customer, command.Total))
            ? $"placed {command.Id}"
            : $"{command.Id} was already placed");
}

// Query: reads, shaped for the screen that asks, never changes state (with EF Core: a DbContext query).
sealed record CustomerOrders(string Customer);

sealed class CustomerOrdersHandler(OrderStore store) : IHandler<CustomerOrders, string[]>
{
    public Task<string[]> HandleAsync(CustomerOrders query, CancellationToken ct = default) =>
        Task.FromResult(store.Orders.Values.Where(o => o.Customer == query.Customer)
            .OrderBy(o => o.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal)
            .Select(o => string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"{o.Id} {o.Total:0.00}"))
            .ToArray());
}

placed A-1
placed A-2
A-1 42.50; A-2 15.00

Clean / onion layering as projects

The compiler enforces the direction once each layer is its own project: a reference that points outward simply does not exist.

ProjectContainsReferencesMust not reference
Shop.Domainentities, value objects, domain rules, ports such as IOrderRepositorynothing (the BCL only)EF Core, ASP.NET Core, MAUI, any NuGet adapter
Shop.Applicationuse cases or handlers, DTOs, validationShop.DomainShop.Infrastructure, any UI project
Shop.Infrastructurethe EF Core DbContext, typed HttpClients, adapters implementing the portsShop.Application, Shop.Domainany UI project
Shop.App / Shop.Apipages, view models, endpoints, and the composition root (MauiProgram.cs, Program.cs)all of the above—
Shop.*.Testsunit tests per layer; integration tests against Infrastructurethe project under testanother test project

How to answer "which architecture would you use?"

Answer with the forces, not a favourite acronym.

  • Start from the constraints — team size, how long the app lives, how many platforms, offline needs, and how much logic is domain versus screens over an API.
  • Name one presentation pattern and one layering — e.g. MVVM with CommunityToolkit.Mvvm for a MAUI app, over a clean core with a repository and use cases.
  • Say how you test it — view models and use cases with in-memory fakes, adapters with integration tests, a few UI tests on the main journeys.
  • Say where navigation, DI and state live — a navigation service, constructor injection from the composition root, one state value per screen.
  • Blazor is component-first — component state and a store (MVU) are more natural there than MVVM; WPF, WinUI and MAUI bindings make MVVM the default.
  • Scale the ceremony — a CRUD screen over an API does not need four projects; vertical slices with one project can be the cleanest answer for a small service.
  • Logic in code-behind or in .razor markup — it can only be tested through the UI; move it into the view model, component class or a service.
  • A domain type or use case that news up HttpClient or a vendor SDK — the dependency arrow points the wrong way; depend on a port the domain owns.
  • DbContext in a handler is a choice, not a mistake — it is the vertical-slice design and EF Core already is a unit of work; add a repository when you need to stub data access in unit tests, and know it costs code to write and maintain (EF Core's testing guide weighs both).

Sources: Choosing a testing strategy — EF Core

C# Engineering Best Practices

The framework design guidelines that matter in review, typed exceptions with `when` filters, nullable discipline, structured logging, options validated at startup, async and disposal rules, a performance checklist and the project hygiene behind them.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12
  • dotnet >=8
  • .NET (any app model; the examples are console apps)

Sources: Framework design guidelines — .NET · Best practices for exceptions — .NET · Nullable reference types — C# · Code analysis in .NET

The ten that matter most

If you say nothing else in a review, say these.

  • Nullable on, warnings as errors — <Nullable>enable</Nullable> and <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors> in Directory.Build.props, from day one.
  • Follow the framework design guidelines — PascalCase public API, Async suffix, I on interfaces, no public fields, read-only collection returns.
  • Exceptions are for the exceptional — typed exceptions, catch only what you can handle, throw; to rethrow; the Try-pattern for ordinary failures.
  • Async all the way — never .Result or .Wait(); accept a CancellationToken and pass it on.
  • Own it, dispose it — using / await using for what you create; never dispose what was injected.
  • Constructor injection, small interfaces — no new of services and no static singletons inside logic; inject TimeProvider for time.
  • Structured logging — ILogger message templates, never string interpolation; pass the exception itself (LogError(e, "… {OrderId}", id)), never e.Message; never log secrets or personal data.
  • Validate configuration at startup — typed options with ValidateOnStart(); secrets from user-secrets in development and a vault or the environment in production, never from source control.
  • Measure before optimising — BenchmarkDotNet and dotnet-counters, then Span<T>, pooling and fewer allocations where the profile says.
  • Immutable by default — record, init, readonly, sealed; mutate only state you own.

Framework design guidelines and XML docs, in review

Properties not fields, enums not magic ints or bool flags, a read-only snapshot not a mutable `List<T>`, argument validation, and `///` docs IntelliSense shows to every caller.

Before
using System.Globalization;

var history = new OrderHistory();
foreach (var o in history.GetOrders("ada", false))
    Console.WriteLine($"{o.id} {o.total.ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)}");
Console.WriteLine($"with cancelled: {history.GetOrders("ada", true).Count}");

public class Order
{
    public string id = "";
    public string customer = "";
    public decimal total;
    public int status;                                  // 1 = delivered, 2 = cancelled
}

public class OrderHistory
{
    private List<Order> orders = new()
    {
        new() { id = "A-1", customer = "ada", total = 42.50m, status = 1 },
        new() { id = "A-2", customer = "ada", total = 99.00m, status = 2 },
        new() { id = "A-3", customer = "ada", total = 15.00m, status = 1 },
        new() { id = "A-4", customer = "grace", total = 30.00m, status = 1 },
    };

    // A mutable List<T>, abbreviated parameters, a bool flag, no docs, no validation
    public List<Order> GetOrders(string c, bool b) =>
        orders.Where(o => o.customer == c && (b || o.status != 2)).ToList();
}
After
using System.Globalization;

var history = new OrderHistory(
[
    new("A-1", "ada", 42.50m, IsCancelled: false), new("A-2", "ada", 99.00m, IsCancelled: true),
    new("A-3", "ada", 15.00m, IsCancelled: false), new("A-4", "grace", 30.00m, IsCancelled: false),
]);
foreach (var order in history.ForCustomer("ada"))
    Console.WriteLine($"{order.Id} {order.Total.ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)}");
Console.WriteLine($"with cancelled: {history.ForCustomer("ada", OrderFilter.IncludeCancelled).Count}");

/// <summary>A customer's order, as the history reports it.</summary>
/// <param name="Id">The order number, such as <c>A-1</c>.</param>
/// <param name="CustomerId">The customer who placed it.</param>
/// <param name="Total">The amount charged, in euros.</param>
/// <param name="IsCancelled">Whether the order was cancelled.</param>
public sealed record Order(string Id, string CustomerId, decimal Total, bool IsCancelled);

/// <summary>Which orders <see cref="OrderHistory.ForCustomer"/> returns.</summary>
public enum OrderFilter
{
    /// <summary>Only orders that still stand.</summary>
    ExcludeCancelled,

    /// <summary>Every order, cancelled ones included.</summary>
    IncludeCancelled,
}

/// <summary>Reads customers' order history.</summary>
public sealed class OrderHistory(IEnumerable<Order> orders)
{
    private readonly IReadOnlyList<Order> orders = orders.ToList();

    /// <summary>Returns one customer's orders.</summary>
    /// <param name="customerId">The customer's id; must not be empty.</param>
    /// <param name="filter">Whether cancelled orders are included; by default they are not.</param>
    /// <returns>A read-only snapshot of the matching orders.</returns>
    /// <exception cref="ArgumentException"><paramref name="customerId"/> is empty or white space.</exception>
    public IReadOnlyList<Order> ForCustomer(
        string customerId, OrderFilter filter = OrderFilter.ExcludeCancelled)
    {
        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(customerId);
        return orders.Where(o => o.CustomerId == customerId &&
            (filter == OrderFilter.IncludeCancelled || !o.IsCancelled)).ToList();
    }
}

A-1 42.50
A-3 15.00
with cancelled: 3

Model errors: typed exceptions and `when` filters

Return a result type when every caller branches on the outcome (as on the Clean Code sheet), throw a typed exception when a component cannot do what its name promises (`ChargeAsync` cannot charge), catch it by type or `when` filter where you can handle it, and let bugs and cancellation reach the global handler.

Catch-all
using static System.Net.HttpStatusCode;

foreach (var status in new[] { OK, PaymentRequired, ServiceUnavailable })
{
    // A demo shortcut: production code injects one HttpClient (IHttpClientFactory), never one per call
    using var client = new HttpClient(new FakeGateway(status)) { BaseAddress = new("https://pay.example/") };
    Console.WriteLine(await Pay(client, "A-1"));
}

static async Task<string> Pay(HttpClient client, string orderId)
{
    try
    {
        var response = await client.PostAsync($"charges/{orderId}", null);
        if ((int)response.StatusCode == 402) throw new Exception("declined");      // thrown to itself
        response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
        return $"{orderId}: paid";
    }
    catch (Exception e)          // also swallows bugs and cancellation, then guesses from the text
    {
        return e.Message == "declined" ? $"{orderId}: card declined"
             : e.Message.Contains("503") ? $"{orderId}: try again later"
             : $"{orderId}: error";
    }
}

sealed class FakeGateway(System.Net.HttpStatusCode status) : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct) => Task.FromResult(new HttpResponseMessage(status));
}
Typed
using static System.Net.HttpStatusCode;

foreach (var status in new[] { OK, PaymentRequired, ServiceUnavailable })
{
    // A demo shortcut: production code injects one HttpClient (IHttpClientFactory), never one per call
    using var client = new HttpClient(new FakeGateway(status)) { BaseAddress = new("https://pay.example/") };
    Console.WriteLine(await Pay(new PaymentsClient(client), "A-1"));
}

static async Task<string> Pay(PaymentsClient payments, string orderId)
{
    try
    {
        await payments.ChargeAsync(orderId, CancellationToken.None);
        return $"{orderId}: paid";
    }
    catch (PaymentDeclinedException e) { return $"{e.OrderId}: card declined"; }
    catch (HttpRequestException e) when (e.StatusCode is ServiceUnavailable or TooManyRequests)
    {
        return $"{orderId}: try again later";
    }
    // Anything else (a bug, cancellation) propagates; if you catch to add context, rethrow with `throw;`
}

sealed class PaymentsClient(HttpClient http)         // the boundary: a 402 becomes a typed exception
{
    public async Task ChargeAsync(string orderId, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        using var response = await http.PostAsync($"charges/{orderId}", content: null, ct);
        if (response.StatusCode == PaymentRequired)
            throw new PaymentDeclinedException(orderId);
        response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();                // HttpRequestException carries StatusCode
    }
}

sealed class PaymentDeclinedException(string orderId) : Exception($"payment for {orderId} was declined")
{
    public string OrderId { get; } = orderId;
}

sealed class FakeGateway(System.Net.HttpStatusCode status) : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct) => Task.FromResult(new HttpResponseMessage(status));
}
Result
A-1: paid
A-1: card declined
A-1: try again later

Nullable reference types discipline

Let the annotations tell the truth — `required` members instead of `= null!`, `[NotNullWhen(true)]` on a Try method instead of a `!` — and the compiler checks every caller.

Silenced
var directory = new CustomerDirectory();
foreach (var id in new[] { "c-1", "c-2", "c-9" }) Console.WriteLine(Greeting(directory, id));

static string Greeting(CustomerDirectory directory, string id)
{
    var customer = directory.Find(id);
    if (customer == null) return "Hello, guest";             // the signature promised it never is
    return customer.Email != null ? $"Hello, {customer.Name} <{customer.Email}>" : $"Hello, {customer.Name}";
}

class Customer
{
    public string Id = null!;                                 // `null!` silences the constructor check
    public string Name = null!;
    public string? Email;
}

class CustomerDirectory
{
    private readonly List<Customer> customers =
    [
        new() { Id = "c-1", Name = "Ada", Email = "ada@example.com" },
        new() { Id = "c-2", Name = "Grace" },
    ];

    public Customer Find(string id) => customers.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Id == id)!;   // `!` hides "not found"
}
Truthful
using System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis;

var directory = new CustomerDirectory();
foreach (var id in new[] { "c-1", "c-2", "c-9" }) Console.WriteLine(Greeting(directory, id));

static string Greeting(CustomerDirectory directory, string id)
{
    if (!directory.TryFind(id, out var customer)) return "Hello, guest";
    return customer.Email is { } email ? $"Hello, {customer.Name} <{email}>" : $"Hello, {customer.Name}";
}

sealed class Customer
{
    public required string Id { get; init; }                // the compiler makes every `new` set it
    public required string Name { get; init; }
    public string? Email { get; init; }                      // `?` only where absence is real
}

sealed class CustomerDirectory
{
    private readonly List<Customer> customers =
    [
        new() { Id = "c-1", Name = "Ada", Email = "ada@example.com" },
        new() { Id = "c-2", Name = "Grace" },
    ];

    public bool TryFind(string id, [NotNullWhen(true)] out Customer? customer)
    {
        customer = customers.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Id == id);
        return customer is not null;
    }
}
Result
Hello, Ada <ada@example.com>
Hello, Grace
Hello, guest

Logging: templates, scopes and [LoggerMessage]

A message template keeps `OrderId` a queryable field and skips formatting when the level is off, a template scope tags every entry inside it, and `[LoggerMessage]` methods add compile-time checking with no params array or boxing.

using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;

using (var factory = LoggerFactory.Create(builder => builder.AddSimpleConsole(options =>
{
    options.SingleLine = true;                 // one entry per line, and no timestamp: stable output
    options.IncludeScopes = true;
})))
{
    var checkout = new CheckoutService(factory.CreateLogger<CheckoutService>());
    checkout.Complete("A-1", 42.50m, paymentAttempts: 2);
}   // disposing the factory flushes the console logger's queue

sealed partial class CheckoutService(ILogger<CheckoutService> logger)
{
    public void Complete(string orderId, decimal total, int paymentAttempts)
    {
        // Don't: logger.LogInformation($"Order {orderId} completed") — it formats even when the level
        // is off, and OrderId becomes plain text instead of a queryable field (analyzer CA2254)
        OrderCompleted(logger, orderId, total);

        using (logger.BeginScope("Order {OrderId}", orderId))    // every entry inside carries OrderId
        {
            if (paymentAttempts > 1) PaymentRetried(logger, paymentAttempts);
        }
    }

    [LoggerMessage(EventId = 1000, Level = LogLevel.Information,
        Message = "Order {OrderId} completed for {Total}")]
    private static partial void OrderCompleted(ILogger logger, string orderId, decimal total);

    [LoggerMessage(EventId = 1001, Level = LogLevel.Warning, Message = "Payment needed {Attempts} attempts")]
    private static partial void PaymentRetried(ILogger logger, int attempts);
}
Result
info: CheckoutService[1000] Order A-1 completed for 42.50
warn: CheckoutService[1001] => Order A-1 Payment needed 2 attempts

Logging an exception you caught

Pass the caught exception itself to the logger — it lands in the entry's exception slot with its type, stack trace and inner exceptions — instead of formatting `e.Message` into the text.

using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Console;

using (var factory = LoggerFactory.Create(builder => builder
    .AddConsole(options => options.FormatterName = "no-trace")
    .AddConsoleFormatter<NoTraceFormatter, ConsoleFormatterOptions>()))
{
    var receipts = new ReceiptService(factory.CreateLogger<ReceiptService>());
    await receipts.SendAsync("A-1", send: () => throw new HttpRequestException("503 Service Unavailable"));
}

sealed partial class ReceiptService(ILogger<ReceiptService> logger)
{
    public async Task SendAsync(string orderId, Func<Task> send)
    {
        try
        {
            await send();
        }
        catch (HttpRequestException e)             // the order is paid either way: log it, retry later
        {
            // Don't: logger.LogError(e.Message) — the type, the stack trace and inner exceptions are lost
            ReceiptNotSent(logger, e, orderId);
        }
    }

    // An Exception parameter goes to the entry's exception slot, not into the message
    [LoggerMessage(EventId = 1002, Level = LogLevel.Error, Message = "Receipt for order {OrderId} not sent")]
    private static partial void ReceiptNotSent(ILogger logger, Exception exception, string orderId);
}

// The default formatters print the full stack trace, which holds this machine's file paths; this demo
// prints only the exception's type and message so its output is the same everywhere.
sealed class NoTraceFormatter() : ConsoleFormatter("no-trace")
{
    public override void Write<TState>(
        in LogEntry<TState> entry, IExternalScopeProvider? scopes, TextWriter output)
    {
        var message = entry.Formatter(entry.State, entry.Exception);
        var error = entry.Exception is { } e ? $" [{e.GetType().Name}: {e.Message}]" : "";
        output.WriteLine($"{entry.LogLevel}: {entry.Category}[{entry.EventId.Id}] {message}{error}");
    }
}
Result
Error: ReceiptService[1002] Receipt for order A-1 not sent [HttpRequestException: 503 Service Unavailable]

Configuration, secrets and feature flags

Bind configuration to a typed options class, validate it before the app takes traffic, keep secrets out of the repository, and make flags typed and off by default.

using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;

// In a host the same check runs before the app takes traffic:
//   services.AddOptions<PaymentOptions>().BindConfiguration("Payments")
//       .ValidateDataAnnotations().ValidateOnStart();
PaymentOptions[] environments =
[
    new() { BaseUrl = "https://pay.example/", TimeoutSeconds = 10, ApiKey = "(from a vault)" },
    new() { BaseUrl = "pay.example", TimeoutSeconds = 0, ApiKey = "" },
];

foreach (var options in environments)
{
    var errors = new List<ValidationResult>();
    var context = new ValidationContext(options);
    var valid = Validator.TryValidateObject(options, context, errors, validateAllProperties: true);
    Console.WriteLine(valid ? "configuration ok: starting" : "refusing to start:");
    foreach (var error in errors) Console.WriteLine($"- {error.ErrorMessage}");
}

// A flag is typed and off by default; read it through IOptionsMonitor<FeatureFlags> to change it live
var flags = new FeatureFlags { NewCheckout = true };
Console.WriteLine(flags.NewCheckout ? "checkout: new flow" : "checkout: classic flow");

sealed class PaymentOptions
{
    [Required, Url] public required string BaseUrl { get; init; }

    [Range(1, 60)] public int TimeoutSeconds { get; init; } = 10;

    // Never in source control: dotnet user-secrets in development, a vault or the environment in production
    [Required] public required string ApiKey { get; init; }
}

sealed class FeatureFlags
{
    public bool NewCheckout { get; init; }
}

configuration ok: starting
refusing to start:
- The BaseUrl field is not a valid fully-qualified http, https, or ftp URL.
- The field TimeoutSeconds must be between 1 and 60.
- The ApiKey field is required.
checkout: new flow

Async practices: tokens, ConfigureAwait, ValueTask

Take a `CancellationToken` and pass it on, use `ConfigureAwait(false)` in library code, and return `ValueTask` only where the result is usually ready synchronously.

using System.Collections.Concurrent;

var prices = new PriceService(new FakeCatalog());
var first = await prices.GetPriceCentsAsync("mug", CancellationToken.None);
var second = prices.GetPriceCentsAsync("mug", CancellationToken.None);       // a cache hit: no Task allocated
Console.WriteLine($"{first} | cached result ready synchronously: {second.IsCompletedSuccessfully}");
Console.WriteLine(await second);                                   // await a ValueTask exactly once

using var timeout = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(50));
try { await prices.GetPriceCentsAsync("lamp", timeout.Token); }
catch (OperationCanceledException) { Console.WriteLine("lamp: lookup cancelled by the timeout"); }

interface ICatalog { Task<int> LoadPriceCentsAsync(string sku, CancellationToken ct); }

sealed class PriceService(ICatalog catalog)                        // library code: no UI context needed
{
    private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, int> cache = new();

    public ValueTask<int> GetPriceCentsAsync(string sku, CancellationToken ct = default) =>
        cache.TryGetValue(sku, out var cents)
            ? ValueTask.FromResult(cents)                              // completes synchronously
            : new ValueTask<int>(LoadAsync(sku, ct));

    private async Task<int> LoadAsync(string sku, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var cents = await catalog.LoadPriceCentsAsync(sku, ct).ConfigureAwait(false);
        cache[sku] = cents;
        return cents;
    }
}

sealed class FakeCatalog : ICatalog
{
    public async Task<int> LoadPriceCentsAsync(string sku, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (sku == "lamp") await Task.Delay(Timeout.Infinite, ct);   // stuck upstream: only the token ends it
        await Task.Yield();
        return 1200;
    }
}
Result
1200 | cached result ready synchronously: True
1200
lamp: lookup cancelled by the timeout

IDisposable discipline

Dispose what you create with `using`, leave what was injected to the container that created it, and make `Dispose` idempotent and fail fast on use after dispose (lifetimes and scopes are on the Architecture sheet).

using System.Text;

using (var printer = new ReceiptPrinter())       // you created it, so you dispose it
{
    printer.Print("A-1");
}
// Injected instead? The container disposes what it created, when its scope ends: never Dispose it yourself.

var closed = new ReceiptPrinter();
closed.Dispose();
closed.Dispose();                                // idempotent: a second call is harmless
try { closed.Print("A-2"); }
catch (ObjectDisposedException e) { Console.WriteLine($"rejected: {e.ObjectName} is disposed"); }

// Sealed, managed resources only: no finalizer and no Dispose(bool) needed.
// An async resource implements IAsyncDisposable and is released with `await using`.
sealed class ReceiptPrinter : IDisposable
{
    private readonly MemoryStream connection = new();       // stands in for a printer connection
    private bool disposed;

    public void Print(string orderId)
    {
        ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf(disposed, this);
        connection.Write(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes($"receipt {orderId}\n"));
        Console.WriteLine($"printed {orderId}");
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        if (disposed) return;
        disposed = true;
        connection.Dispose();
        Console.WriteLine("printer released");
    }
}
Result
printed A-1
printer released
printer released
rejected: ReceiptPrinter is disposed

Performance checklist

In rough order of how often each one is the actual culprit — and only after a profile or benchmark says so.

CheckPreferWhy
I/O and chatty callsbatch requests, IAsyncEnumerable paging, caching, EF Core projections (Select) and AsNoTracking()a round trip costs more than any amount of CPU you can save
allocations in hot pathsSpan<T> / ReadOnlySpan<char> slicing, stackalloc for small buffers, string.Createless garbage means fewer GC pauses
buffers and objectsArrayPool<T>.Shared.Rent / Return; ObjectPool<T> (Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool)reuse large buffers instead of allocating per request
LINQ in a tight loopa for / foreach over an array or Span<T>each operator allocates an enumerator and a delegate; fine everywhere else
collectionspreset capacity, HashSet<T> / Dictionary for lookups, FrozenDictionary for data built once at startupavoids resizing and O(n) List.Contains; a frozen collection is slower to create and never changes
struct versus classa small (under 16 bytes), immutable readonly record struct; a class for everything elseno heap allocation, but large structs copy on every pass and box behind interfaces
async overheadValueTask on hot paths that usually complete synchronously; no Task.Run in ASP.NET Core; no async lambda where a sync one will doevery async state machine and Task costs an allocation
serializationSystem.Text.Json with a source-generated JsonSerializerContextno reflection at run time; required for Native AOT
measureBenchmarkDotNet for code, dotnet-counters and dotnet-trace for running appsintuition about .NET performance is often wrong

Project hygiene, and a five-minute review checklist

The first five are set up once per repository; the rest are asked of every pull request.

  • Analyzers on — <AnalysisLevel>latest-recommended</AnalysisLevel> and <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild> in Directory.Build.props, with TreatWarningsAsErrors; test projects add <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);CA1707</NoWarn> so underscore test names build (see the Modularization sheet).
  • One style — a committed .editorconfig (dotnet new editorconfig) and dotnet format --verify-no-changes in CI.
  • Central package versions — Directory.Packages.props; NuGet audit warnings for vulnerable packages kept at zero (dotnet list package --vulnerable).
  • Pinned SDK and docs — a global.json for the SDK, and <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile> on libraries so a missing /// on public API is a warning.
  • CI on every pull request — dotnet build -warnaserror, dotnet test, dotnet format --verify-no-changes, on every target OS the app ships to.
  • Review: names and API — do the public names read well at the call site, return read-only types and take a CancellationToken?
  • Review: failure — what happens on timeout, cancellation, a 4xx and a 5xx? Is anything caught and swallowed?
  • Review: nulls and disposal — any new !, null! or #nullable disable? Is every created IDisposable disposed?
  • Review: tests — does a test fail without the change, and is it free of real time, network and shared state?
  • Review: accessibility — every control has a SemanticProperties.Description (MAUI) or AutomationProperties.Name (WPF, WinUI) or an accessible name (Blazor), and works by keyboard and screen reader.
  • Review: localization — user-facing text comes from .resx resources; dates, numbers and currency are formatted with a CultureInfo, and machine formats with InvariantCulture.
  • Review: privacy — no personal data, tokens or secrets in logs, exception messages, telemetry or analytics events.

Nullable references

With `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` (the template's default), dereferencing a maybe-null reference is a warning.

var user = new User("Ana", Address: null);
Console.WriteLine(user.Address?.City ?? "unknown city");
string name = user.Name;                       // non-nullable: no check needed
if (user.Address is { City: { } city }) Console.WriteLine(city);
else Console.WriteLine($"no city for {name}");

record Address(string? City);
record User(string Name, Address? Address);

Records and pattern matching

Type, positional, property and list patterns in a `switch` expression.

using System.Globalization;

static double Area(Shape s) => s switch
{
    Circle c => Math.PI * c.Radius * c.Radius,
    Rect(var w, var h) => w * h,
    _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(s)),
};

Console.WriteLine(Area(new Rect(2, 3)));
Console.WriteLine(Area(new Circle(1)).ToString("F2", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
Console.WriteLine(new[] { 1, 2, 3 } is [1, .., 3] ? "list pattern matched" : "no match");

abstract record Shape;
record Circle(double Radius) : Shape;
record Rect(double Width, double Height) : Shape;

Generics and generic math

Constraints with `where`; static abstract interface members make `T.Zero` and `+` generic (.NET 7).

using System.Numerics;

static T Clamp<T>(T value, T low, T high) where T : IComparable<T> =>
    value.CompareTo(low) < 0 ? low : value.CompareTo(high) > 0 ? high : value;

static T Sum<T>(IEnumerable<T> xs) where T : INumber<T> =>
    xs.Aggregate(T.Zero, (acc, x) => acc + x);

Console.WriteLine($"{Clamp(15, 0, 10)} {Clamp("m", "a", "f")} {Sum(new[] { 1, 2, 3 })} {Sum(new[] { 10L, 20L })}");

10 f 6 30
