Binding a store to a view model

The view model subscribes to the store, raises PropertyChanged only when the value it shows differs, sends commands as actions, and unsubscribes on Dispose so the store does not keep a closed screen alive.

using System.ComponentModel;

var store = new CartStore(new CartState(ItemCount: 8));
var badge = new CartBadgeViewModel(store);
badge.PropertyChanged += (_, e) => Console.WriteLine($"{e.PropertyName} -> {badge.BadgeText}");

for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) badge.AddItem();          // 9, 9+, then 9+ again: no third PropertyChanged
badge.Dispose();                                        // the screen closes and unsubscribes
store.Dispatch(new QuantityChanged(-5));                // 6 items: a leaked badge would print "-> 6"

sealed class CartBadgeViewModel : INotifyPropertyChanged, IDisposable
{
    private readonly CartStore store;
    public event PropertyChangedEventHandler? PropertyChanged;
    public string BadgeText { get; private set; } = "";

    public CartBadgeViewModel(CartStore store)
    {
        this.store = store;
        store.StateChanged += OnState;
    }

    public void AddItem() => store.Dispatch(new QuantityChanged(+1));  // bound as a command
    public void Dispose() => store.StateChanged -= OnState;            // else the store keeps it alive

    private void OnState(CartState state)
    {
        var text = state.ItemCount > 9 ? "9+" : $"{state.ItemCount}";  // the selected value
        if (text == BadgeText) return;                                  // raise only when it differs
        BadgeText = text;
        PropertyChanged?.Invoke(this, new PropertyChangedEventArgs(nameof(BadgeText)));
    }
}

sealed class CartStore(CartState initial)                // the minimal store, with its reducer inside
{
    public CartState State { get; private set; } = initial;
    public event Action<CartState>? StateChanged;

    public void Dispatch(CartAction action)
    {
        State = action is QuantityChanged q ? State with { ItemCount = State.ItemCount + q.Delta } : State;
        StateChanged?.Invoke(State);
    }
}

record CartState(int ItemCount);
abstract record CartAction;
sealed record QuantityChanged(int Delta) : CartAction;
Result
BadgeText -> 9
BadgeText -> 9+

The same search in Fluxor — state, reducers, effect

Fluxor finds `[FeatureState]`, `[ReducerMethod]` and `[EffectMethod]` by scanning the assembly, builds effect classes once per store with their dependencies from DI, and leaves cancelling a superseded effect to you.

// Store/SearchFeature.cs
using System.Collections.Immutable;
using Fluxor;

[FeatureState]
public record SearchState(string Query, bool IsLoading, ImmutableList<string> Results)
{
    public SearchState() : this("", false, []) { }          // Fluxor builds the initial state
}

public record SearchSubmitted(string Query);
public record ResultsLoaded(string Query, ImmutableList<string> Results);

public static class SearchReducers
{
    [ReducerMethod]
    public static SearchState OnSubmitted(SearchState state, SearchSubmitted action) =>
        state with { Query = action.Query, IsLoading = true };

    [ReducerMethod]                                          // an answer to an older query changes nothing
    public static SearchState OnLoaded(SearchState state, ResultsLoaded action) =>
        action.Query == state.Query ? state with { IsLoading = false, Results = action.Results } : state;
}

public interface ICatalogApi
{
    Task<ImmutableList<string>> SearchAsync(string query, CancellationToken token);
}

public class SearchEffects(ICatalogApi api)                 // effects get their dependencies from DI
{
    private CancellationTokenSource? inFlight;

    [EffectMethod]
    public async Task OnSubmitted(SearchSubmitted action, IDispatcher dispatcher)
    {
        inFlight?.Cancel();                                  // Fluxor does not cancel for you
        inFlight = new CancellationTokenSource();
        var token = inFlight.Token;
        try
        {
            var results = await api.SearchAsync(action.Query, token);
            if (!token.IsCancellationRequested) dispatcher.Dispatch(new ResultsLoaded(action.Query, results));
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException) { }              // superseded by a newer query
    }
}
Result

Dispatching SearchSubmitted shows the spinner, cancels the previous search, and ResultsLoaded fills the list, while an answer to an older query is ignored.

  2. dotnet add package Fluxor.Blazor.Web (6.x); in Program.cs builder.Services.AddFluxor(o => o.ScanAssemblies(typeof(Program).Assembly)); and register your ICatalogApi
  3. @using Fluxor in Components/_Imports.razor, and <Fluxor.Blazor.Web.StoreInitializer /> at the top of Components/Routes.razor

The Fluxor page: IState<T> in, IDispatcher out

A FluxorComponent re-renders when the injected `IState<T>` changes, and the page only ever dispatches actions.

@* Components/Pages/SearchPage.razor *@
@page "/search"
@inherits Fluxor.Blazor.Web.Components.FluxorComponent
@inject IState<SearchState> SearchState
@inject IDispatcher Dispatcher

<input @bind="query" @bind:event="oninput" @bind:after="Submit" placeholder="Search products" />
@if (SearchState.Value.IsLoading) { <p>Searching…</p> }
<ul>@foreach (var name in SearchState.Value.Results) { <li>@name</li> }</ul>

@code {
    private string query = "";
    private void Submit() => Dispatcher.Dispatch(new SearchSubmitted(query));
}

MVU-style options in .NET MAUI

XAML MAUI is MVVM; to get a unidirectional loop you either put a store behind your view models or pick an MVU library.

OptionShapeStatus
A store behind MVVM view models (this sheet's Store, or Fluxor core)XAML binds to view models that subscribe to the store and dispatch actionsplain .NET: works everywhere, the usual choice
MauiReactor (Reactor.Maui)C# components: Component<TState>, SetState(s => …), Render() builds the treecommunity, actively maintained
Fabulous (Fabulous.MauiControls)F# MVU: init, update, viewcommunity; F# only
CometC# MVU prototype from the .NET teamexperimental, not for production
Blazor Hybrid (BlazorWebView) + FluxorRazor components inside a MAUI app; Fluxor as on the webBlazor Hybrid is supported by Microsoft, Fluxor is community; the UI is HTML, not native controls

Testing a reducer and an effect

A reducer test is a call and an assertion, and an effect test runs the effect against a fake API — including one superseded while it awaits — and records what it dispatched (in xUnit, each check is a `[Fact]`).

var idle = new SearchState("", false, []);

var loading = Search.Reduce(idle, new QueryChanged("desk"));
Check("submitting shows the spinner", loading == idle with { Query = "desk", IsLoading = true });

var stale = Search.Reduce(loading, new ResultsLoaded("de", ["Desk lamp"]));
Check("an answer to an older query is ignored", stale == loading);

var dispatched = new List<SearchAction>();
await Search.SearchEffect("desk", (_, _) => Task.FromResult<IReadOnlyList<string>>(["Oak desk", "Bench"]),
    dispatched.Add, CancellationToken.None);
Check("the effect dispatches the results", dispatched is [ResultsLoaded { Query: "desk", Results.Count: 2 }]);

dispatched.Clear();
var answer = new TaskCompletionSource<IReadOnlyList<string>>();
using var superseded = new CancellationTokenSource();
var running = Search.SearchEffect("desk", (_, _) => answer.Task, dispatched.Add, superseded.Token);
superseded.Cancel();                                       // a newer query arrives while it awaits…
answer.SetResult(["Oak desk"]);                            // …and the server answers anyway
await running;
Check("a superseded effect dispatches nothing", dispatched.Count == 0);

static void Check(string name, bool passed) => Console.WriteLine($"{(passed ? "PASS" : "FAIL")} {name}");

static class Search
{
    public static SearchState Reduce(SearchState state, SearchAction action) => action switch
    {
        QueryChanged q => state with { Query = q.Query, IsLoading = true },
        ResultsLoaded r when r.Query == state.Query => state with { IsLoading = false, Results = r.Results },
        _ => state,
    };

    public static async Task SearchEffect(string query,
        Func<string, CancellationToken, Task<IReadOnlyList<string>>> search,
        Action<SearchAction> dispatch, CancellationToken token)
    {
        var results = await search(query, token);
        if (!token.IsCancellationRequested) dispatch(new ResultsLoaded(query, results));   // superseded: drop
    }
}

record SearchState(string Query, bool IsLoading, IReadOnlyList<string> Results);
abstract record SearchAction;
sealed record QueryChanged(string Query) : SearchAction;
sealed record ResultsLoaded(string Query, IReadOnlyList<string> Results) : SearchAction;
Result
PASS submitting shows the spinner
PASS an answer to an older query is ignored
PASS the effect dispatches the results
PASS a superseded effect dispatches nothing

Rules and pitfalls

The loop only pays off if nothing goes around it.

  • Reducers are pure and synchronous: no await, no DateTime.Now, no Random, no I/O. Pass the time or an id in the action instead.
  • Effects never touch state; they dispatch actions. Cancel the superseded effect and drop what it still sends: an answer can arrive after the cancel, so check the token after every await.
  • Inject dependencies (API clients, TimeProvider) into effects, so tests pass fakes and the reducer stays dependency-free.
  • Mutating state in place (state.Lines.Add(x) on a List<T>, a settable property): the store sees the same reference and no view updates. Use records and immutable collections.
  • Comparing records that hold collections and expecting value equality: ImmutableList<T> and arrays compare by reference. Compare contents in tests, or keep the same instance when nothing changed.
  • Dispatching from a thread-pool continuation (an effect using ConfigureAwait(false), a timer callback): marshal to the UI thread first — WinUI and MAUI on Android and iOS throw, and WPF forwards PropertyChanged itself but throws on collection changes.
  • Setter actions (SetLoading, SetResults): the rules leak into every view. Name events (SearchSubmitted, ResultsLoaded).
  • Selectors recompute only when their input reference changes; with immutable data that check is a cheap ReferenceEquals.
  • One store for the app, or one per feature: both work. Keep transient UI state (a text box's caret, an expanded row) in the view, not the store.

Networking — REST with HttpClient

Typed JSON calls, one long-lived client, errors as values, timeouts, retry and token refresh in DelegatingHandlers, pagination, ETags and progress — every runnable piece tested through a fake HttpMessageHandler.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12
  • dotnet >=8
  • .NET (System.Net.Http, System.Net.Http.Json); the same code runs in .NET MAUI, WPF, WinUI and Blazor

Sources: Make HTTP requests with the HttpClient class — .NET · HttpClient guidelines for .NET · IHttpClientFactory with .NET · Build resilient HTTP apps — .NET

The pieces of HttpClient, and what you add

`HttpClient` is a thin front over a handler pipeline, so cross-cutting behaviour (retry, auth, logging) goes in a `DelegatingHandler`, never in each call.

PieceWhat it gives youWhat you add
HttpClientGetAsync / SendAsync, BaseAddress, DefaultRequestHeaders, Timeout (100 s by default)one long-lived instance (or a factory); per-call headers on an HttpRequestMessage
System.Net.Http.JsonGetFromJsonAsync, PostAsJsonAsync, ReadFromJsonAsync with web defaults (camelCase, case-insensitive)a typed error model: GetFromJsonAsync throws on a non-success status, the others hand you the response
SocketsHttpHandlerthe connection pool, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, TLS — the default on desktop and serverPooledConnectionLifetime so a long-lived client sees DNS changes; on MAUI Android and iOS keep the platform handler
DelegatingHandlera link in the pipeline that sees every request and responseretry with backoff, bearer tokens and refresh, logging, a fake in tests
IHttpClientFactorypooled handlers with a managed lifetime, typed clients, DIAddHttpClient<T>(), Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience
HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersReadreturns once headers arrive instead of buffering the bodystreamed downloads with progress — and disposing the response
MultipartFormDataContenta file plus form fields in one requestStreamContent(File.OpenRead(path)) as one part; wrap it in a progress-reporting content for progress
HTTP cachingSocketsHttpHandler keeps no HTTP cache; in Blazor WebAssembly fetch goes through the browser'sETags and If-None-Match by hand; SetBrowserRequestCache per request in Blazor WebAssembly
Blazor WebAssemblyHttpClient runs on the browser's fetch: no sockets, CORS appliesthe HttpClient the template registers; never a secret in the request

A typed GET and POST

`GetFromJsonAsync` throws `HttpRequestException` on a non-2xx status, so when a 404 is an expected answer take the response and read the status yourself.

using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Net.Http.Json;

using var http = new HttpClient(new FakeShop()) { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://shop.example/api/") };
http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Accept.Add(new MediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue("application/json"));
http.DefaultRequestHeaders.UserAgent.ParseAdd("OrdersApp/1.0");

// A relative path with no leading slash; throws on a non-2xx status.
Order? order = await http.GetFromJsonAsync<Order>("orders/o-1");
Console.WriteLine($"{order!.Id} is {order.Status}");

using var created = await http.PostAsJsonAsync("orders", new NewOrder("sku-42", 2));
created.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
var saved = await created.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<Order>();
Console.WriteLine($"{(int)created.StatusCode} {saved!.Id} at {created.Headers.Location}");

// A status you expect is an answer, not an exception: read it.
using var missing = await http.GetAsync("orders/o-9");
if (missing.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.NotFound) Console.WriteLine("o-9: not found");

try { await http.GetFromJsonAsync<Order>("orders/o-9"); }
catch (HttpRequestException e) { Console.WriteLine($"GetFromJsonAsync threw, status {e.StatusCode}"); }

record Order(string Id, string Sku, string Status);

record NewOrder(string Sku, int Quantity);

// The test seam: HttpClient sends through whatever handler it is given.
sealed class FakeShop : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var path = request.RequestUri!.AbsolutePath;
        if (request.Method == HttpMethod.Post && path == "/api/orders")
        {
            var draft = (await request.Content!.ReadFromJsonAsync<NewOrder>(ct))!;
            var reply = new HttpResponseMessage(HttpStatusCode.Created);
            reply.Content = JsonContent.Create(new Order("o-2", draft.Sku, "pending"));
            reply.Headers.Location = new Uri("/api/orders/o-2", UriKind.Relative);
            return reply;
        }
        if (path != "/api/orders/o-1") return new HttpResponseMessage(HttpStatusCode.NotFound);
        return new HttpResponseMessage { Content = JsonContent.Create(new Order("o-1", "sku-7", "shipped")) };
    }
}

201 o-2 at /api/orders/o-2

Errors as values — problem details and unreadable bodies

Map every HTTP outcome a screen must handle to one result type, including the 200 whose body is a proxy's HTML page, `null`, half an order or in an unknown charset.

using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Net.Http.Json;
using System.Text.Json;

var strict = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web)     // nulls or gaps in a 200: refused
    { RespectRequiredConstructorParameters = true, RespectNullableAnnotations = true };
HttpResponseMessage[] replies =
[
    Reply(200, "application/json", """{"id":"o-1","status":"shipped"}"""),
    Reply(404, "application/problem+json", """{"title":"Order not found"}"""),
    Reply(200, "text/html", "<html>Back soon</html>"),                     // a proxy's maintenance page
    Reply(200, "application/json", "null"),
    Reply(200, "application/json", """{"id":"o-1"}"""),                   // half an order
    Reply(200, "application/json; charset=klingon", """{"id":"o-1","status":"shipped"}"""),
];
foreach (var reply in replies)
    Console.WriteLine(await ReadOrder(reply, strict, CancellationToken.None));

static async Task<ApiResult> ReadOrder(
    HttpResponseMessage response, JsonSerializerOptions options, CancellationToken ct)
{
    try
    {
        if (response.IsSuccessStatusCode)
            return await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<Order>(options, ct) is { } order
                ? new Ok(order) : new Unreadable();
        var isProblem = response.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType == "application/problem+json";
        var problem = isProblem ? await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<Problem>(ct) : null;
        return new Failed((int)response.StatusCode, problem?.Title ?? response.ReasonPhrase);
    }
    catch (Exception e) when (e is JsonException or InvalidOperationException) { return new Unreadable(); }
}

static HttpResponseMessage Reply(int status, string type, string body) =>
    new((HttpStatusCode)status) { Content = new StringContent(body, MediaTypeHeaderValue.Parse(type)) };

abstract record ApiResult;

record Ok(Order Order) : ApiResult;

record Failed(int Status, string? Title) : ApiResult;

record Unreadable : ApiResult;

record Order(string Id, string Status);

record Problem(string? Title, string? Detail);    // RFC 9457 problem details

Failed { Status = 404, Title = Order not found }

Timeouts, cancellation and being offline

A timeout and the user leaving both throw `OperationCanceledException`, so tell them apart by the caller's token, and give each its own message.

using System.Net;

var api = new OrdersApi(new HttpClient(new SlowOrDown()) { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://shop.example/") });
Console.WriteLine(await api.GetStatus("o-slow"));
Console.WriteLine(await api.GetStatus("o-down"));

using var leaving = new CancellationTokenSource();
leaving.Cancel();
try { await api.GetStatus("o-1", leaving.Token); }
catch (OperationCanceledException) { Console.WriteLine("cancelled by the caller: show nothing"); }

sealed class OrdersApi(HttpClient http)
{
    public async Task<string> GetStatus(string id, CancellationToken ct = default)
    {
        // HttpClient.Timeout caps every call (100 s by default); a linked source sets this call's budget.
        using var perCall = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct);
        perCall.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(200));
        try
        {
            using var response = await http.GetAsync($"orders/{id}", perCall.Token);
            return $"status {(int)response.StatusCode}";
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            return "timed out: offer Retry";
        }
        catch (HttpRequestException e) { return $"offline ({e.HttpRequestError}): show the cached copy"; }
    }
}

sealed class SlowOrDown : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (request.RequestUri!.AbsolutePath == "/orders/o-down")
            throw new HttpRequestException(HttpRequestError.NameResolutionError);
        await Task.Delay(Timeout.Infinite, ct);
        return new HttpResponseMessage(HttpStatusCode.OK);
    }
}
Result
timed out: offer Retry
offline (NameResolutionError): show the cached copy
cancelled by the caller: show nothing

Retry with backoff in a DelegatingHandler

Retry only what is safe to repeat and never the caller's cancellation, free the failed response before waiting, and take the delay from an injected policy (next card) so the test sleeps for nothing.

using System.Net;

var replies = new Queue<Func<HttpResponseMessage>>([
    () => throw new HttpRequestException("connection reset"),
    () => new(HttpStatusCode.ServiceUnavailable),
    () => new(HttpStatusCode.OK),
]);
var retry = new RetryHandler(
    nextDelay: (_, attempt) => TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(50 * Math.Pow(2, attempt)),   // RetryDelays.Next
    sleep: (wait, _) => Console.Out.WriteLineAsync($"waited {wait.TotalMilliseconds} ms"))   // Task.Delay
    { InnerHandler = new Scripted(replies) };
var scripted = replies.Count;
using var response = await new HttpClient(retry).GetAsync("https://shop.example/orders");
Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode} after {scripted - replies.Count} attempts");

sealed class RetryHandler(Func<HttpResponseMessage?, int, TimeSpan?> nextDelay,
    Func<TimeSpan, CancellationToken, Task> sleep, int retries = 4) : DelegatingHandler
{
    protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var safe = request.Method.Method is not ("POST" or "PATCH")
            || request.Headers.Contains("Idempotency-Key");
        for (var attempt = 0; ; attempt++)
        {
            HttpResponseMessage? response;
            try { response = await base.SendAsync(request, ct); }
            catch (HttpRequestException) when (safe && attempt < retries) { response = null; }

            if (response is { } r && (!safe || attempt == retries || !IsTransient(r))) return r;
            if (nextDelay(response, attempt) is not { } wait)
                return response ?? throw new HttpRequestException("gave up after a network failure");
            response?.Dispose();                                                  // free the connection first
            await sleep(wait, ct);
        }
    }

    static bool IsTransient(HttpResponseMessage r) => (int)r.StatusCode is 408 or 429 or (>= 502 and <= 504);
}

sealed class Scripted(Queue<Func<HttpResponseMessage>> replies) : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
        => Task.FromResult(replies.Dequeue()());
}
Result
waited 50 ms
waited 100 ms
200 after 3 attempts

The delay policy: Retry-After, a cap, exponential backoff and jitter

Wait what the server asks for (seconds or an HTTP date) unless it is longer than the cap, in which case give up and show the error, and otherwise back off exponentially with full jitter.

using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Headers;

var now = DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch;
var delays = new RetryDelays(new FixedClock(now), random: () => 0.5, cap: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));

Show("network failure, attempt 0", null, 0);
Show("503, attempt 3", new(HttpStatusCode.ServiceUnavailable), 3);
Show("503, Retry-After: 2", Hinted(new(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2))), 1);
Show("503, Retry-After: <a date 5 s away>", Hinted(new(now.AddSeconds(5))), 1);
Show("503, Retry-After: 3600", Hinted(new(TimeSpan.FromHours(1))), 1);

void Show(string reply, HttpResponseMessage? response, int attempt)
{
    var next = delays.Next(response, attempt);
    Console.WriteLine($"{reply} -> {(next is { } wait ? $"wait {wait.TotalMilliseconds} ms" : "give up")}");
}

static HttpResponseMessage Hinted(RetryConditionHeaderValue retryAfter) =>
    new(HttpStatusCode.ServiceUnavailable) { Headers = { RetryAfter = retryAfter } };

sealed class RetryDelays(TimeProvider time, Func<double> random, TimeSpan cap)
{
    // null means "stop retrying": return the response and let the screen show it.
    public TimeSpan? Next(HttpResponseMessage? response, int attempt)
    {
        var after = response?.Headers.RetryAfter;                       // seconds, or an HTTP date
        var hint = after?.Delta ?? after?.Date - time.GetUtcNow();
        if (hint > cap) return null;                                    // don't sleep for an hour
        if (hint is { } wait) return wait > TimeSpan.Zero ? wait : TimeSpan.Zero;
        var ceiling = Math.Min(cap.TotalMilliseconds, 100 * Math.Pow(2, attempt));   // exponential, capped
        return TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(random() * ceiling);                        // "full jitter"
    }
}

sealed class FixedClock(DateTimeOffset now) : TimeProvider
{
    public override DateTimeOffset GetUtcNow() => now;
}
Result
network failure, attempt 0 -> wait 50 ms
503, attempt 3 -> wait 400 ms
503, Retry-After: 2 -> wait 2000 ms
503, Retry-After: <a date 5 s away> -> wait 5000 ms
503, Retry-After: 3600 -> give up

IHttpClientFactory: a typed client with the standard resilience pipeline

In a MAUI, Blazor or ASP.NET Core host, register a typed client and let the factory own the handlers (no socket exhaustion, no stale DNS) and one resilience pipeline that does the two retry cards' work.

using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience;

// Called from MauiProgram.CreateMauiApp or Program.cs: builder.Services.AddShopApi();
public static class ShopServices
{
    public static IServiceCollection AddShopApi(this IServiceCollection services)
    {
        services.AddHttpClient<OrdersApi>(client => client.BaseAddress = new Uri("https://shop.example/api/"))
            .AddStandardResilienceHandler(options =>
            {
                // Rate limit, total timeout, retry, circuit breaker, attempt timeout: one handler, never two.
                options.Retry.DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods();             // never replay a POST by accident
                options.Retry.MaxRetryAttempts = 4;
                options.AttemptTimeout.Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);
            });
        return services;
    }
}

// Typed clients are transient: inject them where needed, and never capture one in a singleton.
public sealed class OrdersApi(HttpClient http)
{
    public Task<string> GetOrderJson(string id, CancellationToken ct) =>
        http.GetStringAsync($"orders/{id}", ct);
}
Result

OrdersApi gets a factory-managed HttpClient behind rate limiting, a total timeout, up to 4 retries of safe methods with jittered exponential backoff, a circuit breaker and a 5-second attempt timeout.

A single-flight token refresh, whatever its outcome

When five requests find the token expired at once they join one in-flight refresh task under a lock, so one call to the token endpoint gives all five the same outcome: the new token, "signed out", or the network error.

foreach (var outcome in new[] { "ok", "revoked", "unreachable" })
{
    var tokens = new TokenStore("t-expired", async () =>
    {
        await Task.Delay(50);                                     // POST grant_type=refresh_token in the app
        if (outcome == "revoked") throw new SignedOutException();                   // 400 invalid_grant
        if (outcome == "unreachable") throw new HttpRequestException("token endpoint down");
        return "t-fresh";
    });
    var results = await Task.WhenAll(Enumerable.Range(0, 5).Select(async _ =>
    {
        try { return await tokens.RefreshAsync("t-expired", CancellationToken.None); }
        catch (SignedOutException) { return "signed out"; }
        catch (HttpRequestException) { return "network error"; }
    }));
    Console.WriteLine($"{outcome}: {string.Join(",", results)}; token endpoint calls: {tokens.RefreshCalls}");
}

sealed class TokenStore(string initial, Func<Task<string>> refresh)
{
    private readonly Lock gate = new();
    private Task<string>? inFlight;
    public string Current { get; private set; } = initial;
    public int RefreshCalls { get; private set; }

    public Task<string> RefreshAsync(string rejected, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        lock (gate)
        {
            if (Current != rejected) return Task.FromResult(Current);            // refreshed meanwhile
            if (inFlight is not { IsCompleted: false }) inFlight = RunAsync();   // else join the one running
            return inFlight.WaitAsync(ct);               // one caller's cancellation leaves the rest waiting
        }
    }

    // Every joiner gets the same outcome: the new token, SignedOutException, or the network error.
    private async Task<string> RunAsync()
    {
        RefreshCalls++;
        return Current = await refresh();
    }
}

sealed class SignedOutException() : Exception("The session ended: sign in again.");
Result
ok: t-fresh,t-fresh,t-fresh,t-fresh,t-fresh; token endpoint calls: 1
revoked: signed out,signed out,signed out,signed out,signed out; token endpoint calls: 1
unreachable: network error,network error,network error,network error,network error; token endpoint calls: 1

Bearer auth in a DelegatingHandler, retried once on 401

The handler attaches the token, refreshes through the previous card's store on a 401 and resends once, so a second 401 or a `SignedOutException` reaches the caller as "sign in again".

using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Headers;

var tokens = new FakeTokens(current: "t-expired", afterRefresh: "t-fresh");
using var http = new HttpClient(new BearerHandler(tokens) { InnerHandler = new AcceptsOnly("t-fresh") });
using var response = await http.GetAsync("https://shop.example/orders");
Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode}, now holding {tokens.Current}");

interface ITokenSource
{
    string Current { get; }
    Task<string> RefreshAsync(string rejected, CancellationToken ct);   // TokenStore in the app
}

sealed class BearerHandler(ITokenSource tokens) : DelegatingHandler
{
    protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var sent = tokens.Current;
        request.Headers.Authorization = new("Bearer", sent);
        var response = await base.SendAsync(request, ct);
        if (response.StatusCode != HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized) return response;

        response.Dispose();                                   // the refresh may throw SignedOutException
        request.Headers.Authorization = new("Bearer", await tokens.RefreshAsync(sent, ct));
        return await base.SendAsync(request, ct);                       // a second 401 reaches the caller
    }
}

sealed class FakeTokens(string current, string afterRefresh) : ITokenSource
{
    public string Current { get; private set; } = current;

    public Task<string> RefreshAsync(string rejected, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        Current = afterRefresh;
        return Task.FromResult(Current);
    }
}

sealed class AcceptsOnly(string token) : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
        => Task.FromResult(new HttpResponseMessage(request.Headers.Authorization?.Parameter == token
            ? HttpStatusCode.OK : HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized));
}

Cursor pagination as an IAsyncEnumerable

The caller writes `await foreach` and never sees pages, and stopping early stops fetching because each page is requested only when the previous one is used up.

using System.Net.Http.Json;
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;
using System.Web;

var server = new FakePagedOrders(total: 7);
using var http = new HttpClient(server) { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://shop.example/") };

var shown = new List<string>();
await foreach (var order in AllOrders(http))
{
    shown.Add(order.Id);
    if (shown.Count == 3) break;                                       // one screen's worth
}
Console.WriteLine($"{string.Join(",", shown)} from {server.PagesServed} pages");

static async IAsyncEnumerable<Order> AllOrders(
    HttpClient http, [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken ct = default)
{
    string? cursor = null;
    do
    {
        var url = cursor is null ? "orders?limit=2" : $"orders?limit=2&cursor={Uri.EscapeDataString(cursor)}";
        var page = await http.GetFromJsonAsync<Page<Order>>(url, ct);
        foreach (var order in page!.Items) yield return order;
        cursor = page.NextCursor;
    } while (cursor is not null);
}

record Order(string Id);

record Page<T>(T[] Items, string? NextCursor);

sealed class FakePagedOrders(int total) : HttpMessageHandler
{
    public int PagesServed { get; private set; }

    protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        PagesServed++;
        var query = HttpUtility.ParseQueryString(request.RequestUri!.Query);
        var start = int.Parse(query["cursor"] ?? "0");
        var count = Math.Min(int.Parse(query["limit"]!), total - start);
        var items = Enumerable.Range(start + 1, count).Select(i => new Order($"o-{i}")).ToArray();
        var page = new Page<Order>(items, start + count < total ? $"{start + count}" : null);
        return Task.FromResult(new HttpResponseMessage { Content = JsonContent.Create(page) });
    }
}
Result
o-1,o-2,o-3 from 2 pages

Caching with ETag and If-None-Match

`SocketsHttpHandler` keeps no HTTP cache, so store the body with its `ETag` and send `If-None-Match`: a `304 Not Modified` costs a round trip but no body.

using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Net.Http.Json;

var server = new FakeCatalog();
var catalog = new CatalogCache(new HttpClient(server) { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://shop.example/") });
Console.WriteLine((await catalog.GetAsync()).Length + " products");
Console.WriteLine((await catalog.GetAsync()).Length + " products");      // revalidated: no body sent
server.Current = (2, ["Mug", "Tee", "Cap"]);                                // the catalog changes
Console.WriteLine((await catalog.GetAsync()).Length + " products");

sealed class CatalogCache(HttpClient http)
{
    private EntityTagHeaderValue? etag;
    private string[] products = [];

    public async Task<string[]> GetAsync(CancellationToken ct = default)
    {
        using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "products");
        if (etag is not null) request.Headers.IfNoneMatch.Add(etag);
        using var response = await http.SendAsync(request, ct);
        Console.Write($"{(int)response.StatusCode} -> ");
        if (response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.NotModified) return products;
        response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
        products = (await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<string[]>(ct))!;
        etag = response.Headers.ETag;
        return products;
    }
}

sealed class FakeCatalog : HttpMessageHandler
{
    public (int Version, string[] Products) Current { get; set; } = (1, ["Mug", "Tee"]);

    protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var current = new EntityTagHeaderValue($"\"v{Current.Version}\"");
        var response = request.Headers.IfNoneMatch.Contains(current)
            ? new HttpResponseMessage(HttpStatusCode.NotModified)
            : new HttpResponseMessage { Content = JsonContent.Create(Current.Products) };
        response.Headers.ETag = current;
        return Task.FromResult(response);
    }
}

Upload and download with progress, cancellable

Download with `ResponseHeadersRead` and copy the stream in chunks, upload through an `HttpContent` that reports as it writes, and pass the screen's token everywhere so leaving stops the transfer.

using var http = new HttpClient(new FakeFiles()) { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://files.example/") };
var ct = CancellationToken.None;                       // the screen's token: leaving stops the transfer

using var response = await http.GetAsync(
    "invoices/2026-10.pdf", HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, ct);
response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
var total = response.Content.Headers.ContentLength;                   // null: show an indeterminate bar
await using var body = await response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(ct);
var buffer = new byte[64 * 1024];
long received = 0;
for (int read; (read = await body.ReadAsync(buffer, ct)) > 0;)
{
    received += read;                                                 // write buffer[..read] to the file
    Console.WriteLine(total > 0 ? $"download {received * 100 / total}%" : $"download {received} bytes");
}

var receipt = new ProgressContent(new byte[40 * 1024], sent => Console.WriteLine($"upload {sent / 1024} KB"));
using var posted = await http.PostAsync("receipts", receipt, ct);   // report: an IProgress<long> in an app
Console.WriteLine($"upload: {(int)posted.StatusCode}");

sealed class ProgressContent(byte[] data, Action<long> report) : ByteArrayContent(data)   // knows its length
{
    private readonly byte[] bytes = data;

    protected override async Task SerializeToStreamAsync(
        Stream stream, System.Net.TransportContext? context, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        for (var offset = 0; offset < bytes.Length; offset += 16 * 1024)
        {
            var chunk = bytes.AsMemory(offset, Math.Min(16 * 1024, bytes.Length - offset));
            await stream.WriteAsync(chunk, ct);
            report(offset + chunk.Length);
        }
    }
}

sealed class FakeFiles : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (request.Content is not null) await request.Content.CopyToAsync(Stream.Null, ct);
        return new() { Content = new ByteArrayContent(new byte[200 * 1024]) };
    }
}

Pitfalls worth saying out loud

Most HttpClient incidents in production are one of these.

  • new HttpClient() per request in a using: each disposal leaves a socket in TIME_WAIT, and under load the machine runs out of ports (socket exhaustion).
  • One static client over the default handler with no PooledConnectionLifetime: connections live forever and never see a DNS change after a failover. Without DI: new HttpClient(new SocketsHttpHandler { PooledConnectionLifetime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2) }), kept for the app's life.
  • .Result or .Wait() on an HTTP call (sync-over-async): it blocks the UI thread in MAUI, WPF or WinUI, can deadlock, and starves the thread pool on a server. await all the way up.
  • Not disposing HttpResponseMessage — above all with ResponseHeadersRead — keeps the connection checked out of the pool until the GC finds it.
  • Catching TaskCanceledException and calling it a timeout: check the caller's token first, or a user who left the screen sees an error.
  • Mutating DefaultRequestHeaders after the first request: it is shared and not thread-safe. Per-call headers belong on the HttpRequestMessage.
  • BaseAddress needs a trailing slash and request paths none: https://x/api + orders resolves to https://x/orders.
  • On MAUI Android and iOS the default handler is the platform's (AndroidMessageHandler, NSUrlSessionHandler): share one HttpClient there too, but don't swap in SocketsHttpHandler without a reason.
  • Retry only idempotent requests (or a POST with an Idempotency-Key), with capped, jittered backoff, and keep one resilience handler per client.
  • Test through a fake HttpMessageHandler or DelegatingHandler: no network, no mocking library, and the same pipeline the app runs.

Networking — SOAP, gRPC & GraphQL

SOAP envelopes with XDocument or a dotnet-svcutil proxy, GraphQL over plain HttpClient or StrawberryShake, gRPC with Grpc.Net.Client (and gRPC-Web for Blazor WebAssembly), SignalR for push — and which one to choose.

  • dotnet
  • csharp >=12
  • dotnet >=8
  • .NET (System.Net.Http, System.Xml.Linq, System.Text.Json); gRPC and WCF clients need their NuGet packages

Sources: Overview of gRPC on .NET · Call gRPC services with the .NET client · WCF dotnet-svcutil tool overview — .NET · GraphQL over HTTP · SOAP 1.1 — W3C Note

What goes over the wire

All three ride on HTTP, but each has its own envelope and its own place for errors: read the error where the protocol puts it, not only the HTTP status.

ProtocolRequestErrors arrive asThe .NET client
SOAP 1.1POST of an XML Envelope; Content-Type: text/xml, a SOAPAction headera soap:Fault in the body, with HTTP 500XDocument + HttpClient, or a dotnet-svcutil proxy (System.ServiceModel.Http)
SOAP 1.2Content-Type: application/soap+xml; action="…", no SOAPActionenv:Fault with Code / Reasonthe same; BasicHttpBinding is 1.1, a CustomBinding gives 1.2
GraphQLPOST of JSON { query, variables, operationName } to one endpointerrors beside data, usually with HTTP 200; data may be partialHttpClient + System.Text.Json, or StrawberryShake (generated, typed)
gRPCHTTP/2 POST /package.Service/Method, Protobuf framesa grpc-status trailer: RpcException.StatusCodeGrpc.Net.Client with stubs generated by Grpc.Tools; gRPC-Web in the browser
SignalRa WebSocket (or SSE / long polling) to a hub; JSON or MessagePack messagesa faulted InvokeAsync task, the Closed eventMicrosoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Client HubConnection

SOAP: build the envelope and POST it with the right headers

For one or two operations without WSDL tooling, `XElement` and `HttpClient` are shorter than a generated proxy, and the namespaces and the quoted `SOAPAction` are the parts people get wrong.

using System.Xml.Linq;

XNamespace soap = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/";
XNamespace ord = "urn:shop:orders";
using var http = new HttpClient(new WireLog()) { BaseAddress = new("https://legacy.shop.example/") };

// XElement escapes values (quotes, ampersands): never build SOAP XML by concatenation.
var envelope = new XElement(soap + "Envelope", new XAttribute(XNamespace.Xmlns + "soap", soap),
    new XElement(soap + "Body",
        new XElement(ord + "GetOrderStatus", new XElement(ord + "orderId", "o-1 & co"))));

using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "OrderService.asmx");
request.Content = new StringContent(envelope.ToString(SaveOptions.DisableFormatting), null, "text/xml");
request.Headers.Add("SOAPAction", "\"urn:shop:orders/GetOrderStatus\"");      // SOAP 1.1: required, quoted
// SOAP 1.2 instead: Content-Type application/soap+xml; action="urn:shop:orders/GetOrderStatus"
using var response = await http.SendAsync(request);                           // read it as the next card does

// Prints what goes over the wire.
sealed class WireLog : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"POST {request.RequestUri!.AbsolutePath}");
        Console.WriteLine($"Content-Type: {request.Content!.Headers.ContentType}");
        Console.WriteLine($"SOAPAction: {request.Headers.GetValues("SOAPAction").Single()}");
        Console.WriteLine(await request.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(ct));
        return new HttpResponseMessage();
    }
}
Result
POST /OrderService.asmx
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8
SOAPAction: "urn:shop:orders/GetOrderStatus"
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"><soap:Body><GetOrderStatus xmlns="urn:shop:orders"><orderId>o-1 &amp; co</orderId></GetOrderStatus></soap:Body></soap:Envelope>

SOAP: read the response, a Fault, or a reply that is not SOAP

A SOAP 1.1 fault arrives with HTTP 500, so parse the XML before checking the status, but only after checking that the reply is XML at all.

using System.Net;
using System.Xml.Linq;

XNamespace soap = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/";
XNamespace ord = "urn:shop:orders";
var ok = Envelope(new XElement(ord + "GetOrderStatusResponse", new XElement(ord + "status", "shipped")));
var fault = Envelope(new XElement(soap + "Fault",
    new XElement("faultcode", "soap:Client"), new XElement("faultstring", "Unknown order o-9")));

var gateway = Reply(502, "text/html", "<h1>Bad gateway</h1>");
foreach (var reply in new[] { Reply(200, "text/xml", ok), Reply(500, "text/xml", fault), gateway })
{
    try
    {
        var body = await ReadBodyAsync(reply);
        Console.WriteLine("status: " + (string?)body.Descendants(ord + "status").SingleOrDefault());
    }
    catch (SoapFaultException e) { Console.WriteLine($"fault {e.Code}: {e.Message}"); }
    catch (HttpRequestException e) { Console.WriteLine($"not a SOAP reply: HTTP {(int?)e.StatusCode}"); }
}

async Task<XElement> ReadBodyAsync(HttpResponseMessage response)
{
    // A fault comes with 500 (SOAP 1.2 Sender fault: 400): parse before the status, but only XML.
    var type = response.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType;
    if (type is not ("text/xml" or "application/soap+xml"))
        throw new HttpRequestException("not a SOAP reply", null, response.StatusCode);
    var body = XDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()).Root!.Element(soap + "Body")!;
    if (body.Element(soap + "Fault") is { } f)
        throw new SoapFaultException((string?)f.Element("faultcode"), (string?)f.Element("faultstring"));
    response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
    return body;
}

string Envelope(XElement content) =>
    new XElement(soap + "Envelope", new XAttribute(XNamespace.Xmlns + "soap", soap),
        new XElement(soap + "Body", content)).ToString(SaveOptions.DisableFormatting);

static HttpResponseMessage Reply(int status, string type, string body) =>
    new((HttpStatusCode)status) { Content = new StringContent(body, null, type) };

sealed class SoapFaultException(string? code, string? reason) : Exception(reason)
{
    public string? Code => code;
}
Result
status: shipped
fault soap:Client: Unknown order o-9
not a SOAP reply: HTTP 502

SOAP: a generated proxy with dotnet-svcutil

For a large WSDL, generate the client (typed requests, the SOAP plumbing done, faults as `FaultException`), and abort rather than close a client whose channel faulted.

using System.ServiceModel;
using ServiceReference;                                            // the namespace dotnet-svcutil generated

var client = new OrderServiceClient(
    new BasicHttpBinding(BasicHttpSecurityMode.Transport) { SendTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15) },
    new EndpointAddress("https://legacy.shop.example/OrderService.svc"));
try
{
    string status = await client.GetOrderStatusAsync("o-1");      // the operation's generated Async method
    Console.WriteLine(status);
    await client.CloseAsync();
}
catch (FaultException<OrderFault> fault)                           // a fault the contract declares
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{fault.Detail.Reason} ({fault.Code.Name})");
    client.Abort();
}
catch (FaultException fault)                                       // any other soap:Fault
{
    Console.WriteLine(fault.Message);
    client.Abort();
}
catch (Exception e) when (e is CommunicationException or TimeoutException)   // transport failure, timeout
{
    client.Abort();
    throw;
}
Result

Prints the order's status, or the fault's reason; the client is closed on success and aborted after a fault or a transport failure.

Setup
  1. dotnet tool install --global dotnet-svcutil, then dotnet-svcutil https://legacy.shop.example/OrderService.svc?wsdl in the project folder
  2. It writes ServiceReference/Reference.cs and adds the WCF client packages (System.ServiceModel.Http, System.ServiceModel.Primitives)

GraphQL: a typed query with variables over HttpClient

One `POST` of `{ query, variables }` to one endpoint, with values sent as `variables` and never formatted into the query text.

using System.Net.Http.Json;
using System.Text.Json;

using var http = new HttpClient(new FakeGraphQL()) { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://shop.example/") };
var gql = new GraphQLClient(http);

// Values travel in "variables", never formatted into the query text.
const string GetOrder = "query GetOrder($id: ID!) { order(id: $id) { id status } }";
var result = await gql.SendAsync<OrderData>(GetOrder, new { id = "o-1" });
Console.WriteLine($"order {result.Data?.Order?.Id}: {result.Data?.Order?.Status}");

sealed class GraphQLClient(HttpClient http)
{
    public async Task<GraphQLResponse<T>> SendAsync<T>(
        string query, object? variables, CancellationToken ct = default)
    {
        using var response = await http.PostAsJsonAsync("graphql", new { query, variables }, ct);
        response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();                  // transport only: GraphQL errors arrive with 200
        return (await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<GraphQLResponse<T>>(ct))!;
    }
}

record GraphQLResponse<T>(T? Data, GraphQLError[]? Errors);

record GraphQLError(string Message, JsonElement[]? Path, Dictionary<string, JsonElement>? Extensions);

record Order(string Id, string Status);

record OrderData(Order? Order);

sealed class FakeGraphQL : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"> POST /graphql {await request.Content!.ReadAsStringAsync(ct)}");
        const string Reply = """{"data":{"order":{"id":"o-1","status":"shipped"}}}""";
        return new HttpResponseMessage { Content = new StringContent(Reply, null, "application/json") };
    }
}
Result
> POST /graphql {"query":"query GetOrder($id: ID!) { order(id: $id) { id status } }","variables":{"id":"o-1"}}
order o-1: shipped

GraphQL: a mutation, and errors beside data

A `200 OK` can still carry `errors`, so read them first, keep whatever `data` is not null, and treat `extensions.code` as optional.

using System.Net.Http.Json;
using System.Text.Json;

using var http = new HttpClient(new FakeGraphQL()) { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://shop.example/") };
var gql = new GraphQLClient(http);

const string CancelOrder = "mutation CancelOrder($id: ID!) { cancelOrder(id: $id) { id status } }";
var result = await gql.SendAsync<CancelData>(CancelOrder, new { id = "o-1" });

// Errors first; then use whatever data is not null (it may be partly filled in).
foreach (var error in result.Errors ?? [])
{
    var code = error.Extensions?.GetValueOrDefault("code").ToString();     // extensions.code is optional
    Console.WriteLine($"error at {string.Join('.', error.Path ?? [])} [{code}]: {error.Message}");
}
Console.WriteLine($"cancelOrder is {(result.Data?.CancelOrder is null ? "null" : "set")}");

sealed class GraphQLClient(HttpClient http)
{
    public async Task<GraphQLResponse<T>> SendAsync<T>(
        string query, object? variables, CancellationToken ct = default)
    {
        using var response = await http.PostAsJsonAsync("graphql", new { query, variables }, ct);
        response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
        return (await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<GraphQLResponse<T>>(ct))!;
    }
}

record GraphQLResponse<T>(T? Data, GraphQLError[]? Errors);

record GraphQLError(string Message, JsonElement[]? Path, Dictionary<string, JsonElement>? Extensions);

record Order(string Id, string Status);

record CancelData(Order? CancelOrder);

sealed class FakeGraphQL : HttpMessageHandler
{
    protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        const string Reply = """
            {"data":{"cancelOrder":null},
             "errors":[{"message":"Order o-1 has already shipped","path":["cancelOrder"],
                        "extensions":{"code":"ORDER_SHIPPED"}}]}
            """;
        var content = new StringContent(Reply, null, "application/json");
        return Task.FromResult(new HttpResponseMessage { Content = content });
    }
}
Result
error at cancelOrder [ORDER_SHIPPED]: Order o-1 has already shipped
cancelOrder is null

GraphQL: a typed client with StrawberryShake, in outline

Once there are more than a handful of operations, generate the client from the schema: the result types follow each query's selection, and a schema change breaks the build instead of the screen.

// GetOrder.graphql
//   query GetOrder($id: ID!) { order(id: $id) { id status } }

// MauiProgram.cs or Program.cs: the generated AddShopClient registers IShopClient
builder.Services
    .AddShopClient()
    .ConfigureHttpClient(client => client.BaseAddress = new Uri("https://shop.example/graphql"));

// A view model or component: one generated property per operation
public sealed class OrderDetailsViewModel(IShopClient shop)
{
    public async Task<string?> LoadStatus(string id, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var result = await shop.GetOrder.ExecuteAsync(id, ct);
        if (result.Errors.Count > 0) return null;                     // or result.EnsureNoErrors() to throw
        return result.Data?.Order?.Status;
    }
}
Result

IShopClient.GetOrder.ExecuteAsync sends the stored operation with $id as a variable and returns a result whose Data is typed to the query's selection and whose Errors lists GraphQL errors.

gRPC: the contract, a unary call, a deadline and status codes

There is no default deadline: set one on every call, and branch on `RpcException.StatusCode` — `NotFound` and `InvalidArgument` are answers, `Unavailable` is worth a retry.

// Protos/orders.proto
//   syntax = "proto3";
//   option csharp_namespace = "Shop.Orders";
//   package shop.orders;
//   service Orders {
//     rpc GetOrder (GetOrderRequest) returns (Order);
//     rpc WatchOrder (WatchOrderRequest) returns (stream OrderEvent);
//   }
//   message GetOrderRequest { string id = 1; }
//   message Order { string id = 1; string status = 2; }
//   message WatchOrderRequest { string id = 1; }
//   message OrderEvent { string id = 1; string status = 2; }
using Grpc.Core;
using Grpc.Net.Client;
using Shop.Orders;

// One channel for the app's lifetime: it owns the HTTP/2 connection. Clients are cheap.
using var channel = GrpcChannel.ForAddress("https://orders.shop.example");
var client = new Orders.OrdersClient(channel);

try
{
    Order order = await client.GetOrderAsync(new GetOrderRequest { Id = "o-1" },
        deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(5));                     // a UTC instant, not a duration
    Console.WriteLine($"{order.Id}: {order.Status}");
}
catch (RpcException e)
{
    Console.WriteLine(e.StatusCode switch
    {
        StatusCode.NotFound => "no such order",                       // an answer, not a fault
        StatusCode.DeadlineExceeded => "timed out",
        StatusCode.Unavailable => "offline: worth a retry",
        _ => $"{e.StatusCode}: {e.Status.Detail}",
    });
}
Result

Prints o-1: shipped, or the branch for the call's gRPC status; a call still running after 5 seconds is aborted with DeadlineExceeded.

Setup
  1. dotnet add package Grpc.Net.Client, Google.Protobuf and Grpc.Tools
  2. Save the contract as Protos/orders.proto and add <Protobuf Include="Protos\orders.proto" GrpcServices="Client" /> to the .csproj: the stubs are generated at build time

gRPC: a server stream with await foreach, and gRPC-Web for Blazor WebAssembly

Dispose the streaming call (or cancel its token) when the screen goes away; in the browser, gRPC-Web carries unary and server-streaming calls only.

using Grpc.Core;
using Grpc.Net.Client;
using Grpc.Net.Client.Web;
using Shop.Orders;

public sealed class OrderTracker(Orders.OrdersClient client)
{
    // Called when the tracking screen opens; ct is cancelled when it closes.
    public async Task Track(string orderId, Action<OrderEvent> show, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        using var call = client.WatchOrder(new WatchOrderRequest { Id = orderId }, cancellationToken: ct);
        try
        {
            await foreach (var update in call.ResponseStream.ReadAllAsync(ct))
                show(update);                                   // marshal to the UI thread (MAUI, WPF, WinUI)
        }
        catch (RpcException e) when (e.StatusCode == StatusCode.Cancelled) { }   // the screen closed
    }

    // Blazor WebAssembly has no HTTP/2 sockets: the same client over gRPC-Web.
    // GrpcWebText (base64) is the mode browsers need for server streaming.
    public static Orders.OrdersClient ForBrowser(string address) =>
        new(GrpcChannel.ForAddress(address, new GrpcChannelOptions
        {
            HttpHandler = new GrpcWebHandler(GrpcWebMode.GrpcWebText, new HttpClientHandler()),
        }));
}
Result

Each OrderEvent the server streams is shown as it arrives; cancelling the token ends the call with StatusCode.Cancelled, which is swallowed as a normal close.

  1. The project and contract of the previous card
  2. Blazor WebAssembly: also dotnet add package Grpc.Net.Client.Web, and enable gRPC-Web on the server (app.UseGrpcWeb(), .EnableGrpcWeb(), with CORS)

Bonus: server push over a WebSocket

`ClientWebSocket` is in the box for raw push; in an app talking to ASP.NET Core, a SignalR `HubConnection` (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Client`, `.WithAutomaticReconnect()`) adds reconnection, hub methods and fallbacks on top.

using System.Net;
using System.Net.Sockets;
using System.Net.WebSockets;
using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Text;

var listener = new TcpListener(IPAddress.Loopback, 0);
listener.Start();
var server = PushUpdates(listener);
var port = ((IPEndPoint)listener.LocalEndpoint).Port;

using var socket = new ClientWebSocket();
await socket.ConnectAsync(new Uri($"ws://127.0.0.1:{port}/orders/o-1"), default);   // pass the screen's token
var buffer = new byte[4 * 1024];
using var message = new MemoryStream();
while (socket.State == WebSocketState.Open)                           // until the server's Close frame
{
    var frame = await socket.ReceiveAsync(buffer.AsMemory(), default);
    message.Write(buffer, 0, frame.Count);
    if (frame.MessageType == WebSocketMessageType.Close || !frame.EndOfMessage) continue;   // or a part
    Console.WriteLine("update: " + Encoding.UTF8.GetString(message.ToArray()));
    message.SetLength(0);
}
await socket.CloseAsync(WebSocketCloseStatus.NormalClosure, "bye", default);
await server;

const string Rfc6455Guid = "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11";

static async Task PushUpdates(TcpListener listener)
{
    using var tcp = await listener.AcceptTcpClientAsync();
    var stream = tcp.GetStream();
    var reader = new StreamReader(stream);
    var key = "";
    for (string? line; !string.IsNullOrEmpty(line = await reader.ReadLineAsync());)
        if (line.StartsWith("Sec-WebSocket-Key:")) key = line[18..].Trim();
    var accept = Convert.ToBase64String(SHA1.HashData(Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(key + Rfc6455Guid)));
    var handshake = "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\n";
    await stream.WriteAsync(Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(handshake + $"Sec-WebSocket-Accept: {accept}\r\n\r\n"));
    using var ws = WebSocket.CreateFromStream(stream, new WebSocketCreationOptions { IsServer = true });
    foreach (var json in new[] { """{"status":"packed"}""", """{"status":"shipped"}""" })
        await ws.SendAsync(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(json), WebSocketMessageType.Text, true, default);
    await ws.CloseAsync(WebSocketCloseStatus.NormalClosure, "delivered", default);
}
Result
update: {"status":"packed"}
update: {"status":"shipped"}

Choosing between REST, SOAP, gRPC and GraphQL

The server usually decides; when you do, choose by who calls it and how the data is shaped, not by fashion.

ChooseWhenThe cost
REST + JSONpublic or partner APIs, browsers and every client stack, HTTP caching matterschatty for nested screens; the contract lives in OpenAPI, if anywhere
SOAPan existing enterprise or government service with a WSDL; WS-Security already in placeverbose XML, heavyweight tooling; nobody starts a new API with it
gRPCservice-to-service, streaming both ways, strict contracts, low latencyHTTP/2 end to end; browsers need gRPC-Web (no client or bidirectional streams); not human-readable
GraphQLmany screens wanting different slices of one graph; mobile on slow linksno HTTP caching of POST; query cost limits and errors-in-200 to handle
SignalR / WebSocketsthe server pushes: live status, chat, dashboardsa long-lived connection to keep alive across sleep and network changes

Rules worth saying out loud

The mistakes that survive code review.

  • Building SOAP XML or a GraphQL query by string concatenation of user input: build XML with XElement (it escapes) and pass GraphQL values as variables.
  • Treating a GraphQL 200 OK as success: check errors first, then use whatever data is not null.
  • Reading only the HTTP status of a SOAP call: a fault comes back as 500 (SOAP 1.2: 400 for a Sender fault) with the reason in the body — parse it before EnsureSuccessStatusCode.
  • A gRPC call without a deadline: it can wait forever. And a GrpcChannel per call: channels are expensive, clients are not.
  • Calling a generated gRPC or WCF method's blocking overload (GetOrder, not GetOrderAsync) on a UI thread or in Blazor WebAssembly: the app freezes.
  • Wrap each protocol behind your own interface (IOrderService): screens and tests never see envelopes, stubs or RpcException.
  • Generate clients from the contract (WSDL, .proto, GraphQL schema) once the API has more than a few operations, and regenerate in CI when it changes.
  • Protobuf on gRPC is schema-first: add fields with new numbers, never reuse or renumber one, and old clients keep working.

Protocol against player and platform

Give each platform the manifest it plays natively (HLS for Apple, DASH or HLS elsewhere) and keep that choice in one place, knowing that `MediaElement`, AVPlayer and `MediaPlayerElement` don't let you swap their ABR algorithm while hls.js, dash.js and Media3 do.

PlayerHLSDASHDRM it can reachNotes
MAUI MediaElement on Android (Media3 ExoPlayer)yesyes (the toolkit ships the Media3 HLS and DASH modules)Widevine — through Media3 in a custom handler; MediaElement has no DRM APIAndroid 8.0 (API 26) or later; the platform picks renditions, MediaElement exposes no bitrate setting
MAUI MediaElement on iOS / Mac Catalyst (AVPlayer)nativenoFairPlay — AVContentKeySession in a custom handlerthe platform's own ABR; HLS is the only adaptive format

What a multivariant playlist holds, and how a rendition is picked

The player does this for you on every platform, so you write it to pick a rendition for a download, a preview or a bitrate cap, or to understand why the player chose 360p.

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

const string Multivariant = """
    #EXTM3U
    #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=6500000,RESOLUTION=1920x1080,CODECS="avc1.640028,mp4a.40.2"
    1080p/index.m3u8
    #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=3000000,RESOLUTION=1280x720,CODECS="avc1.4d401f,mp4a.40.2"
    720p/index.m3u8
    #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=500000,RESOLUTION=640x360
    360p/index.m3u8
    #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=64000,CODECS="mp4a.40.2"
    audio/index.m3u8
    """;
var all = Parse(Multivariant, new Uri("https://cdn.shop.example/videos/unboxing/master.m3u8"));
Console.WriteLine($"{all.Count} variants, {all.Count(r => r.Height == 0)} audio-only");

// The best video rendition under 80% of the measured throughput that the view can show; else the lowest.
var video = all.Where(r => r.Height > 0).ToList();
foreach (var (bps, viewHeight) in new[] { (400_000L, 1080), (4_500_000L, 1080), (20_000_000L, 720) })
{
    var pick = video.LastOrDefault(r => r.Bandwidth <= bps * 0.8 && r.Height <= viewHeight) ?? video[0];
    Console.WriteLine($"{bps / 1000} kbps, {viewHeight}-line view -> {pick.Height}p {pick.Uri.AbsolutePath}");
}

static List<Rendition> Parse(string text, Uri playlistUri)
{
    // NAME=value or NAME="quoted, with commas"; RESOLUTION and CODECS are optional (RFC 8216).
    var attribute = new Regex("([A-Z0-9-]+)=(\"[^\"]*\"|[^,]*)");
    var lines = text.Split('\n', StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries | StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
    var result = new List<Rendition>();
    for (var i = 0; i < lines.Length - 1; i++)
    {
        if (!lines[i].StartsWith("#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:")) continue;
        var a = attribute.Matches(lines[i])
            .ToDictionary(m => m.Groups[1].Value, m => m.Groups[2].Value.Trim('"'));
        var height = a.TryGetValue("RESOLUTION", out var size) ? int.Parse(size.Split('x')[1]) : 0;
        var uri = new Uri(playlistUri, lines[i + 1]);                    // relative to the playlist
        result.Add(new Rendition(long.Parse(a["BANDWIDTH"]), height, a.GetValueOrDefault("CODECS"), uri));
    }
    return [.. result.OrderBy(r => r.Bandwidth)];
}

record Rendition(long Bandwidth, int Height, string? Codecs, Uri Uri);    // Bandwidth: peak bits per second
Result
4 variants, 1 audio-only
400 kbps, 1080-line view -> 360p /videos/unboxing/360p/index.m3u8
4500 kbps, 1080-line view -> 720p /videos/unboxing/720p/index.m3u8
20000 kbps, 720-line view -> 720p /videos/unboxing/720p/index.m3u8
Setup
  1. .NET 8 SDK or later
  2. dotnet new console -o Demo, replace Demo/Program.cs with the example, then dotnet run --project Demo

Play a stream in .NET MAUI with MediaElement

Register the toolkit once, point `Source` at the `.m3u8` (or `.mpd` on Android and Windows), and drive your own UI from `StateChanged` and `MediaFailed`, dispatching to the UI thread.

<!-- VideoPage.xaml -->
<ContentPage xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/dotnet/2021/maui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2009/xaml"
             xmlns:toolkit="http://schemas.microsoft.com/dotnet/2022/maui/toolkit"
             x:Class="Shop.VideoPage">
    <Grid>
        <toolkit:MediaElement x:Name="player"
                              Source="https://cdn.shop.example/videos/unboxing/master.m3u8"
                              ShouldAutoPlay="True"
                              ShouldShowPlaybackControls="True"
                              ShouldKeepScreenOn="True"
                              MetadataTitle="Unboxing the Trail 2 backpack"
                              StateChanged="OnStateChanged"
                              MediaFailed="OnMediaFailed" />
        <ActivityIndicator x:Name="spinner" IsRunning="False" />
    </Grid>
</ContentPage>

// VideoPage.xaml.cs
using CommunityToolkit.Maui.Core;

namespace Shop;

public partial class VideoPage : ContentPage
{
    public VideoPage() => InitializeComponent();

    // Player events may arrive off the UI thread.
    void OnStateChanged(object? sender, MediaStateChangedEventArgs e) => Dispatcher.Dispatch(() =>
        spinner.IsRunning = e.NewState is MediaElementState.Opening or MediaElementState.Buffering);

    // Or hand it to the recovery card's PlaybackSupervisor.
    void OnMediaFailed(object? sender, MediaFailedEventArgs e) => Dispatcher.Dispatch(async () =>
        await DisplayAlert("Playback stopped", e.ErrorMessage, "OK"));

    protected override void OnDisappearing()
    {
        player.Stop();                                                   // leaving the page ends playback
        base.OnDisappearing();
    }
}
Result

The page plays the HLS stream with the platform's controls and adaptive bitrate, shows a spinner while opening or buffering, keeps the screen on while playing, and stops when the page disappears.

Setup

  2. In MauiProgram.CreateMauiApp: builder.UseMauiApp<App>().UseMauiCommunityToolkitMediaElement(); — on MediaElement 8.0+ (MAUI 10) it takes a required bool isAndroidForegroundServiceEnabled
  3. Android: MainActivity needs ResizeableActivity = true, LaunchMode = LaunchMode.SingleTask on its [Activity] attribute

Play HLS or DASH in WinUI with AdaptiveMediaSource

`MediaSource.CreateFromUri` is enough to play, so go through `AdaptiveMediaSource` only when you need a bitrate cap, the current bitrate or custom headers, and dispose both it and the player when leaving.

using Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls;
using Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Navigation;
using Windows.Media.Core;
using Windows.Media.Playback;
using Windows.Media.Streaming.Adaptive;

public sealed partial class VideoPage : Page
{
    private AdaptiveMediaSource? source;
    private MediaPlayer? player;

    public async Task PlayAsync(Uri manifest)                            // .m3u8 or .mpd
    {
        var created = await AdaptiveMediaSource.CreateFromUriAsync(manifest);
        if (created.Status != AdaptiveMediaSourceCreationStatus.Success)
        {
            StatusText.Text = $"Cannot open the stream ({created.Status})";
            return;
        }
        source = created.MediaSource;
        source.DesiredMaxBitrate = 3_000_000;                            // e.g. on a metered connection
        source.PlaybackBitrateChanged += (_, e) =>
            DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue(() => BitrateText.Text = $"{e.NewValue / 1000} kbps");

        player = new MediaPlayer { Source = MediaSource.CreateFromAdaptiveMediaSource(source) };
        player.PlaybackSession.PlaybackStateChanged += (session, _) => DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue(() =>
            Spinner.IsActive = session.PlaybackState is MediaPlaybackState.Opening
                or MediaPlaybackState.Buffering);
        player.MediaFailed += (_, e) =>
            DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue(() => StatusText.Text = $"{e.Error}: {e.ErrorMessage}");
        Video.SetMediaPlayer(player);
        player.Play();
    }

    protected override void OnNavigatedFrom(NavigationEventArgs e)
    {
        Video.SetMediaPlayer(null);                                      // detach before disposing
        player?.Dispose();                                               // the decoder and the network
        source?.Dispose();                                               // the adaptive source's downloads
        base.OnNavigatedFrom(e);
    }
}
Result

The stream plays in the page with transport controls, never above 3 Mbps; the current playback bitrate, a buffering ring and any failure are shown on the UI thread.

Setup

  2. Page XAML: <MediaPlayerElement x:Name="Video" AreTransportControlsEnabled="True" Stretch="Uniform"/>, a ProgressRing x:Name="Spinner" and two TextBlocks

Blazor: a video component that drives hls.js through JS interop

The component owns the player's lifetime: it attaches after the first render, shows a Retry button when the module reports a fatal error, and destroys the player in `DisposeAsync`.

@implements IAsyncDisposable
@inject IJSRuntime JS

<video @ref="video" controls playsinline style="width:100%"></video>
@if (status is not null) { <p role="alert">@status <button @onclick="StartAsync">Retry</button></p> }

@code {
    [Parameter, EditorRequired] public string ManifestUrl { get; set; } = "";
    private ElementReference video;
    private IJSObjectReference? module, playback;
    private DotNetObjectReference<ProductVideo>? self;
    private string? status;

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (firstRender) await StartAsync();                     // the <video> exists only after a render
    }

    private async Task StartAsync()
    {
        status = null;
        if (playback is not null) await playback.DisposeAsync();     // attach() destroys the old player
        module ??= await JS.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("import", "./js/hls-player.js");
        self ??= DotNetObjectReference.Create(this);
        playback = await module.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("attach", video, ManifestUrl, self);
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public void OnFatalError(string details)
    {
        status = $"Playback stopped ({details}).";
        StateHasChanged();
    }

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
    {
        try
        {
            if (playback is not null) await playback.InvokeVoidAsync("destroy");
            if (playback is not null) await playback.DisposeAsync();
            if (module is not null) await module.DisposeAsync();
        }
        catch (JSDisconnectedException) { }                      // Blazor Server: the circuit is gone
        self?.Dispose();
    }
}
Result

The video plays the stream; after a fatal error the message and a Retry button appear, Retry attaches a fresh player once the module has torn down the old one, and leaving the page destroys it.

  2. Save this as ProductVideo.razor and the next card as wwwroot/js/hls-player.js; with server rendering it needs an interactive render mode

The JavaScript module: hls.js first, native HLS second, bounded retries

Ask `Hls.isSupported()` before `canPlayType`, let hls.js retry within its default, bounded load policies, and after that report the fatal error to .NET instead of calling `startLoad()` in a loop.

// wwwroot/js/hls-player.js — hls.js 1.x, loaded by the page as window.Hls
const players = new WeakMap();                    // video → its destroy(), so a Retry never stacks listeners

export function attach(video, url, dotnet) {
  players.get(video)?.();                         // tear down whatever an earlier attach left behind
  const report = (details) => dotnet.invokeMethodAsync("OnFatalError", details);
  const destroy = start(video, url, report) ?? (() => {});
  players.set(video, destroy);
  return { destroy };
}

function start(video, url, report) {
  if (Hls.isSupported()) {                        // MSE or ManagedMediaSource: desktop Safari, iPhone 17.1+
    const hls = new Hls();                        // its default load policies retry a bounded number of times
    let mediaRecoveries = 0, destroyed = false;
    const destroy = () => {
      if (!destroyed) hls.destroy();
      destroyed = true;
    };
    hls.on(Hls.Events.ERROR, (_, data) => {
      if (!data.fatal) return;                               // hls.js is already retrying it
      if (data.type === Hls.ErrorTypes.MEDIA_ERROR && mediaRecoveries++ < 2) return hls.recoverMediaError();
      destroy();                                             // never startLoad() in a loop: show Retry
      report(data.details);
    });
    hls.loadSource(url);
    hls.attachMedia(video);
    return destroy;
  }

  if (video.canPlayType("application/vnd.apple.mpegurl")) {  // older iPhone Safari: native HLS only
    const listeners = new AbortController();
    const onError = () => report(`media error ${video.error?.code}`);
    video.addEventListener("error", onError, { signal: listeners.signal });
    video.src = url;
    return () => {
      listeners.abort();
      video.removeAttribute("src");
      video.load();
    };
  }

  report("this browser cannot play HLS");                    // and attach() returns a no-op destroy
}
Result

hls.js plays the stream wherever MSE or ManagedMediaSource exists and native HLS elsewhere on Apple devices; segment and playlist failures are retried within hls.js's default bounded load policies, a media error is recovered twice at most, any other fatal error destroys the player and calls OnFatalError once, and a Retry first tears down the previous player and its listeners (checked in Node with a fake video element: one error after two retries gives one report).

Setup
  1. hls.js 1.5 or later loaded by the host page (<script src="js/hls.min.js"></script>) or bundled
  2. Save as wwwroot/js/hls-player.js; the previous card imports it

Player state, errors and recovery — as a policy you can test

Keep the decision out of the page: back off and reload, resume a VOD where it broke and rejoin a live stream at its edge, and let only 30 s of healthy playback earn the retry budget back so a flapping stream gives up.

var now = DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch;
Func<DateTimeOffset> clock = () => now;                          // TimeProvider.System.GetUtcNow in the app

var vod = new PlaybackSupervisor(clock, Wait, Reload, isLive: false);
vod.OnPosition(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42));
await vod.OnFailed("network lost", CancellationToken.None);

var live = new PlaybackSupervisor(clock, Wait, Reload, isLive: true);
for (var i = 0; i < 4; i++)
{
    live.OnPlaying();
    now += TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);                              // plays for 5 s, then fails again
    await live.OnFailed("HTTP 503", CancellationToken.None);
}
Console.WriteLine($"live: {live.Status}");

static Task Wait(TimeSpan delay, CancellationToken ct) =>
    Console.Out.WriteLineAsync($"wait {delay.TotalSeconds} s");  // Task.Delay(delay, ct) in the app

static void Reload(TimeSpan? at) =>
    Console.WriteLine(at is { } t ? $"reload at {t.TotalSeconds} s" : "reload at the live edge");

sealed class PlaybackSupervisor(Func<DateTimeOffset> now, Func<TimeSpan, CancellationToken, Task> wait,
    Action<TimeSpan?> reload, bool isLive, int maxRetries = 3)
{
    private int failures;
    private TimeSpan resumeAt;
    private DateTimeOffset? playingSince;
    public string Status { get; private set; } = "playing";

    public void OnPlaying() => playingSince = now();            // MediaElement: StateChanged to Playing

    public void OnPosition(TimeSpan position)                    // MediaElement: PositionChanged
    {
        resumeAt = position;
        if (now() - playingSince >= TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)) failures = 0;   // only a healthy stretch
    }

    public async Task OnFailed(string reason, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        playingSince = null;
        if (++failures > maxRetries) { Status = $"gave up: {reason}"; return; }
        await wait(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(Math.Pow(2, failures - 1)), ct);   // 1 s, 2 s, 4 s
        ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();                                  // the page closed: no reload
        reload(isLive ? null : resumeAt);
    }
}
Result
wait 1 s
reload at 42 s
wait 1 s
reload at the live edge
wait 2 s
reload at the live edge
wait 4 s
reload at the live edge
live: gave up: HTTP 503

Live versus on-demand, read from the media playlist

`#EXT-X-ENDLIST` means on-demand; without it the playlist is live and must be reloaded about every target duration, and playback should start at least three target durations from the end.

using System.Globalization;

CultureInfo.CurrentCulture = CultureInfo.InvariantCulture;

const string Vod = """
    #EXTM3U
    #EXT-X-TARGETDURATION:6
    #EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE:VOD
    #EXTINF:6.0,
    seg0.ts
    #EXTINF:4.5,
    seg1.ts
    #EXT-X-ENDLIST
    """;
const string Live = """
    #EXTM3U
    #EXT-X-TARGETDURATION:6
    #EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE:1500
    #EXTINF:6.0,
    seg1500.ts
    #EXTINF:6.0,
    seg1501.ts
    #EXTINF:6.0,
    seg1502.ts
    #EXTINF:6.0,
    seg1503.ts
    """;
Console.WriteLine(Describe(Vod));
Console.WriteLine(Describe(Live));

static string Describe(string playlist)
{
    var lines = playlist.Split('\n', StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries | StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
    string? Tag(string name) => lines.FirstOrDefault(l => l.StartsWith(name + ":"))?[(name.Length + 1)..];

    var target = double.Parse(Tag("#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION")!);
    var length = lines.Where(l => l.StartsWith("#EXTINF:")).Sum(l => double.Parse(l[8..].Split(',')[0]));
    if (lines.Contains("#EXT-X-ENDLIST"))
        return $"on-demand: {length} s, seekable 0..{length}, start at 0, never reload";

    var kind = Tag("#EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE") == "EVENT" ? "live event (grows, DVR)" : "live (sliding window)";
    var start = Math.Max(0, length - 3 * target);                // at least 3 target durations from the edge
    var first = Tag("#EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE") ?? "0";
    return $"{kind}: window {length} s from segment {first}, start at {start} s, reload every {target} s";
}
Result
on-demand: 10.5 s, seekable 0..10.5, start at 0, never reload
live (sliding window): window 24 s from segment 1500, start at 6 s, reload every 6 s
Setup
  1. .NET 8 SDK or later
  2. dotnet new console -o Demo, replace Demo/Program.cs with the example, then dotnet run --project Demo
