Pseudo-localization and testing a culture

Run the app on pseudo-localized resources to find hard-coded text and clipped layouts before translation, and test logic under `tr-TR`, `ar-SA` and `de-DE` inside a scope that restores the culture.

using System.Globalization;
using System.Text;
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

// pseudo-localize the neutral resources: accents expose hard-coded text, padding and brackets clipping
Console.WriteLine(Pseudo.Localize("Order {0} shipped to {1}."));

var before = CultureInfo.CurrentCulture;
foreach (var name in new[] { "en-US", "tr-TR", "ar-SA", "de-DE" })      // cultures that break assumptions
{
    using var _ = new CultureScope(name);
    var direction = CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture.TextInfo.IsRightToLeft ? "rtl" : "ltr";
    var separator = CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.NumberFormat.NumberDecimalSeparator;
    // ar-SA can show Hijri dates; whether that is its default depends on the ICU version
    var hijri = CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.OptionalCalendars.Any(c => c is UmAlQuraCalendar);
    Console.WriteLine($"{name}: dir={direction} title={"title".ToUpper()} decimal={separator} hijri={hijri}");
}
Console.WriteLine($"restored: {CultureInfo.CurrentCulture == before}");

static class Pseudo
{
    const string Plain = "abcdeghiklnorstuyACDEINOSU";
    const string Accented = "àƀçđéğĥîķĺñöŕšţûýÅÇĐÉÎÑÖŠÛ";

    public static string Localize(string text)
    {
        var builder = new StringBuilder("[");
        // keep {0}-style placeholders intact; transform only the words around them
        foreach (var part in Regex.Split(text, @"(\{\d+[^}]*\})"))
            builder.Append(part.StartsWith('{') ? part : new string(part.Select(Accent).ToArray()));
        var padding = Math.Max(2, text.Length * 4 / 10);         // translations run ~40% longer
        return builder.Append(' ').Append('~', padding).Append(']').ToString();
    }

    private static char Accent(char c) => Plain.IndexOf(c) is var i and >= 0 ? Accented[i] : c;
}

// sets both cultures for a block, then restores them: one test cannot leak its culture into the next
sealed class CultureScope : IDisposable
{
    private readonly (CultureInfo Culture, CultureInfo UiCulture) saved =
        (CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture);

    public CultureScope(string name) =>
        CultureInfo.CurrentCulture = CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo(name);

    public void Dispose() => (CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture) = saved;
}
Result
[Öŕđéŕ {0} šĥîppéđ ţö {1}. ~~~~~~~~~~]

tr-TR: dir=ltr title=TİTLE decimal=, hijri=False
ar-SA: dir=rtl title=TITLE decimal=٫ hijri=True
de-DE: dir=ltr title=TITLE decimal=, hijri=False
restored: True

Rules and pitfalls

Most localization bugs are a culture that was never chosen on purpose.

  • Put whole sentences with numbered placeholders in resources, and add a <comment> saying what each placeholder is. Translators see no code.
  • Pass a culture to every ToString, Parse and string.Format: the user's for display, InvariantCulture for anything stored or sent.
  • Since .NET 5, Windows 10 1903 and later use ICU like Linux and macOS (older Windows falls back to NLS). To keep the old NLS behaviour, set <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Globalization.UseNls" Value="true" /> or DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_USENLS=1. Sorting and IndexOf results change between the two.
  • <InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization> drops ICU (a smaller app). Creating any culture other than InvariantCulture then throws CultureNotFoundException (with <PredefinedCulturesOnly>false</PredefinedCulturesOnly> it is created, but formats as invariant), casing is invariant, and IANA↔Windows time-zone id conversion is gone (IANA zones still load on Linux and macOS). Only for apps that never format for people.
  • Concatenating translated fragments ("Order " + id + " shipped"), or a count == 1 ? "item" : "items" ternary — Russian needs three forms, Arabic six.
  • Hard-coded formats like ToString("MM/dd/yyyy") for display, and DateTime.Now stored without an offset.
  • Fixed widths and heights on text: German and Finnish run 30–40% longer, and Arabic needs taller lines. Let layouts size to content.
  • Asserting culture-formatted output against hard-coded text: it depends on the ICU version, so macOS (Apple ICU), Linux (vanilla ICU) and Windows can format the same culture differently (¥ or ￥ for yen, p.m. or p. m., ' or ’ in de-CH). Assert against the formatter's own output, or pick formats that do not vary.
  • Test by switching the device or browser language. MAUI documents setting CurrentUICulture in code as inconsistent across platforms.

The base of the pyramid — the screen's logic without the screen

Every state the screen can show (loading, loaded, filtered, failed) is a view-model state, so test them all here with a fake whose answer the test releases, and no UI test has to.

// the fake server: each load waits until the test answers it — no timers, no network
TaskCompletionSource<IReadOnlyList<Order>> answer = new();
var screen = new OrdersViewModel(() => (answer = new()).Task);

var loading = screen.LoadAsync();
Check("shows a spinner while loading", screen.IsLoading && screen.Orders.Count == 0);
answer.SetResult([new("A-1042", "Ada Lovelace"), new("A-1043", "Grace Hopper")]);
await loading;
Check("lists the orders", !screen.IsLoading && screen.Orders.Count == 2);

screen.Query = "GRACE";
Check("filters by customer, ignoring case", screen.Visible.Single().Number == "A-1043");

var failing = screen.LoadAsync();
answer.SetException(new HttpRequestException("503 Service Unavailable"));
await failing;
Check("keeps the list, shows a retry message", screen.Orders.Count == 2 && screen.Error == "Refresh failed");

var retry = screen.LoadAsync();
answer.SetResult([new("A-1042", "Ada Lovelace")]);
await retry;
Check("a successful retry clears the message", screen.Error is null && screen.Orders.Count == 1);

static void Check(string what, bool ok) => Console.WriteLine($"{(ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL")} {what}");

record Order(string Number, string Customer);

class OrdersViewModel(Func<Task<IReadOnlyList<Order>>> loadOrders)
{
    public IReadOnlyList<Order> Orders { get; private set; } = [];
    public bool IsLoading { get; private set; }
    public string? Error { get; private set; }
    public string Query { get; set; } = "";

    // ordinal: the same answer on every machine (a culture-aware search passes the user's CompareInfo)
    public IEnumerable<Order> Visible =>
        Orders.Where(o => o.Customer.Contains(Query, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

    public async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        (IsLoading, Error) = (true, null);
        try { Orders = await loadOrders(); }
        catch (HttpRequestException) { Error = "Refresh failed"; }
        finally { IsLoading = false; }
    }
}
Result
PASS shows a spinner while loading
PASS lists the orders
PASS filters by customer, ignoring case
PASS keeps the list, shows a retry message
PASS a successful retry clears the message

A Blazor component test with bUnit — render, interact, assert

Register fakes in `Services` before `Render`, drive the component with event helpers, and wait for async renders with `WaitForAssertion`, never `Thread.Sleep`.

using Bunit;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Xunit;

public class OrderListTests : BunitContext
{
    private static readonly Order[] Orders = [new("A-1042", "Ada Lovelace"), new("A-1043", "Grace Hopper")];

    [Fact]
    public void Search_shows_only_matching_orders()
    {
        Services.AddSingleton<IOrdersApi>(new FakeOrdersApi(Orders));
        var cut = Render<OrderList>(parameters => parameters.Add(p => p.PageSize, 20));

        cut.WaitForAssertion(() => Assert.Equal(2, cut.FindAll("[aria-label='Orders'] li").Count));

        cut.Find("input[type=search]").Input("grace");

        cut.WaitForAssertion(() => cut.Find("[role=status]").MarkupMatches("<p role=\"status\">1 order</p>"));
        Assert.Equal("Grace Hopper", cut.Find("[aria-label='Orders'] li .customer").TextContent);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Delete_asks_the_api_and_removes_the_row()
    {
        var api = new FakeOrdersApi(Orders);
        Services.AddSingleton<IOrdersApi>(api);
        var cut = Render<OrderList>();

        await cut.Find("button[aria-label='Delete order A-1042']").ClickAsync();

        Assert.Equal(new[] { "A-1042" }, api.Deleted);
        cut.WaitForAssertion(() => Assert.Single(cut.FindAll("[aria-label='Orders'] li")));
    }
}
Result

dotnet test runs both tests in milliseconds without a browser. A missing aria-label or a changed status text fails with a semantic markup diff.

Setup
  1. An xUnit test project referencing the Blazor app, with the bunit package (2.x)
  2. OrderList.razor injects IOrdersApi, renders a search box, a role="status" result count and a list labelled Orders; the test's FakeOrdersApi returns the given orders and records Deleted numbers

An end-to-end journey with Playwright for .NET

Locate by role and accessible name, the way a user and a screen reader find things, and assert with `Expect(...)`, which retries until the page matches.

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using Microsoft.Playwright;
using Microsoft.Playwright.NUnit;

[Parallelizable(ParallelScope.Self)]
public class CheckoutTests : PageTest              // a fresh browser context (cookies, storage) per test
{
    // CI passes the app's URL; the dev certificate is not trusted on a CI runner
    public override BrowserNewContextOptions ContextOptions() => new()
    {
        BaseURL = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("BASE_URL") ?? "https://localhost:7043",
        IgnoreHTTPSErrors = true,
    };

    [Test]
    public async Task Customer_can_place_an_order()
    {
        await Page.GotoAsync("/products");
        await Page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Searchbox, new() { Name = "Search products" }).FillAsync("espresso");
        await Page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Listitem)
            .Filter(new() { HasText = "Espresso beans" })
            .GetByRole(AriaRole.Button, new() { Name = "Add to cart" })
            .ClickAsync();                          // waits until it is visible, enabled and stable

        var cart = Page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Link, new() { Name = "Cart (1)" });
        await Expect(cart).ToBeVisibleAsync();
        await cart.ClickAsync();

        await Page.GetByLabel("Email for receipts").FillAsync("ada@example.com");
        await Page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Button, new() { Name = "Place order" }).ClickAsync();

        await Expect(Page).ToHaveURLAsync(new Regex(@"/orders/A-\d+$"));
        var heading = Page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Heading, new() { Level = 1 });
        await Expect(heading).ToHaveTextAsync(new Regex(@"^Order A-\d+$"));
        await Expect(Page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Status)).ToContainTextAsync("Order placed");
    }
}
Result

dotnet test drives headless Chromium through search, cart and checkout. A failure reports which locator or assertion timed out. Run headed with dotnet test -- Playwright.LaunchOptions.Headless=false.

An Appium test for a .NET MAUI app, by AutomationId, with explicit waits

Give every view a test touches an `AutomationId`, find it with `MobileBy.Id` on Android or `MobileBy.AccessibilityId` on iOS and Windows, and wait with `WebDriverWait` until the condition holds.

using NUnit.Framework;
using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Appium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Appium.Android;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Support.UI;

public class OrdersScreenTests
{
    private const string AppPackage = "com.example.shop";
    private AndroidDriver driver = null!;
    private WebDriverWait wait = null!;

    [OneTimeSetUp]
    public void InstallAndLaunch()
    {
        var options = new AppiumOptions
        {
            PlatformName = "Android",
            AutomationName = "UiAutomator2",
            App = Path.GetFullPath($"../../../../Shop/bin/Release/net9.0-android/{AppPackage}-Signed.apk"),
        };
        driver = new AndroidDriver(new Uri("http://127.0.0.1:4723/"), options);
        wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15));
        // keep polling while the screen loads or the list re-renders under the element
        wait.IgnoreExceptionTypes(typeof(NoSuchElementException), typeof(StaleElementReferenceException));
    }

    [SetUp]
    public void RestartApp()                          // each test starts from the app's first screen
    {
        driver.TerminateApp(AppPackage);
        driver.ActivateApp(AppPackage);
    }

    [Test]
    public void Search_filters_the_order_list()
    {
        wait.Until(d => d.FindElement(MobileBy.Id("SearchEntry"))).SendKeys("grace");

        // wait for the state you expect, not for a number of seconds; a timeout fails the test
        wait.Until(d => d.FindElement(MobileBy.Id("ResultCount")).Text == "1 order");
    }

    [OneTimeTearDown]
    public void QuitApp() => driver.Quit();
}
Result

The fixture installs the app once and every test restarts it on its first screen. The test types into the search bar and passes when the count reads "1 order", or fails with WebDriverTimeoutException after 15 seconds. The same test runs on iOS with IOSDriver, XCUITest and MobileBy.AccessibilityId.

Setup
  1. An NUnit test project with the Appium.WebDriver package; an Appium 2+ server (npm i -g appium, appium driver install uiautomator2) and a booted emulator
  2. A Release APK of the MAUI app: Appium cannot install a Debug build that uses fast deployment
  3. In XAML: <SearchBar AutomationId="SearchEntry" … /> and <Label AutomationId="ResultCount" … />

Select by role or AutomationId, never by layout

A selector should survive a redesign, a translation and a wrapper `Grid`: role and accessible name first, a stable id next, a position in the tree never.

By layout, text and styling
// Appium: a path through today's view tree
driver.FindElement(By.XPath("//android.widget.LinearLayout[2]/android.widget.EditText[1]"));
driver.FindElement(By.XPath("//*[@text='Place order']"));       // breaks in Spanish

// Playwright: CSS that mirrors the grid and the theme
await Page.Locator("div.col-md-4 > div:nth-child(3) button.btn-primary").ClickAsync();

// bUnit: markup structure
cut.Find("div > div:nth-child(2) > span");

// FlaUI: the third button in the window
window.FindAllDescendants(cf => cf.ByControlType(ControlType.Button))[2].AsButton().Invoke();
By role, label or AutomationId
<!-- MAUI / WPF / WinUI: a stable, untranslated id on the views a test touches -->
<SearchBar AutomationId="SearchEntry" Placeholder="{x:Static strings:AppResources.SearchPlaceholder}" />

// Appium: AutomationId (Android resource-id; iOS and Windows accessibility id)
driver.FindElement(MobileBy.Id("SearchEntry"));

// Playwright: role + accessible name, then label, then data-testid as the last resort
await Page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Button, new() { Name = "Place order" }).ClickAsync();
await Page.GetByLabel("Email for receipts").FillAsync("ada@example.com");
await Expect(Page.GetByTestId("order-total")).ToHaveTextAsync("$25.50");

// bUnit: the accessible structure the component promises
cut.Find("[aria-label='Orders'] li");

// FlaUI (WPF/WinUI): AutomationProperties.AutomationId, or x:Name by default, retried until it appears
var save = Retry.WhileNull(() => window.FindFirstDescendant(cf => cf.ByAutomationId("SaveButton")),
    TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), throwOnTimeout: true).Result;
save!.AsButton().Invoke();
Result

Both sides find the same elements today. After a redesign or a Spanish build the left side breaks and the right side still passes. Role-based selectors also fail when a control loses its accessible name — a real bug.

Isolate network and state: WebApplicationFactory, route interception, launch arguments

A UI test owns its data — replace the service in memory, intercept the browser's requests, or start the app in a test mode that registers fakes — and never depends on a shared staging database.

// 1. ASP.NET Core / Blazor Server: the real pipeline in memory, one service replaced
public class OrdersPageTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
    : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task Orders_page_renders_orders_from_the_fake_api()
    {
        var fake = new FakeOrdersApi([new("A-1042", "Ada Lovelace")]);
        var client = factory
            .WithWebHostBuilder(builder => builder.ConfigureTestServices(services =>
                services.AddSingleton<IOrdersApi>(fake)))
            .CreateClient();

        var html = await client.GetStringAsync("/orders");

        Assert.Contains("A-1042", html);
    }
}

// 2. Playwright: answer the browser's API calls from the test, including failures on demand
await Page.RouteAsync("**/api/orders*", route => route.FulfillAsync(new()
{
    Status = 200,
    Json = new[] { new { number = "A-1042", customer = "Ada Lovelace" } },
}));
await Page.RouteAsync("**/api/payments", route => route.FulfillAsync(new() { Status = 503 }));

// 3. Appium: launch the MAUI app with a flag it reads at startup to register fakes —
//    Android: an intent extra, read in MainActivity; iOS and Windows: Environment.GetCommandLineArgs()
options.AddAdditionalAppiumOption("appium:optionalIntentArguments", "--ez uitest true");   // UiAutomator2
options.AddAdditionalAppiumOption("appium:processArguments",
    new Dictionary<string, object> { ["args"] = new[] { "--uitest" } });                   // XCUITest
options.AddAdditionalAppiumOption("appium:appArguments", "--uitest");                       // Windows driver
Result

The server test renders A-1042 from the fake without a network. The browser test sees one order and a failing payment every run. The device test starts on known data. Nothing depends on what another test or another person left behind.

Page objects — locators and actions in one place, assertions in the test

Put locators and actions in a page object that exposes intent (`PlaceOrderAsync`) and keep the assertions in the test, so a changed screen means fixing one class instead of twenty tests.

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using Microsoft.Playwright;
using Microsoft.Playwright.NUnit;

public sealed class CheckoutPage(IPage page)
{
    public ILocator Email => page.GetByLabel("Email for receipts");
    public ILocator Confirmation => page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Status);
    private ILocator PlaceOrderButton => page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Button, new() { Name = "Place order" });

    public Task OpenAsync() => page.GotoAsync("/checkout");

    public async Task PlaceOrderAsync(string email)
    {
        await Email.FillAsync(email);
        await PlaceOrderButton.ClickAsync();
    }
}

public class CheckoutPageTests : PageTest
{
    public override BrowserNewContextOptions ContextOptions() => new()
    {
        BaseURL = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("BASE_URL") ?? "https://localhost:7043",
        IgnoreHTTPSErrors = true,
    };

    [Test]
    public async Task Confirms_a_placed_order()
    {
        var checkout = new CheckoutPage(Page);
        await checkout.OpenAsync();
        await checkout.PlaceOrderAsync("ada@example.com");
        await Expect(checkout.Confirmation).ToContainTextAsync("Order placed");
    }

    [Test]
    public async Task Rejects_an_invalid_email()
    {
        var checkout = new CheckoutPage(Page);
        await checkout.OpenAsync();
        await checkout.PlaceOrderAsync("ada@");
        await Expect(checkout.Email).ToHaveAttributeAsync("aria-invalid", "true");     // state, not wording
        await Expect(checkout.Email).ToHaveAccessibleDescriptionAsync(new Regex(".+"));  // aria-describedby
    }
}
Result

Both tests read as user intent and select nothing by wording, so renaming the button, moving the email field or translating the error message changes only CheckoutPage, or nothing at all.

The flake checklist

A flaky test is a bug in the test, the app or the environment — find which, never retry it into silence.

  • Wait for a state, never for time: Playwright's auto-waiting and Expect, bUnit's WaitForAssertion, Appium's WebDriverWait.Until. No Thread.Sleep, Task.Delay or implicit-wait guesses.
  • Own the data: fakes in ConfigureTestServices, Page.RouteAsync for the browser, a launch flag for the device. Each test creates what it reads.
  • Isolate every test: a new browser context per test (the PageTest default), a fresh app launch or reset for Appium, no ordering between tests.
  • Pin the environment: culture, time zone, clock (TimeProvider), viewport, animations off on the emulator, the same browser build in CI and locally.
  • XPath by position, CSS by layout or theme classes, and matching on translated text. All three break without any bug.
  • Asserting right after an action with a non-retrying Assert, such as Assert.That(await locator.IsVisibleAsync()). Use the web-first Expect(locator).ToBeVisibleAsync().
  • Quarantine a flaky test with an issue link and a deadline. Keep traces (Context.Tracing), screenshots and Appium logs from every failed run.
  • Debug builds of MAUI Android use fast deployment, which Appium cannot install. Test a Release APK, or set noReset and launch an already-deployed package.

Coverage against the Swift Catalog

Every Swift topic, and what this catalog has for it — an equivalent, a partial counterpart, or the reason there is none.

How to read the matrix

Nothing here is a translation made to fill a gap.

  • equivalent — a sheet here covers the same concept and shares its concept id, so the language selector lands on it from the Swift sheet.
  • partial — a sheet here covers part of it under its own concept id, so the selector does not land on it: the Here column names it and the reason says what is missing.
  • no counterpart — nothing here; the reason says whether the topic does not exist in this language or is simply not written yet.
